==Ownership Tree==

This ownership tree is part of the [https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-energy-ownership-tracker/ Global Energy Ownership Tracker], a project of Global Energy Monitor.

{{#widget:ObservableOwnershipTree|}}

==Background==

Mitsui & Co., Ltd. entered into a project finance agreement with Gulf Energy Development Public Company Limited for a gas-fired thermal power generation project in November 2018.<ref name="Mitsui">[https://www.mitsui.com/jp/en/release/2018/1227529_11215.html Mitsui to Move Forward with Gas-fired Thermal Power Plant Project in Chonburi Province, Thailand], Mitsui website, Nov 9. 2018</ref> They announced that Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems, Ltd. will be the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor.<ref>[https://www.mhps.com/news/20180209.html MHPS Receives Order to Construct 5,300MW Power Plant Project in Thailand Incorporating Eight M701JAC Gas Turbines], MHPS website, Feb 9, 2018</ref>

''Kaohoon.com'' reported that construction started on December 3, 2018.<ref>[https://www.kaohoon.com/content/268336 GULF เดินหน้าโรงไฟฟ้า”GSRC” 2,500MW รับลูกกกพ.ไฟเขียวพื้นที่สร้างสายส่ง พร้อมCODมี.ค.64], ''Kaohoon.com'', Dec 14, 2018</ref>

In December 2019, Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems shipped the first eight turbines to Bangkok, four for this plant and four for the [[Rayong Gulf PD power station]].<ref>[https://www.power-eng.com/2019/12/06/mhps-ships-jac-turbines-for-ccgt-plant-in-thailand/#gref MHPS ships JAC turbines for CCGT plant in Thailand], ''Power Engineering'', Dec. 6, 2019</ref>

The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand plans to commission two units in 2021 and the remaining two in 2022.<ref name="egatAnnual19">[https://www.egat.co.th/en/images/annual-report/2019/annual-report-2019-en.pdf Annual Report 2019], Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand, accessed Feb. 9, 2021</ref>

Units 1 and 2 started commercial operations in 2021,<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/51051/51051-001-esmr-en_32.pdf|title=Thailand: Chonburi Natural Gas Power Project - Environmental and Social Monitoring Report|last=|first=|publisher=Asian Development Bank.|year=May 2021|isbn=|location=|pages=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.gulf.co.th/en/pdf/onereport-gulf-2021-en.pdf|title=Annual Report|last=|first=|publisher=Gulf Energy Development Public Company Limited|year=2021|isbn=|location=|pages=}}</ref> with units 3 and 4 then starting commercial operations in 2022.<ref name="autoref_4" /><ref name="autoref_5" />

The total project cost for the four units is estimated to be US$1.55 billion.<ref name="Mitsui" /><ref name="NS">[https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/gulf-sriracha-power-plant-chonburi/?cf-view Gulf Sriracha Power Plant, Chonburi], NS Energy, Nov. 21, 2018</ref> In November 2018, 12 international financial institutions provided the project promoters with loans totalling US$1.15 billion, including a US$227 million loan facility from the Japan Bank for International Cooperation<ref name="NS" /> and a US$228 million loan from the multilateral Asian Development Bank.<ref>[https://www.adb.org/projects/51051-001/main Thailand : Chonburi Natural Gas Power Project], Asian Development Bank Project Data Sheet, last updated Nov. 5, 2024</ref> Gulf Energy and Mitsui together invested US$395 million as equity.<ref>[https://www.ijglobal.com/data/transaction/48821/sriracha-gsrc-ccgt-power-plant-265gw-ipp Sriracha GSRC CCGT Power Plant (2.65GW) IPP], IJGlobal Transaction Data, last updated Oct. 31, 2024</ref>

{{#widget:ObservableOwnershipTree|}}

==Background==

The Cirebon power station is a coal-fired power plant developed by Cirebon Electric Power (CEP) in the Kanci area to the southeast of Cirebon, Indonesia.<ref name = "na">[http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2012/10/19/cirebon-power-plant-stream-java-and-bali.html Cirebon power plant on stream for Java and Bali], Amahl S. Azwar, ''The Jakarta Post'', 19 October 2012.</ref> CEP is a joint venture between four companies: Japan-owned [[Marubeni Corporation]] (32.5%), Korea Midland Power Co (27.5%), South Korean company [[Samtan]] Co Ltd (20%) and Indonesian company PT Indika Energy (a subsidiary of the [[Indika Group]]) (20%). 

Like other IPPs in Indonesia, the plant will sell the electricity produced to the PLN at an agreed feed-in tariff price. The initial agreed rate was reported to be US 4.43 cents per kWh (USD 0.0443/kWh) although, because of high coal prices, it was reported that the PLN would adjust the purchase price upwards to US 5.2 cents per kWh (USD 0.052/kWh).

The first unit of the plant was launched in mid October 2012. The reported cost of the plant was nearly $850 million. Construction began in 2008 and was completed in mid-2012. Sales from the plant to the Indonesian state-owned electricity company [[PLN]] began in July 2012.<ref name = "na">[http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2012/10/19/cirebon-power-plant-stream-java-and-bali.html Cirebon power plant on stream for Java and Bali], Amahl S. Azwar, ''The Jakarta Post'', 19 October 2012.</ref>

In November 2022, Indonesia committed to capping power sector emissions and doubling renewable energy generation by 2030, utilizing US$20 billion in grants and concessional loans. Indonesia’s Energy Transition Mechanism signed a non-binding agreement to close Unit 1 of the Cirebon power station. The target was retirement by 2037, which was 15 years before the initial targeted lifespan.<ref name=":0">[https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-11-14/indonesia-gets-state-wealth-fund-to-retire-660mw-coal-plant?leadSource=uverify%20wall "Indonesia Gets State Wealth Fund to Retire 660MW Coal Plant,"] Bloomberg, November 13, 2022</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ijglobal.com/articles/168484/indonesia-coal-fired-ipp-taps-adb-for-early-retire|title=Indonesia coal-fired IPP taps ADB for early retire|last=|first=|date=November 2022|website=www.ijglobal.com|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

A February 2023 article highlighted environmental and social concerns that had not yet been addressed by retirement plans. Friends of the Earth Indonesia (WALHI) stated that over 3,000 farmers and fishermen have had their livelihoods disrupted by the power station. The article argues that the November 2022 announcement was insufficient without reparations for the local community, especially because the expansion unit was expected to begin operation soon under the same ownership.<ref>[https://theprakarsa.org/indonesias-cirebon-1-coal-power-project-highlights-gaps-in-adbs-coal-to-clean-etm-scheme/ "Indonesia’s Cirebon 1 coal power project highlights gaps in ADB’s ‘coal-to-clean’ ETM scheme,"] Prakarsa, February 10, 2023</ref>

In July 2023, the government announced that an early retirement of Cirebon-1 would be announced in 2023 as part of a PLN trial project on coal plant early retirements.<ref>[https://industri.kontan.co.id/news/kementerian-bumn-pastikan-pln-eksekusi-pensiun-dini-pltu-cirebon-1-tahun-ini "Kementerian BUMN Pastikan PLN Eksekusi Pensiun Dini PLTU Cirebon 1 Tahun Ini,"] Kontan.co.id, July 13, 2023</ref> As of August 2023, negotiations on refinancing the plant for early retirement were ongoing among the Asian Development Bank (ADB), private sector banks, and the power station's investors.<ref>[https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2023-08-15/closing-coal-plant-early-in-indonesia-tests-climate-finance-in-asia "Closing Coal Plants Proves a Hard Sell for Big Global Banks,"] Bloomberg, August 14, 2023</ref> 

In December 2023, the Government of Indonesia and ADB officially announced the deal to retire Unit 1 of Cirebon power station at the end of 2035. The deal was revealed at the COP28 conference in Dubai. Cirebon-1's power purchase agreement would be ended 7 years early through a first of its kind Energy Transition Mechanism (ETM) framework. ADB hoped to replicate the deal for other projects.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/indonesia-adb-owners-agree-shutter-first-coal-fired-power-station-early-2023-12-03/ "Indonesia, ADB, owners agree to shutter first coal-fired power station early,"] Reuters, December 3, 2023</ref>

In January 2024, a Center of Economic and Law Studies analysis found that the retirement of Cirebon power station and [[Pelabuhan Ratu power station]] would eliminate up to 14,022 jobs, but their replacement by renewable energy alternatives would create up to 639,269 jobs.<ref>[https://indonesiabusinesspost.com/insider/prabowo-gibran-pledge-to-continue-energy-transition/ "Prabowo-Gibran pledge to continue energy transition,"] Indonesia Business Post, January 31, 2024</ref>

In November 2024, Indonesia's Finance Minister reportedly raised concerns about "state losses" regarding the retirement of Cirebon power station Unit 1. However, experts and community activists stated that the replacement of the unit would be profitable, in addition to the environmental and public health benefits.<ref>[https://indonesiabusinesspost.com/insider/experts-question-governments-coal-fired-power-plants-retirement-dilemma/ "Experts question government’s coal-fired power plants retirement dilemma,"] Indonesia Business Post, November 6, 2024</ref>

In December 2024, the Cirebon-1 early retirement program roadmap, which was initially expected to be completed in September 2024, was described as "stalled".<ref>[https://www.tempo.co/ekonomi/pensiun-dini-pltu-batu-bara-cirebon-1181582 "Cerita di Balik Macetnya Pensiun Dini PLTU Cirebon,"] Tempo, December 15, 2024</ref>

In February 2025, Indonesia’s Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources confirmed that Cirebon-1 would close in 2035.<ref name=CREA_Mar25>[https://energyandcleanair.org/publication/cirebon-1-indonesias-first-coal-to-renewables-milestone/ “Cirebon-1, Indonesia’s first coal-to-renewables milestone,”] Centre for Research Energy and Clear Air, March 4, 2025</ref>

According to reporting from November 2025, the Asian Development Bank’s Energy Transition Mechanism had earmarked about half of the US$2.56 billion of funding to Indonesia to support the closure of Cirebon-1.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/indonesia-coal-power-phase-out-plan-risk-due-stalled-international-funding-2025-11-17/ “Exclusive: Indonesia coal power phase-out plan at risk due to stalled international funding,”] Reuters, November 17, 2025</ref>

In December 2025, PLN announced that they were pulling out of the early retirement plan for Cirebon-1.<ref>[https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-12-05/coal-plant-seen-as-flagship-for-fuel-s-exit-scraps-early-closure "Indonesia Coal Plant Seen as Flagship For Fuel’s Exit Scraps Early Closure,"] Bloomberg, December 5, 2025</ref> A PLN Director stated that Indonesia would be focusing on a "phase down" approach rather than a "phase out" approach, retiring coal plants at the end of their Power Purchase Agreements (PPA). The last coal PPA with an independent power producer would end in 2056.<ref>[https://www.petromindo.com/news/article/pln-cancels-early-retirement-of-cirebon-coal-fired-power-plant "PLN cancels early retirement of Cirebon coal-fired power Plant,"] Petromindo, December 3, 2025</ref>

==Description of Expansion==

There are plans to extend the Cirebon plant with the installation of an additional 2 x 1,000-MW units, units 2 and 3, costing around US$2 billion.<ref name = "na">[http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2012/10/19/cirebon-power-plant-stream-java-and-bali.html Cirebon power plant on stream for Java and Bali], Amahl S. Azwar, ''The Jakarta Post'', 19 October 2012.</ref> In November 2013, CEP announced that it was set to start the construction of the plant's second unit, which will provide an additional power supply of 1,000 megawatts (MW) in 2014, with completion targeted for 2018.<ref>[http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2013/11/13/new-1000-mw-power-plant-be-built-cirebon.html "New 1,000 MW-power plant to be built in Cirebon"] Anggi M. Lubis, The Jakarta Post, Jakarta, November 13, 2013.</ref> This plant is also shown in PLN's 2013-2022 long-range plan with a 2018 completion.
<ref name=LT>[http://energy-indonesia.com/03dge/0140317pln.pdf “PLN Long Term Electricity Plan (2013-2023),”] presentation by Moch. Sofyan, Head of New & Renewable Division of PT PLN (Persero), 06 March 2014</ref> Funding for the project would come from loans from the [[Japan Bank for International Cooperation]] and the [[Export-Import Bank of Korea]].<ref>[http://www.beritasatu.com/ekonomi/153906-pembangunan-pltu-cirebon-unit-2-ditargetkan-pertengahan-2014.html Pembangunan PLTU Cirebon Unit 2 Ditargetkan Pertengahan 2014], Berita Satu, 5 Dec. 2013.</ref> The PT PLN 2018-2027 long range plan lists Unit 2 as 924 MW with a completion date of 2020.<ref name=RUPTL2018>[http://listrik.org/pln/ruptl/ Rencana Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik (RUPTL) 2018-2027,] PT PLN Persero, V-4</ref>

In December 2014, government officials allocated land for the project. At that time, construction was planned to begin in 2015, with completion in 2020.<ref name=DJKN>[https://www.djkn.kemenkeu.go.id/2013/berita/kerjasama-pemanfaatan-proyek-pltu-cirebon-jawa-barat Utilisasi Kerja Sama Pemanfaatan BMN KPKNL Jakarta II: Kerjasama Pemanfaatan untuk Proyek PLTU Cirebon Jawa Barat], Direktorat Jenderal Kekayaan Negara website, 11 Dec. 2014.</ref> 

In April 2015, project co-sponsor Indika withdrew from the power station, citing financial difficulties.<ref>Anggi M. Lubis, [http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2015/04/30/indika-cancels-cirebon-power-plant-project.html "Indika cancels Cirebon power plant project,"] The Jakarta Post, April 30 2015</ref>

In May 2015, PT Cirebon Energi Prasarana (CEPR), the developer of Cirebon II power plant, said construction of Cirebon II would begin near the end of 2015,<ref>[http://en.tempo.co/read/news/2015/05/12/056665712/Cirebon-II-Steam-Power-Plant-Construction-to-Start-by-Year-end "Cirebon II Steam Power Plant Construction to Start by Year-end,"] Tempo, May 12, 2015</ref> later pushed to January 2016.<ref>[http://jabar.tribunnews.com/2015/07/02/pembangunan-pltu-cirebon-ii-harus-negosiasi-ulang-dengan-pendana "Pembangunan PLTU Cirebon II Harus Negosiasi Ulang dengan Pendana,"] Tribun Jabar, 2 July 2015</ref>

In March 2016, Director of Corporate Planning of PLN Nicke Widyawati said PLN expects to begin construction of the plant within the month.<ref>[http://www.rambuenergy.com/2016/03/pln-expects-to-soon-start-construction-of-pltu-jawa-7-pltu-cilacap-pltu-cirebon/ "PLN expects to soon start construction of PLTU Jawa 7, PLTU Cilacap, PLTU Cirebon,"] RambuEnergy, March 1, 2016</ref>

In May 2016, it was reported that initial construction prep on unit 2 was underway, and a 1,000 MW ultra-supercritical unit 3 was planned.<ref>[http://newsbase.com/topstories/marubeni-partners-build-new-power-plant-indonesia "Marubeni, Partners To Build New Power Plant In Indonesia,"] Asia Power, 24 May 2016</ref>

In December 2016, a legal challenge to the project was filed by The People for Environmental Protection (RAPEL), with legal representation by the Advocacy Team for Climate Justice. At the heart of the legal challenge was RAPEL’s claim that local planning law only permitted power plant development in the district of Astanajapura, and that the Cirebon 2 expansion also extended into Mundu district, which was zoned for local livelihoods. On April 19, 2017, the regional court in Bandung ruled the environmental permit for the plant was issued illegally.<ref name=awesomebob>Bob Burton, [http://endcoal.org/2017/04/embarrassment-for-japanese-government-bank-as-court-rules-coal-plants-permit-illegal/ "Embarrassment for Japanese Government bank as court rules coal plant’s permit illegal,"] EndCoal, Apr 19, 2017</ref>

A coalition of Japanese groups are calling on JBIC to immediately review and repeal its decision to provide financing for Cirebon 2, saying the project is illegal according to local law and in violation of the “JBIC Guidelines for Confirmation of Environmental and Social Considerations,” which require “the compliance with environmental laws of the host nation and local governments concerned” and “the submission of environmental permit certificates issued by the host governments.”<ref>[http://www.foejapan.org/en/aid/170419.html "Cirebon Coal-fired Power Plant Projects, West Java, Indonesia,"] FOE Japan, Apr 17, 2017</ref>

In October 2017, the Head of Communications at Cirebon Electric Power, Yuda Panjaitan, said problems around Spatial Planning (RTRW) and licensing in the State Administrative Court (PTUN) had been resolved, and Unit 2 had now obtained an environmental permit from the West Java Provincial Government under the legal umbrella of Government Regulation No. 13 of 2017. The plant was reported as under construction,<ref>[http://bisnis.liputan6.com/read/3115307/pltu-cirebon-unit-2-ditargetkan-beroperasi-pada-2021 PLTU Cirebon Unit 2 Ditargetkan Beroperasi pada 2021], Liputan 6, Oct. 2, 2017</ref> but Google Earth (dated November 1, 2017) shows only leveling of the site has begun, but no visible construction of the power station.

In September 2018, it was reported that construction of Cirebon 2 was 24% complete.<ref>[https://finance.detik.com/energi/d-4231976/proyek-pltu-2-cirebon-sudah-capai-24 Cirebon PLTU 2 Project Reaches 24%], Detik Finance, Sep. 27, 2018</ref>

In October 2018, the KOMIPO CEO told a Korean National Assembly hearing that “construction on Cirebon 3 has been suspended” and “we plan to do renewables.” The statements came while the CEO was being questioned by Assemblywoman Bae-sook Cho of the Trade, Industry and Energy Committee, who criticized the lack of emission controls attached to Cirebon 1 compared to Korean coal plants, and said coal will be an unreasonable choice in six to seven years when Cirebon 2 is completed, given the LCOE trends. According to an anonymous source within KOMIPO: “As of now we are not in the condition to proceed with the construction of Unit 3. This is because the Indonesian Government did not reflect the plant (Cirebon 3) in its power supply and demand plan.”<ref>[http://www.electimes.com/article.php?aid=1540192247167026002 "중부발전, 찌레본 석탄화력 신규 발전사업 중단하나,"] ElecTimes, 2018년 10월 22일</ref>

In February 2019, the government's long-range plan for 2019-2028 listed the project with a completion date of 2022.<ref name=RUPTL2019>[http://listrik.org/pln/ruptl/ Rencana Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik (RUPTL) 2019-2028,] PT PLN Persero, V-43</ref> Construction was 28% complete as of February 2019.<ref>[https://katadata.co.id/berita/2019/02/07/pltu-cirebon-unit-ii-dipastikan-beroperasi-tahun-2022 PLTU Cirebon Unit II Dipastikan Beroperasi Tahun 2022], Katadata, Feb. 7, 2019</ref> Construction was 61% complete as of September 2019.<ref>[https://katadata.co.id/berita/2019/09/16/terhubung-dengan-kasus-suap-pembangunan-pltu-cirebon-ii-jalan-terus Terhubung Dengan Kasus Suap, Pembangunan PLTU Cirebon II Jalan Terus], Katadata, Sep. 16, 2019</ref>

In March 2020, the project's sponsor declared force majeure and stated that development would be delayed as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref name=ko>[https://industri.kontan.co.id/news/jadwal-operasional-pembangkit-terganggu-wabah-corona-ini-tanggapan-pln?page=all Jadwal operasional pembangkit terganggu wabah corona, ini tanggapan PLN], Kontan, Mar. 8, 2020</ref> As of June 30, 2020 construction was reported to be 81.15% complete by the Directorate General of Electricity.<ref>[https://industri.kontan.co.id/news/simak-berikut-pembangkit-dan-proyek-kelistrikan-35000-mw-yang-terdampak-covid-19 Simak! Berikut pembangkit dan proyek kelistrikan 35.000 MW yang terdampak Covid-19], Kontan, Aug. 2, 2020</ref> 

In February 2021, PLN's Regional Business Director for Java, Madura and Bali said that Unit 2 would be commissioned in 2022.<ref>[https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/news/20210223155055-4-225552/termasuk-pltu-batang-2022-akan-nambah-5000-mw-pembangkit Termasuk PLTU Batang, 2022 Akan Nambah 5.000 MW Pembangkit], CNBC Indonesia, Feb. 23, 2021</ref>

In April 2023, Unit 2 was reportedly 99.8% complete and was slated for commercial operation in mid-May 2023.<ref>[https://market.bisnis.com/read/20230409/192/1644983/grup-indika-indy-siap-operasikan-pltu-cirebon-ii-tambah-cuan Grup Indika (INDY) Siap Operasikan PLTU Cirebon II, Tambah Cuan], Bisnis, April 9, 2023</ref>

As of mid-June 2023, the unit was not yet operating.<ref>[https://bandung.bisnis.com/read/20230608/550/1663461/pltu-unit-2-cirebon-masih-uji-coba-terbatas PLTU unit 2 Cirebon Masih Uji Coba Terbatas], Bandung Bisnis, June 8, 2023</ref>

In September 2023, an article stated that Cirebon II had been operating for "a matter of months". The unit appeared to have gone online in July or August 2023.<ref>[https://ekonomi.republika.co.id/berita/s1mk32370/kementerian-esdm-apresiasi-pltu-cirebon-2-terapkan-baku-mutu-emisi-internasional Kementerian ESDM Apresiasi PLTU Cirebon 2 Terapkan Baku Mutu Emisi Internasional], Republika, September 27, 2023</ref>

In December 2025, Cirebon-2 was reportedly designated as a "National Vital Object".<ref>[https://bandung.bisnis.com/read/20251222/550/1938789/pltu-cirebon-2-resmi-jadi-objek-vital-nasional#goog_rewarded PLTU Cirebon 2 Resmi Jadi Objek Vital Nasional], Bandung Bisnis, December 22, 2025</ref>

==Cancellation of Unit 3==

As of June 2020, there had been no progress on Unit 3 since a May 2016 by Marubeni and other potential sponsors, and the unit appears to be cancelled.

==Financing==

'''Unit 1:''' The financing agreement for Unit 1 was closed in March 2010. US$595 million in debt was provided by the Japan Bank of International Cooperation, the Export-Import Bank of Korea, ING Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Mizuho Financial Group, and MUFG Bank. US$255 million in equity was provided by KEPCO, Marubeni, PT Tripatra Engineers & Constructors, and ST International.<ref name = ij>[https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/19508/cirebon-coal-fired-power-plant-660mw-ipp Cirebon Coal-Fired Power Plant (660MW) IPP], IJGlobal, May 29, 2017</ref>

'''Unit 2:''' In May 2016 a press article listed a consortium of five banks (ING, Crédit Agricole, Mizuho, SMBC, MUFG) set to provide a US$640 million loan for financing of Unit 2, aiming to reach financial close by the beginning of the third-quarter of 2016. The export credit agencies Exim Bank of Korea, JBIC, and Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI) are also considering financing for the project.<ref name=bank>[http://www.banktrack.org/show/dodgydeal/cirebon3#popover=financiers "Cirebon 2 coal fired power plant,"] BankTrack, accessed Dec 2016</ref>

In April 2017, a loan agreement was finalised to provide US$1.74 billion for Cirebon 2. The export credit agencies Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) and the Export–Import Bank of Korea (Kexim) will provide 66% of project debt (US$1.148 billion). The private banks ING, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, Mizuho Bank and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation are providing the remaining 34% of project debt (US$592m). The commercial bank loans are being insured by Kexim and the Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI). The project sponsors are providing US$435 million in equity to cover the remainder of the US$2.175 billion project costs.<ref>[https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/34565?name=Cirebon%202%20Coal-Fired%20Power%20Plant%20(1000MW)%20IPP&link=%2Farticles%2F131063%2Fcirebon-2-financial-close-update "Cirebon 2 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1000MW) IPP,"] IJGlobal, accessed Sep. 2020</ref> The lead arranger of finance for the project is the global Dutch bank ING, which rejected pressure to withdraw from its role despite adopting a policy in November 2015 that it would reduce its exposure to coal projects.<ref name=awesomebob>Bob Burton, [http://endcoal.org/2017/04/embarrassment-for-japanese-government-bank-as-court-rules-coal-plants-permit-illegal/ "Embarrassment for Japanese Government bank as court rules coal plant’s permit illegal,"] EndCoal, Apr 19, 2017</ref>

'''Unit 1 Early Retirement Refinancing Facility 1 (Proposed)''' - Refinancing transaction was proposed in 2022/2023 under the Energy Transition Mechanism developed by the ADB. USD 250-300m facility on the condition that Unit 1 retires earlier (target 2035). In December 2023, a nonbinding framework agreement was signed at COP28 by ADB, PT PLN and PT Cirebon Electric Power stating that they conditionally agreed to shorten the PPA and end the plant’s obligation to provide electricity in December 2035 instead of the original July 2042. The transaction is to be finalized in the first half of 2024. The framework agreement confirmed the parties will continue discussing the financing scheme for the early retirement of Cirebon Unit 1.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adb.org/news/new-agreement-aims-retire-indonesia-660-mw-coal-plant-almost-7-years-early|title=New Agreement Aims to Retire Indonesia 660-MW Coal Plant Almost 7 Years Early|date=December 2023|website=www.adb.org|url-status=live}}</ref> As of March 2025, there was no news on the closing of the transaction.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lowyinstitute.org/the-interpreter/cutting-coal-power-indonesia-s-test-case-turning-climate-pledge-reality|title=Cutting coal power: Indonesia’s test case for turning a climate pledge into reality|date=November 2024|website=www.lowyinstitute.org|url-status=live}}</ref> In November 2025, Reuters reported that the Cirebon-1 closure was facing delays after a deadline had passed without a funding deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/indonesia-coal-power-phase-out-plan-risk-due-stalled-international-funding-2025-11-17/|title=Indonesia coal power phase-out plan at risk due to stalled international funding|date=November 17, 2025|website=Reuters|access-date=June 2026}}</ref> In December 2025, Reuters reported that Indonesia was unlikely to move forward with the early retirement of Cirebon-1, with officials instead prioritizing the retirement of older coal plants.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/indonesia-backpedals-retiring-cirebon-coal-power-plant-early-2025-12-05/|title=Indonesia backpedals on retiring Cirebon coal power plant early|date=December 5, 2025|website=Reuters|access-date=June 2026}}</ref> As of June 2026, no financial close or replacement retirement-refinancing arrangement had been identified for Cirebon-1.

==Bribery Scandal==

In May 2019 Hyundai Engineering & Construction admitted that it had given bribes of between Rp 6.5 billion and Rp 9.5 billion to Cirebon Regent Sunjaya Purwadisastra to appease residents who were opposed to construction of Cirebon 2.<ref>[https://katadata.co.id/berita/2019/05/03/hyundai-akui-suap-bupati-cirebon-dalam-proyek-pltu Hyundai Akui Suap Bupati Cirebon dalam Proyek PLTU], Katadata, May 3, 2019</ref> In October 2019 Indonesia's Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) banned three additional suspects in the case from leaving the country for three years.<ref>[https://jabar.tribunnews.com/2019/10/30/kasus-bupati-cirebon-sunjaya-kpk-perpanjangan-larangan-ke-luar-negeri-bagi-3-tersangka Kasus Bupati Cirebon Sunjaya, KPK Perpanjangan Larangan ke Luar Negeri Bagi 3 Tersangka], Katadata, Oct. 30, 2019</ref> Investigation of the bribery allegations was delayed in February 2021 when PT Cirebon Power's Corporate Affairs Director Teguh Haryono failed to appear in response to a summons of the Corruption Eradication Commission.<ref>[https://www.liputan6.com/news/read/4485786/petinggi-pt-cirebon-power-mangkir-pemeriksaan-kpk-soal-kasus-suap-izin-pltu-2], Liputan6, Feb. 17, 2021</ref>

In December 2022, the KPK announced that a former broker of Hyundai Engineering & Construction would be arrested for his alleged involvement in the bribery scandal. As Hyundai maintained their denial of the allegations, an ongoing legal battle was likely.<ref>[http://www.businesskorea.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=105743 Indonesian Authorities to Arrest Hyundai E&C Broker over Bribery Scandal], Business Korea, December 12, 2022</ref>

In March 2023, Friends of the Earth Japan and three other NGOs called on Japan’s Ministry of Finance and the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) to suspend financial disbursements for the project until a verdict was determined on the bribery charges.<ref>[https://foejapan.org/en/issue/20230329/12090/ Commencement of Trial in the Bribery Case of Cirebon Coal-Fired Power Plant Unit 2 in Indonesia: JBIC should suspend its loan disbursement and take responsible actions to halt the project!], Friends of the Earth Japan, March 29, 2023</ref>

In August 2023, former Regent Sunjaya Purwadisastra was convicted of bribery and money laundering, which included bribes related to the Cirebon 2 expansion.<ref>[https://www.kabariku.com/2023/08/kpk-nyatakan-pikir-pikir-atas-vonis-7-tahun-eks-bupati-cirebon-kasus-uang-spp/ "KPK Nyatakan Pikir-Pikir atas Vonis 7 Tahun eks Bupati Cirebon Kasus "Uang SPP","] August 2023</ref><ref>[https://foejapan.org/en/issue/20230818/13961/ "Bribery of Project Owner Revealed at Cirebon Coal Plant Unit 2 in Indonesia - Request Submitted to MoF and JBIC for Prompt Suspension of Public Support,"] Friends of the Earth Japan, August 18, 2023</ref>

In August 2024, the Indonesian Supreme Court confirmed the conviction. Following the ruling, Walhi (Friends of the Earth Indonesia) and three other local community organizations and NGOs called on the JBIC to immediately suspend the loans for the project and require mandatory prepayment of loans for the unit, in line with the provisions of its anti-bribery policy.<ref>[https://foejapan.org/en/issue/20240807/19794/ “Conviction Confirmed for Bribery of Cirebon 2 Coal-Fired Power Plant in Indonesia: “JBIC Must End Public Financing!” Local Residents and NGOs Demanded,”] Friends of the Earth Japan, August 7, 2024</ref>

In November 2024, the case had reportedly not yet been officially resolved. Walhi organizers held a demonstration demanding that the legal process be completed by the KPK.<ref>[https://betahita.id/news/detail/10740/kasus-pltu-hyundai-di-korea-maju-di-kpk-jalan-di-tempat.html?v=1732965703 Kasus PLTU Hyundai: Di Korea Maju, di KPK Jalan di Tempat], Betahita, November 29, 2024</ref>

According to reporting from May 2025, South Korean prosecutors had successfully lobbied Indonesia’s anti-corruption agency, the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK), to reactivate its investigation into allegations that a Hyundai Engineering and Construction official paid US$368,493 to former Regent Sunjaya Purwadisastra to help facilitate the construction of Cirebon-2. KPK investigators had recently interviewed Herry Jung, the then general manager of Hyundai Engineering and Construction, who was first named as a suspect in the case in 2019.<ref>[https://voi.id/en/news/485326 “South Korean Prosecutors Ask KPK To Investigate Problems Caused By The Construction Of PLTU 2 Cirebon,”] VOI, May 28, 2025</ref><ref>[https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2025/05/29/south-korea-urges-kpk-to-continue-probe-into-cirebon-bribery-case.html “South Korea urges KPK to continue probe into Cirebon bribery case,”] The Jakarta Post, May 29, 2025</ref>

In August 2025, the Seoul Central District Prosecutors’ Office announced that it had abandoned its investigation of Hyundai under the International Anti-Bribery Act for paying 550 million won (US$395,000) to win a US$727 million construction contract for Cirebon 2. The prosecutor said the investigation confirmed company employees paid bribes to the local military governor, who sought 1.7 billion won (US$1.22 million) to suppress protests by residents and civil society groups. The prosecutor said it was difficult to establish an “intent to obtain undue advantage” under the International Anti-Bribery Act, stating that the company had no choice other than to pay the bribes to ensure the safety of its staff.<ref>[https://www.chosun.com/english/national-en/2025/08/26/X6VAW5YLV5AFFLD5A2XZTKJEDA/ “Prosecutors Clear Hyundai in 550M Won Bribe Case Involving Indonesian Official,”] The Chosun Daily, August 26, 2025</ref>

==Opposition to Plant==

Protests from the community in relation to its land acquisition status delayed initial operation of the plant.<ref name = "na">[http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2012/10/19/cirebon-power-plant-stream-java-and-bali.html Cirebon power plant on stream for Java and Bali], Amahl S. Azwar, ''The Jakarta Post'', 19 October 2012.</ref>

In December 2016, a legal challenge to the project was filed by The People for Environmental Protection (RAPEL), with legal representation by the Advocacy Team for Climate Justice. At the heart of the legal challenge was RAPEL’s claim that local planning law only permitted power plant development in the district of Astanajapura, and that the Cirebon 2 expansion also extended into Mundu district, which was zoned for local livelihoods. On April 19, 2017, the regional court in Bandung ruled the environmental permit for the plant was issued illegally.<ref name=awesomebob>Bob Burton, [http://endcoal.org/2017/04/embarrassment-for-japanese-government-bank-as-court-rules-coal-plants-permit-illegal/ "Embarrassment for Japanese Government bank as court rules coal plant’s permit illegal,"] EndCoal, Apr 19, 2017</ref>

In February 2023, ResponsiBank Indonesia and WALHI (Friends of the Earth Indonesia) called on CEP and its shareholders to be held accountable for the damages the power station has placed on surrounding communities. Residents living between the Cipaluh and Kanci rivers have repeatedly voiced concerns over the social, environmental and public health impacts of Cirebon-1.<ref>[https://www.eco-business.com/news/indonesias-cirebon-1-coal-power-project-highlights-gaps-in-adbs-coal-to-clean-etm-scheme/ Indonesia's Cirebon 1 coal power project highlights gaps in ADB's 'coal-to-clean' ETM scheme], Eco-Business, February 7, 2023</ref>

In November 2024, residents of five surrounding communities held a demonstration at the gates of Cirebon power station Unit 2, demanding compensation for land now occupied by the project.<ref>[https://listrikindonesia.com/detail/14548/ratusan-warga-geruduk-pltu-2-cirebon Ratusan Warga Geruduk PLTU 2 Cirebon], Listrik Indonesia, November 7, 2024</ref>

==Environmental Impact==

Three villages located close to the Cirebon power station are experiencing severe health impacts due to coal ash from the power station being blown into residential areas. Five public health centers near the power station documented a drastic uptick in severe respiratory illness among the villagers, from 613 people in 2018 to 1,525 people in 2019.<ref>Riky Ferdianto, [https://magz.tempo.co/read/38000/voices-against-the-waste Voices Against the Waste], Tempo, June 11, 2021</ref>

An August 2023 special report in the Jakarta Post described how [https://www.gem.wiki/Fly_ash fly ash] and emissions from the Cirebon power station had polluted the farmland and fishing grounds of nearby villages.<ref>[https://www.thejakartapost.com/longform/2023/08/31/silent-invisible-danger-at-cirebon-coast.html "Silent, invisible danger on Cirebon coast,"] The Jakarta Post, August 31, 2023</ref>

A June 2024 report by the Centre for Research Energy and Clear Air (CREA) estimated that air pollution from Cirebon 1 was linked to 441 deaths a year and an associated annual economic burden of US$308 million (IDR 4.57 trillion). Cirebon 1 and [[Pelabuhan Ratu power station]] Units 1-3 have been earmarked for early retirement under Indonesia's Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) plan, and [[Banten Suralaya power station]] Units 1-4 have been mentioned as another likely candidate for early closure. CREA's report noted that these three plants account for only 20% of the top ten most polluting coal plants in Java, and that "considering health impacts as part of the factors in setting coal retirement pathways is not explicitly stated in the JETP" plan.<ref>[https://energyandcleanair.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/EN-ID-early-retirement-Cirebon-1_Pelabuhan-Ratu_Suralaya-1-4.pdf "Health and economic benefits from early phase out of Indonesia’s first JETP coal power plants,"] Centre for Research Energy and Clear Air, June 20, 2024</ref>

A March 2025 report by the Centre for Research Energy and Clear Air (CREA) estimated that the early closure of the Cirebon-1 plant in 2035 would avoid about 6000 deaths between 2036 and 2042.<ref name=CREA_Mar25/>

In November 2025, reporting recounted losses suffered by fishing communities surrounding Cirebon power station.<ref>[https://mongabay.co.id/2025/11/04/pltu-cirebon-picu-kehancuran-ruang-tangkap-nelayan/ PLTU Cirebon Picu Kehancuran Ruang Tangkap Nelayan], Mongabay, November 4, 2025</ref>

==Outage Concerns==

On June 13th, 2026, the National Energy Council inspected the Cirebon expansion unit amid concerns over electricity supply reliability following recent outages in several regions.<ref name = outage>[https://www.petromindo.com/news/article/energy-council-says-cirebon-coal-plant-operating-normally-amid-outage-concerns, "Energy council says Cirebon coal plant operating normally amid outage concerns"], Petromindo, June 15, 2026</ref>

Earlier in the month, Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia denied rumors that coal shortages triggered recent power blackouts, confirming that domestic supply allocations have comfortably reached 170 million tons. Instead, he attributed the grid issues to technical malfunctions at several power stations and noted that state-owned utility PLN is currently restoring the affected systems.<ref name=outage></ref>

==Background==

The 550 MW project received environmental approval in September 2009.<ref name="SEIA">[http://seia.sea.gob.cl/expediente/ficha/fichaPrincipal.php?modo=ficha&id_expediente=3030994 "Ficha del Proyecto: EIA Central Termoeléctrica Cochrane,"], SEIA, September 2, 2009.</ref><ref name=":10">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aes.com/sites/default/files/2022-09/AES-Fact-Sheet_Q2-2022_0.pdf|title=Fact Sheet (p 13)|last=|first=|date=August 4, 2022|website=The AES Corporation|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> A consortium of Japanese and Korean financial institutions has guaranteed up to US$1 billion in funding.<ref name="Reuters">[https://www.reuters.com/article/chile-aes-gener-loan/chile-aes-gener-in-loan-deal-of-up-to-1-bln-for-power-project-idUSL2N0CK0LD20130328 "Chile AES Gener in loan deal of up to $1 bln for power project,"], Reuters, March 2013.</ref>

Construction of the plant began in April 2013. According to AES Gener's website, the Cochrane plant was to be constructed adjacent to AES Gener's [[Angamos power station]] to take advantage of existing port and coal stockpiling facilities.<ref name="AESGener">[https://www.biobiochile.cl/noticias/2013/03/28/aes-gener-iniciara-construccion-de-planta-termoelectrica-cochrane-en-abril.shtml "AES Gener iniciará construccion de planta termoelectrica Cochrane,"], AES Gener, March 2013.</ref> 

The power generated by Cochrane's two coal-fired units will supply copper mines in Chile, with commercial operations expected to start in 2016.<ref>[http://www.mitsubishicorp.com/jp/en/pr/archive/2012/html/0000017806.html "First Independent Power Project in Chile,"] Mitsubishi, Nov. 30, 2012.</ref> In October 2014, at a press conference covered by the trade publication ''Electricidad'', AES Gener's Vice President of Engineering Luis Knaak said that the first unit would be completed by May 2016 and the second by October 2016.<ref>[http://www.revistaei.cl/2014/10/07/termoelectrica-cochrane-presenta-un-avance-de-53/# "Termoeléctrica Cochrane presenta un avance de 53%,"] Electricidad, October 7, 2014.</ref> A report from Chile's Corporación de Bienes de Capital (CBC) stated that construction on the Cochrane plant was 48% complete as of 2015.<ref>[https://www.revistaenergia.com/5274/ "El 45% de los proyectos eléctricos para quinquenio 2015-2019 está postergado,"], La Tercera, July 20, 2015.</ref>

The power station was fully commissioned in October 2016.<ref name=":2">[http://www.revistaei.cl/2016/10/13/aes-gener-puso-operacion-segunda-parte-central-cochrane/ "AES Gener puso en operación segunda parte de Central Cochrane,"] Revistaei, October 13, 2016</ref> The station comprised of two 275 MW units.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.chilesustentable.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Minuta-Anuncios-Descarbonizacion-04062019_CHS.pdf|title=Plan de Descarbonización y Retiro de Centrales Termoeléctricas a Carbón en Chile, Anuncio del gobierno de Sebastián Piñera|last=|first=|date=June 4, 2019|website=Chile Sustentable|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

In July 2020, Mitsubishi sold its 40% stake in the Cochrane power station to Daelim Energy, a subsidiary of the South Korea-based Daelim Group.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-affirms-cochrane-at-bbb-outlook-stable-22-07-2020|title=Fitch Affirms Cochrane at 'BBB-'; Outlook Stable|last=|first=|date=July 22, 2020|website=Fitch Ratings|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|url=https://www.revistaei.cl/2020/07/20/japonesa-mitsubishi-abandona-sociedad-con-aes-gener-y-deja-el-negocio-electrico-en-chile/|title=Japonesa Mitsubishi abandona sociedad con AES Gener y deja el negocio eléctrico en Chile|last=|first=|date=July 20, 2020|website=Electricidad|language=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

In April 2021, AES Gener changed its name to AES Andes.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aeschile.com/es/la-energia-de-aes-gener-es-ahora-aes-andes|title=La energía de AES Gener es ahora AES Andes {{!}} AES Chile|last=|first=|date=May 4, 2021|website=AES Chile|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=https://www.powermag.com/aes-accelerates-1-gw-of-coal-plant-retirements-in-chile/|title=AES Accelerates 1 GW of Coal Plant Retirements in Chile|last=|first=|date=July 7, 2021|website=POWER Magazine|language=en-US|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

The ownership of the plant was distributed as such:
*AES Andes S.A. (formerly AES Gener) 30%<ref name=":9">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aeschile.com/es/la-energia-de-aes-gener-es-ahora-aes-andes|title=La energía de AES Gener es ahora AES Andes {{!}} AES Chile|last=|first=|date=May 4, 2021|website=AES Chile|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> , 
*Toesca Infraestructura II 30%<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://toesca.com/en/infrastructure/cochrane-thermoelectric-plant|title=Cochrane Thermoelectric Plant|last=|first=|date=|website=Toesca|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2022-01-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oaklins.com/us/en/deals/106643/|title=AES Gener has sold a preferred stock minority stake in Empresa Eléctrica Cochrane to Toesca Infraestructura II|last=|first=|date=August 2020|website=Oaklins|language=en-US|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>, 
*Daelim Group 40%.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-affirms-cochrane-at-bbb-outlook-stable-22-07-2020|title=Fitch Affirms Cochrane at 'BBB-'; Outlook Stable|last=|first=|date=July 22, 2020|website=Fitch Ratings|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

In September 2022, the Chilean Superintendency of Environment (SMA) initiated sanctioning proceedings against Cochrane on four charges, including a severe instance of noncompliance with the Environmental Qualification Resolution (RCA). In addition to other structural and reporting infractions, an unauthorized underwater outfall was found to be discharging hot water from the facility into the bay, risking ocean pollution and other impacts. Cochrane was given 10 business days to present a Compliance Program (PDC) and 15 days to restructure its releases, after which the sanctioning process would resume.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://portal.sma.gob.cl/index.php/2022/09/05/antofagasta-sma-formula-cargos-a-termoelectrica-cochrane-por-incumplimientos-asociados-al-emisario-submarino-y-norma-de-riles/|title=Antofagasta: SMA formula cargos a termoeléctrica Cochrane por incumplimientos asociados al emisario submarino y norma de Riles|last=|first=|date=5 septiembre 2022|work=Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente, Gobierno de Chile|access-date=26 September 2022}}</ref>

In March 2023, the SMA approved a Compliance Program submitted by Empresa Eléctrica Cochrane SpA in response to the charges. As of May 2026, the sanctioning proceedings remained open with the compliance program under execution; no sanctions had been imposed.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://snifa.sma.gob.cl/Sancionatorio/Ficha/2981|title=Expediente F-042-2022: Termoeléctrica Cochrane|website=Sistema Nacional de Información de Fiscalización Ambiental (SNIFA), Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente|url-status=live|access-date=May 2026}}</ref>

==Financing==

In March 2013, a financing agreement for the plant was closed. US$1,055 million in loans were provided by MUFG Bank, HSBC, Mizuho Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Korea Finance Corporation, Japan Bank for International Cooperation, and BancoEstado. US$295 million in equity was provided by AES Corporation and Mitsubishi Corporation. HSBC acted as the financial advisor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/19237/cochrane-coal-fired-power-plant-550mw|title=Preview of Cochrane Coal-fired Power Plant (550MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-10-07}}</ref>

In October 2019, a refinancing agreement for the plant was closed. US$915 million of refinancing consists of a USD430 million, 7.5-year project bond, and a USD485 million, 15-year bank loan. The proceeds were used to repay the plant's existing project finance debt of around USD864 million.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/48609/cochrane-coal-fired-power-plant-550mw-refinancing|title=Preview of Cochrane Coal-Fired Power Plant (550MW) Refinancing {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-10-07}}</ref> Financial close was on 30 October 2019.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/48609/cochrane-coal-fired-power-plant-550mw-refinancing|title=Preview of Cochrane Coal-Fired Power Plant (550MW) Refinancing {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-10-07}}</ref> Goldman Sachs, HSBC, SMBC Nikko Securities, and LarrainVial acted as Bond arrangers.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/48609/cochrane-coal-fired-power-plant-550mw-refinancing|title=Preview of Cochrane Coal-Fired Power Plant (550MW) Refinancing {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-10-07}}</ref> It is not known who are the lenders of the bank loan.

==Planned Phase-out==

According to the Chilean Ministry of Energy's national decarbonization plan, announced by President Sebastián Piñera in June 2019, both units of Cochrane power station will cease operations no later than 2040. Plant owner AES Gener agrees to consult with the government every five years to update details of the plan, taking into account system stability requirements, energy costs, and environmental goals.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.chilesustentable.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Minuta-Anuncios-Descarbonizacion-04062019_CHS.pdf|title=Plan de Descarbonización y Retiro de Centrales Termoeléctricas a Carbón en Chile, Anuncio del gobierno de Sebastián Piñera|last=|first=|date=June 4, 2019|website=Chile Sustentable|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> 

As of June 2022, a specific decommissioning date for the Cochrane plant was yet to be determined.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=https://www.powermag.com/aes-accelerates-1-gw-of-coal-plant-retirements-in-chile/|title=AES Accelerates 1 GW of Coal Plant Retirements in Chile|last=|first=|date=July 7, 2021|website=POWER Magazine|language=en-US|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> AES Gener's recent corporate reports have listed a contract expiration date of 2030 to 2037 for its Cochrane units<ref name=":10">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aes.com/sites/default/files/2022-09/AES-Fact-Sheet_Q2-2022_0.pdf|title=Fact Sheet (p 13)|last=|first=|date=August 4, 2022|website=The AES Corporation|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aes.com/sites/default/files/2021-02/AES-2019-Annual-Report.pdf|title=2019 Annual Report (page 23)|last=|first=|date=March 1, 2019|website=AES Gener|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>, while Chile's Ministry of Energy did not include the Cochrane power station in its list of plants to be disconnected in 2019-2024.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aesgener.cl/investors/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Cochrane-3Q-2020-Earnings-Report.pdf|title=3Q-2020 Earnings Report (p 11)|last=|first=|date=December 2020|website=Empresa Eléctrica Cochrane SpA|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> In a July 2021 interview with the Chilean newspaper ''El Mercurio'', AES Corp CEO Andrés Gluski hinted at the possibility of advancing the shutdown timeline for AES Andes' remaining coal plants in Chile from 2040 to 2030, but did not commit to specific shutdown dates for either the Cochrane plant or AES's [[Nueva Tocopilla Power Station|Nueva Tocopilla power station]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://generadoras.cl/prensa/presidente-de-aes-corp-y-retiro-del-100-de-sus-carboneras-en-chile-me-parece-razonable-acelerar-estas-decisiones-para-el-2030|title=Presidente de AES Corp y retiro del 100% de sus carboneras en Chile: “Me parece razonable acelerar estas decisiones para el 2030”|last=|first=|date=July 11, 2021|website=Generadoras de Chile|language=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

According to a decarbonization report by the Chilean Ministry of Energy, the Cochrane power station would be the last remaining coal-fired power station in the community of Mejillones after 2025.<ref>[https://energia.gob.cl/sites/default/files/seguridad_abastecimiento_-_11_enero.pdf Plan de Descarbonización], Ministerio de Energia, Government of Chile, January 11, 2024</ref> By late 2024, the power station owners had still not committed to a planned shut-off date prior to 2040.<ref>[https://energia.gob.cl/sites/default/files/documentos/20241108_plan_descarbonizacion.pdf Borrador para Consulta Pública: Plan de Descarbonización], Ministerio de Energia, November 2024</ref><ref>[https://laderasur.com/columnas/declaracion-coalicion-chao-carbon-alerta-sobre-la-falta-de-ambicion-metas-y-acciones-concretas-en-el-nuevo-plan-de-descarbonozacion/ Declaración | Coalición Chao Carbón alerta sobre la falta de ambición, metas y acciones concretas en el nuevo Plan de Descarbonización], Ladera Sur, December 2, 2024</ref> The company's presentation dated March 2025 stated no specific retirement date for Cochrane.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://s27.q4cdn.com/957035463/files/doc_presentations/2024/4Q-2024-Corporate-Presentation-AES-Andes.pdf|title=AES Andes – 4Q 2024 Corporate Presentation|date=March 2025|website=https://www.aesandes.com/es|url-status=live}}</ref>

Reports published by AES Andes in the second half of 2025 identified Cochrane as one of the company's two remaining coal plants in Chile (the other being the [[Angamos power station]]). An August 2025 corporate presentation noted the Cochrane plant's "critical role in ensuring grid stability and reliability,"<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://s27.q4cdn.com/957035463/files/doc_presentations/2025/2Q-2025-Corporate-Presentation-AES-Andes.pdf|title=2Q 2025 Corporate Presentation (p 8)|date=August 2025|website=AES Andes|url-status=live}}</ref> while the company's November 2025 earnings report confirmed that Cochrane generated 642 GWh in the third quarter of 2025, an increase of 133 GWh over the same period in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://s27.q4cdn.com/957035463/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/AES-Andes-3Q-2025-Earnings-Report.pdf|title=3Q - 2025 Earnings Report (p 27)|date=2025-11-20|website=AES Andes|url-status=live}}</ref>

According to AES Andes' fourth quarter 2025 corporate presentation, Cochrane and the [[Angamos power station]] remained the only coal-fired plants in the company's portfolio as of December 31, 2025, with both described as playing a critical role in ensuring grid stability and reliability. The presentation made no reference to a specific retirement date for either plant.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://s27.q4cdn.com/957035463/files/doc_presentations/2025/q4/4Q-2025-Corporate-Presentation-AES-Andes-vf.pdf|title=AES Andes – 4Q 2025 Corporate Presentation|date=February 2026|website=AES Andes|url-status=live|access-date=}}</ref> A November 2024 report by IPS News Agency noted that Cochrane Units 1 and 2 were the only power stations in Mejillones without a defined closure date, and that the plant could remain in operation until 2040 under the existing decarbonization agreement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ipsnoticias.net/2024/11/de-fosil-a-fosil-la-contradicciones-de-la-transicion-energetica-chilena-en-la-reconversion/|title=De fósil a fósil: las contradicciones de la transición energética chilena en la reconversión|date=November 2024|website=IPS Agencia de Noticias|url-status=live|access-date=}}</ref> According to AES's Q3 2025 fact sheet published in December 2025, the Cochrane plant's contract expiration date remained 2030-2037, with electricity supplied to SQM, Sierra Gorda, and Quebrada Blanca.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aes.com/sites/vault/files/2025-12/AES-Fact-Sheet-Q3-2025-Dec-15-2025.pdf|title=AES Fact Sheet Q3 2025|date=December 15, 2025|website=AES Corporation|url-status=live|access-date=May 2026}}</ref>

==Opposition==

{{#ev:youtube|wLXgpOQMbjY|400|right|Protest video: "Mr Aes Gener: Polluting Chile for more than 50 years with coal-fired power plants", [https://chaocarbon.cl/ Alianza Chao Carbón]}}

{{#ev:youtube|EBkX6X6Bmw0|400|right|Webinar Launching the Report "AES Gener, Dirty Energy", [http://www.chilesustentable.net/ Chile Sustentable]}}

Plant owner AES Andes (formerly AES Gener) has been the subject of heavy criticism in recent years from Chilean environmental groups. In 2021, the groups Chile Sustentable, Fundación Terram and Alianza Chao Carbón published reports documenting the company's negative impact on human rights, health, and the environment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chilesustentable.net/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/Aes-Gener-Energia-Sucia.pdf|title=AES Gener: Energía Sucia: Afectación de Derechos Humanos e Incumplimiento de la Regulación Eléctrica y Ambiental|last=|first=|date=December 2021|website=Chile Sustentable / Alianza Chao Carbón|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.terram.cl/descargar/ambiente/contaminacion/Minuta-Varamientos-CarboCC81n-Ventanas-2020.pdf|title=Minuta Relativa al Registro de Varamientos de Carbón en Caleta Ventanas Ano 2020|last=|first=|date=February 2021|website=Fundación Terram|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> Alianza Chao Carbón has taken a lead role in criticizing AES Gener for not committing to a precise shutdown date for all of its Chilean coal operations, noting that it is among the few companies that have failed to do so.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elmostrador.cl/dia/2021/04/28/tras-anuncio-de-engie-de-salida-total-del-carbon-para-2025-ambientalistas-apuntan-a-aes-gener-y-colbun/|title=Tras anuncio de Engie de salida total del carbón para 2025, ambientalistas apuntan a Aes Gener y Colbún|last=|first=|date=April 28, 2021|website=El Mostrador|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

Dedisa power station and [[Avon Power Station,]] have a combined capacity of 1005 MW and are privately-owned. Dedisa started operations in September 2015 after a 24-month construction period.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.peakers.com/dedisa.html|title=Avon Dedisa Peaking Power Dedisa Peaking Power|website=www.peakers.com|access-date=2022-06-20}}</ref>

==Background==

In April 2017, J-Power submitted plans to Quang Ngai provincial leaders to construct a coal plant in Dung Quat Economic Zone (DQEZ) in two phases. Phase I would be an ultra-supercritical coal plant with a capacity of 2,400 MW, which would begin operating in 2028. Phase II would be an IGCC coal plant with a capacity of 2,000 MW that would begin operating in 2030. The plant would use coal imported from Australia, Russia, and Indonesia, as well as domestic coal.

According to Dang Ngoc Dung, vice chairman of Quang Ngai provincial People's Committee, J-Power must submit additional information concerning use of land, total investment capital, number of workers, and environmental protection commitments prior to the beginning of a pre-feasibility survey.<ref>[http://english.vov.vn/investment/japan-company-proposes-building-a-power-plant-in-quang-ngai-347585.vov "Japan company proposes building a power plant in Quang Ngai,"] Voice of Vietnam, 14 April 2017</ref>

In July 2018 Vietnam's seventh Power Development Plan (PDP7) was amended to include a 3 x 750 MW gas-fired plant in the Dung Quat Economic Zone instead of a coal-fired plant.<ref>[http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/en/electricity/announcing-the-adjustment-of-planning-of-dung-quat-power-center.html Announcing the adjustment of planning of Dung Quat Power Center], Vietnam Energy Online, Mar. 3, 2019</ref><ref>[https://www.power-technology.com/projects/quang-ngai-power-complex/ Quang Ngai Power Complex], Power Technology, Sep. 13, 2018</ref> The coal-fired plant appears to be cancelled.

==Financing==

==Background==

The plant is the largest power generating station in Nigeria.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egbin_Thermal_Power_Station|title=Egbin Thermal Power Station|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> 

'''In 1982''', construction of the plant commenced.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egbin_Thermal_Power_Station|title=Egbin Thermal Power Station|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/42567|title=Egbin Thermal Power Plant Nigeria - GEO|website=globalenergyobservatory.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref>

'''In July 1985''', the first unit was commissioned.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/42567|title=Egbin Thermal Power Plant Nigeria - GEO|website=globalenergyobservatory.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref>

'''In November 1986''', the sixth unit was commissioned.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/42567|title=Egbin Thermal Power Plant Nigeria - GEO|website=globalenergyobservatory.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref> 

'''In 2006''', unit six of the plant suffered a boiler tube explosion. Its rehabilitation lasted 3 months and was completed in January 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.vanguardngr.com/2015/01/egbin-power-plant-rehabilitated-produce-220mw/|title=Egbin power plant rehabilitated, to produce 220MW|last=Eboh|first=Michael|date=19 January 2015|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> 

'''In 2007''', KEPCO Energy Resources offered to pay US $280 million to acquire 51 percent of the power plant.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ppi.worldbank.org/en/snapshots/project/egbin-power-plant-4858|title=Private Participation in Infrastructure (PPI) - World Bank Group|website=ppi.worldbank.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref> KEPCO paid 10% of the bid amount to express interest.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211111315/http://nigeriapoliticsonline.com/korean-firm-wins-bid-for-egbin-power-plant/|title=Korean firm wins bid for Egbin Power plant {{!}} Nigeria Politics Online|date=2015-02-11|website=web.archive.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref> However, as a result of power purchase and gas supply agreement issues, the privatization process was halted.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211111315/http://nigeriapoliticsonline.com/korean-firm-wins-bid-for-egbin-power-plant/|title=Korean firm wins bid for Egbin Power plant {{!}} Nigeria Politics Online|date=2015-02-11|website=web.archive.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref>

'''In November 2013''', 70% of the company was acquired by KEPCO at US $407.3 million. The other 30% is held by the Government of Nigeria.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ozabs-us-nigeria-power-kepco-idAFKBN0TZ1MN20151216|title=Nigeria's Egbin Power plans to double generating capacity - CEO|last=Ohuocha|first=Chijioke|date=2015-12-16|work=Reuters|access-date=2022-07-11|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.usaid.gov/powerafrica/nigeria|title=Power Africa in Nigeria {{!}} Fact Sheet {{!}} Power Africa {{!}} U.S. Agency for International Development|date=2022-04-05|website=www.usaid.gov|language=en|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150211111315/http://nigeriapoliticsonline.com/korean-firm-wins-bid-for-egbin-power-plant/|title=Korean firm wins bid for Egbin Power plant {{!}} Nigeria Politics Online|date=2015-02-11|website=web.archive.org|access-date=2022-07-11}}</ref>

Egbin Power Plc plans to increase its generation capacity to 2,640 MW over three to four years at a cost of US $1.8 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ozabs-us-nigeria-power-kepco-idAFKBN0TZ1MN20151216|title=Nigeria's Egbin Power plans to double generating capacity - CEO|last=Ohuocha|first=Chijioke|date=2015-12-16|work=Reuters|access-date=2022-07-11|language=en}}</ref> The project is expected to help meet the growing energy demand. 

'''In December 2015''', Reuters reported that the company had talks with Exim Bank, the World Bank and African Development Bank were ongoing to fund the Phase II expansion plan.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ozabs-us-nigeria-power-kepco-idAFKBN0TZ1MN20151216|title=Nigeria's Egbin Power plans to double generating capacity - CEO|last=Ohuocha|first=Chijioke|date=2015-12-16|work=Reuters|access-date=2022-07-11|language=en}}</ref> The company spent US $250 million to commission engineering analysis and evacuation studies for transmission.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ozabs-us-nigeria-power-kepco-idAFKBN0TZ1MN20151216|title=Nigeria's Egbin Power plans to double generating capacity - CEO|last=Ohuocha|first=Chijioke|date=2015-12-16|work=Reuters|access-date=2022-07-11|language=en}}</ref>

'''In March 2016''', it was announced that the plant may be closed due to financial strains.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/middle-east-and-africa/2016/03/03/powerless|title=Powerless|work=The Economist|access-date=2022-07-11|issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

'''In December 2017''', the plant commenced commercial operations.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/middle-east-and-africa/2016/03/03/powerless|title=Powerless|work=The Economist|access-date=2022-07-11|issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

'''In 2022''', Egbin Power intends to begin the first phase of the expansion project starting with the construction of open-cycle turbines.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.power-technology.com/news/nigeria-egbin-power/|title=Egbin Power plans to raise $1.8bn to increase power capacity|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

'''In 2025''', Egbin expects to finish the construction of closed-cycle units.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.power-technology.com/news/nigeria-egbin-power/|title=Egbin Power plans to raise $1.8bn to increase power capacity|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

==Background==

The power station is owned by Enecogen, a partnership between utilities Eneco Energie and Dong Energy, each with a 50% stake. Construction of the plant started in May 2009 and began commercial operation in late 2011.<ref>[http://www.power-technology.com/projects/enecogen-ccgt/ "Enecogen CCGT Power Station, Netherlands,"] Power-technology.com, accessed Feb 2013.</ref>

C.Gen originally planned for the power station to be fueled by coal.{{fact}}

In 2017 DONG Energy changed its name to Ørsted and began divesting its fossil fuel assets.<ref>[https://orsted.com/en/about-us/about-orsted/about-our-name About Our Name], Ørsted, accessed Apr 8, 2021</ref> In 2018 Castleton Commodities International (CCI) bought Orsted's 50% stake in the project.<ref>[https://www.cci.com/assets/power Power Assets], CCI, accessed Apr 8, 2021</ref>

As part of its "ambition [...] to become climate neutral [...] in 2035" Eneco has proposed running Enecogen on "Green Gas", implementing CCUS, running the plants on Hydrogen, or a combination thereof.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eneco.com/wat-we-doen/duurzame-bronnen/enecogen/|title=Enecogen|website=www.eneco.com|language=en|access-date=2021-11-27}}</ref>

==Background==

An investment decision from the Quang Tri Provincial People’s Committee for the US$2.3 billion project was taken in October 2021.
<ref>[https://en.nhandan.vn/investment-policy-decision-offered-to-hai-lang-lng-electricity-centre-post104943.html Investment policy decision offered to Hai Lang LNG Electricity Centre], Nhan Dan, Oct. 8, 2021</ref>

In January 2024, ''The Investor'' reported that the joint South Korean and Vietnamese sponsors of the project were targeting 2029 for operation of an entire LNG-to-power complex, including the [[Hai Lang LNG Terminal]]. Despite construction on the power plant beginning in 2022, little progress had been made.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theinvestor.vn/hanwha-energy-kogas-invested-23-bln-lng-power-plant-targets-commercial-operations-in-2029-d8197.html|title=Hanwha Energy, Kogas-invested $2.3 bln LNG power plant targets commercial operations in 2029|last=theinvestor.vn|website=theinvestor.vn|language=en|access-date=2024-07-16}}</ref>

In May 2024, ''Gas Outlook'' said that "the project has been mired in controversy amid concerns over its economic feasibility." An analysis by the South Korean group Solutions for our Climate (SFOC) found that, based on an internal economic feasibility study, Vietnam's state utility EVN could end up spending up to US$1 billion per year buying electricity generated from the Hai Lang gas plant. In addition, the SFOC report found that the South Korean project developers plan to set electricity prices from the plant at 2,596.5 VND/kWh (US$108.8/MWh), which is 70% higher than the average price of electricity generated at major coal plants in Vietnam.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gasoutlook.com/analysis/corporate-self-interest-drives-vietnam-lng-development/|title=Corporate self-interest drives Vietnam LNG development|website=Gas Outlook|language=en-US|access-date=2024-07-16}}</ref>

In November 2024, it was reported that the target construction restart date for the plant was January 2026 by which time a range of challenges were expected to be solved. On this timeline, construction is hoped to be completed by April 2029.<ref> Tri Duc, [https://theinvestor.vn/construction-of-23-bln-central-vietnam-lng-power-plant-to-restart-in-2026-d13366.html Construction of $2.3 bln central Vietnam LNG power plant to restart in 2026], The Investor, Nov. 17, 2024</ref>

==Background==

Heshun power station is a proposed 2 x 350 MW waste coal plant in Heshun County.<ref>[http://www.sxcoal.com/coal/4183809/articlenew.html "潞安集团加快星光低热值煤项目实施,"] 中国煤炭资源网, 2015年07月01日</ref> 

===Nationwide Restrictions Imposed on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity===
In January 2017 China's National Energy Administration suspended over 100 planned and under-construction coal power projects with a total capacity of over 100GW in 13 provinces, including Heshun power station. In response, Shanxi International Energy Group voluntarily cancelled the coal plant.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20170116/803648.shtml "能源局下发13省市新建火电机组停建清单(附文件),"] Polaris, Jan 16, 2017</ref>

For details, see [[China's 2016 Restrictions on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity]].

==Background==

High River power station is a proposed power station of two units of 600 MW each. The environmental impact assessment was approved in 2014.<ref>[http://www.sxdrc.gov.cn/xxlm/nyfz/zhdt/201402/t20140217_71243.htm "第三批低热值煤发电项目公示,"] 山西日报, February 17, 2014</ref><ref>[http://cz.sxgov.cn/content/2015-05/07/content_5837836.htm "许霞就加快低热值煤发电项目开工建设现场办公,"] 长治日报, 2015-05-07</ref> 

Environmental submittals place the unit size at 2 x 660 MW.<ref>Communication from Greenpeace East Asia, January 2017</ref>

The project is under construction. It is planned for operation in 2017.<ref>[http://www.zgdlhg.com/xwzx/qyxw/2016040723270.html "山西潞安长子高河2×660MW低热值煤发电项目间冷塔及烟囱施工工程烟囱环壁浇筑提前完成,"] 中国电力化工网, 2016-04-07</ref>

==Project suspended, then revived==

===July 2017: Plant halted by government===
In July 2017 China's National Energy Administration (NEA) postponed or halted 185 coal-burning units across 21 provinces, totaling nearly 107 gigawatts (GW). 114 coal units totaling 65 GW are postponed for consideration until after the end of the 13th 5-year plan, in 2020. In addition, 71 coal units totaling nearly 42 GW were halted indefinitely for regulation violations. NEA said its goal is to eventually suspend or halt 150 GW of coal capacity during the 13th 5-year plan (2016-2020).<ref name=july17>[https://www.sohu.com/a/161854870_651522 "16部委联合发文防范化解煤电产能过剩风险,"] Sohu.com, 2017-08-03</ref>

High River power station Units 1-2 are among the halted coal-burning units, suspended indefinitely.<ref name=july17>[https://www.sohu.com/a/161854870_651522 "16部委联合发文防范化解煤电产能过剩风险,"] Sohu.com, 2017-08-03</ref>

For more information, see [[China's 2016/2017 Restrictions on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity]].

===September 2017: Suspension lifted===
After political negotiations, China's National Energy Administration (NEA) released an updated list of postponed and halted coal projects on September 26, 2017. The new list contained 151 units totaling 95 gigawatts (GW). High River power station was no longer on the list, suggesting the plant is not suspended.<ref>[https://www.sohu.com/a/197969653_279604 "2017年分省煤电停建和缓建项目名单,"] Sohu, 2017-10-12</ref>

In April 2018 it was reported the two units are planned for commissioning in 2019.<ref>[http://fgw.shanxi.gov.cn/fggz/dsdt/czsfgw/201804/t20180426_97152.shtml "杨勤荣调研潞安长子高河低热值煤发电项目建设情况,"] 长治日报, 2018-04-26</ref> [https://www.planet.com/stories/36-165148deg-n-112-96158deg-e-G-8p93NmR Planet satellite photos] through March 2018 shows construction is ongoing. In April 2020 it was reported that operation was planned for both units in August 2020.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20200413/1062627.shtml "长子高河2×660MW低热值煤发电厂即将并网发电,"] 北极星电力网新闻中心, 2020/4/13</ref>

==2021: Plant commissioned==

Unit 1 was commissioned in April 2021.<ref>[https://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20210428/1149889.shtml "山西长子高河低热值煤发电项目1号机组通过168小时试运行,"] 北极星电力网新闻中心, 2021/4/28</ref>

==Background==

The Ho-ping power station was built in 1999 and completed and commissioned in 2002. It is operated by the Ho-Ping Power Company (和平電力股份有限公司), a joint venture established by the Taiwan Cement Corporation (TCC), the CLP Group, and Mitsubishi Corporation Energy Solutions. It is the largest power plant in eastern Taiwan. Since 2002, the power station has operated under a 25-year power purchase agreement with Taiwan Power Company.<ref>[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/3564 "Ho-Ping Coal Power Station Taiwan,"] Global Energy Observatory, last updated February 15, 2010</ref><ref>[https://www.clpgroup.com/en/about/our-business/assets-and-services/southeast-asia-taiwan/ho-ping-power-station.html "Ho-Ping Power Station,"] CLP, accessed June 21, 2021</ref>

The power station, the TCC Hoping Cement Plant, and the Hoping Industrial Zone's dedicated port are coexisting structures and form a "Three-in-one Hoping Port Power Plant" circular economy park.<ref name=einfo>[https://e-info.org.tw/node/231458 "升級空污防制設備 和平電廠環評變更卡關 環委：排放濃度仍較他廠高,"] Environmental Information Center, June 18, 2021</ref>

In 2016, the legislature’s Economics Committee passed a nonbinding resolution that privately owned coal-fired power plants should be transformed to gas power plants before their electricity supply contracts with Taipower can be renewed. The committee said the coal-fired power plants should suspend operations if they cannot be transformed into gas power plants and that Taipower should not renew the contracts if privately owned utilities fail to do so. This included the Ho-ping plant, whose contract with Taipower reportedly expires around 2025.<ref>[https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2016/10/27/2003657983 "Closure of Formosa generators to affect power supplies: Lee,"] Taipei Times, October 27, 2016</ref>

In June 2021, the company was in the process of coordinating an environment assessment with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to upgrade air pollution equipment.<ref name=einfo>[https://e-info.org.tw/node/231458 "升級空污防制設備 和平電廠環評變更卡關 環委：排放濃度仍較他廠高,"] Environmental Information Center, June 18, 2021</ref><ref>[https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/life/breakingnews/3573038 "首次環評視訊會議 花蓮和平電廠案被打回票將補正再審,"] Liberty Times Net, June 18, 2021</ref>

In August 2022, CLP Group's Interim Report stated that the power station had reliable operations following a "major overhaul" completed earlier in the year. They also reported that profits were down from the project due to rising coal prices.<ref>[https://www.clp.com.cn/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/e_2022-Interim-Report.pdf "2022 Interim Report"] CLP Group, August 15, 2022</ref> CLP Group's 2022 Annual Report stated that "an amendment to the tariff reimbursement mechanism, effective from July onwards, greatly relieved the margin pressure and led to a minimal profit for the year."<ref>[https://www.clp.com.cn/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/e_2022Annual-Report.pdf "2022 Annual Report,"] CLP Group, March 2023</ref>

A company report of operations from January to September 2023 stated that the Ho-Ping power station had "continued to operate reliably and benefitted from a gradual easing of fuel costs from the second quarter onwards."<ref>[https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2023/1016/2023101600193.pdf Quarterly Statement 2023 (January – September),] CLP Holdings Limited, October 2023</ref>

According to CLP reports from early- to mid-2024, the Ho-Ping power station was still in operation, but had temporarily ceased operations following an April earthquake.<ref>[https://www.clpgroup.com/content/dam/clp-group/channels/investor/document/3-3-financial-reports/2024/e_1st%20Quarterly%20Statement%20(announcement%20version)_final.pdf.coredownload.pdf Quarterly Statement 2024 (January – March)], CLP Holdings Limited, May 13, 2024</ref><ref>[https://www.clpgroup.com/content/dam/clp-group/channels/investor/document/3-3-financial-reports/2024/e_2024%20Interim%20Report.pdf.coredownload.pdf Connected as One Strengthening Development], CLP Group, August 5, 2024</ref> Operations reportedly resumed in May of the same year.

==Background==

The two existing coal-fired units of Huaneng Jiaxiang power station, totaling 660 MW, were brought online in 2006-2007. The plant is owned by [[China Huaneng]].<ref name=ch>[http://www.chng.com.cn/n31531/n31613/n293133/n418910/n418990/c469955/content.html "华能嘉祥电厂,"] 华能集团, 2010-12-10</ref>

==Description of Expansion==

Huaneng was planning to build two additional coal-fired units at this plant, with a total planned capacity of 1,360 MW.<ref name=WRI>Ailun Yang and Yiyun Cui, [http://pdf.wri.org/global_coal_risk_assessment.pdf "Global Coal Risk Assessment: Data Analysis and Market Research,"] World Resources Institute working paper, November 2012</ref><ref name=ch>[http://www.chng.com.cn/n31531/n31613/n293133/n418910/n418990/c469955/content.html "华能嘉祥电厂,"] 华能集团, 2010-12-10</ref>

===2016: Nationwide Restrictions Imposed on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity===
Due to new restrictions announced during 2016 by the National Energy Administration and the National Development and Reform Commission, further capacity expansions at this location appear to be on hold or cancelled. For details, see [[China's 2016 Restrictions on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity]].

==Background==

The Huaneng Qufu power station was commissioned in September 2006, with construction starting in May 2005. It is located in Qufu, China.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wikimapia.org/25997324/Power-plant|title=Power plant - Wikimapia|website=wikimapia.org|language=en|access-date=2021-06-01}}</ref> The plant's boiler and steam turbine generator were manufactured by Sichuan Boiler Factory and Beijing Beizhong Turbine Motor Co., Ltd. respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%8D%8E%E8%83%BD%E6%9B%B2%E9%98%9C%E7%94%B5%E5%8E%82|title=华能曲阜电厂|last=|first=|date=|website=Baidu|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=June 1, 2021}}</ref> As the only central heating facility in the city of Qufu, it is responsible for heating the urban area (eight million square meters) and has an annual power generation capacity of 2.4 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ynpxrz.com/n2130701c1277.aspx|title=华能曲阜电厂2021年应届毕业生校园招聘启事_易贤网|last=|first=|date=October 11, 2020|website=www.ynpxrz.com|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-01}}</ref> As of September 2020, it has generated 33.4 billion kWh of electricity and 17.95 million GJ of heating.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ynpxrz.com/n2130701c1277.aspx|title=华能曲阜电厂2021年应届毕业生校园招聘启事_易贤网|last=|first=|date=October 11, 2020|website=www.ynpxrz.com|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-01}}</ref>

In February 2020, at the start of the coronavirus pandemic, coal stocks fell, creating a shortage in coal. The owners of the Huaneng Qufu power plant asked the government for aid with the delivery of new. The Qufu Transportation Bureau immediately opened a so-called 'green channel' for the Huaneng Power Plant, which ensured the smooth passage for the 15 transportation vehicles carrying coal to the facility.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sohu.com/a/372073921_118392|title=山东曲阜“绿色通道”让企业生产无后顾之忧_运输|last=|first=|date=2020-02-11|website=Sohu News|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-01}}</ref>
