==Background==

The AES Levant power plant is located east of Amman, on the same site of the existing Amman East power plant. The project was built and is owned and operated by AES Levant. The project is a tri-fuel engine technology, designed primarily for peaking operation, allowing a high range of flexibility in terms of fuel usage and dispatch.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aesjordan.com.jo/about-us/|title=– About Us|website=www.aesjordan.com.jo|access-date=2024-03-22}}</ref>

The total project cost was 360 million US Dollars. The project financing was supported by the US governmental institution Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC) and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).<ref name=":0" />

The project got commissioned in July 2014.The power generated from the project is sold to National Electric Power under a power purchase agreement for a period of 25 years, starting from 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.power-technology.com/marketdata/power-plant-profile-al-manakher-ipp-4-power-plant-jordan/|title=Power plant profile: Al-Manakher IPP 4 Power Plant, Jordan|last=kgi-admin|date=2023-04-24|website=Power Technology|language=en-US|access-date=2024-03-22}}</ref>

==Background on Project==

In March 2008, it was announced that Korean investors were exploring a plan to build a 100-MW coal-fired power plant in Sarolangun Regency in Sumatra's Jambi Province. The plan was apparently to build a mine-to-mouth plant.<ref>[http://berita.ohapa.com/28/06/41/korea-siap-bangun-pltu-berkapasitas-100-mw-di-jambi.htm Korea Siap Bangun PLTU Berkapasitas 100 MW di Jambi Jambi], Antara News, March 2008.</ref> 

In October 2013, after years of delays, a memorandum of understanding was signed between the provincial government of Jambi and Korean company Korea South-East Power Company (KOSEP), a subsidiary of Korean state-owned power producer [[KEPCO]], to build what had by then become a two-unit, 400-MW coal-fired power plant in Jambi's Tebo Regency. The cost was projected at $750 million. Groundbreaking was expected in mid-2014.<ref>[http://www.metrojambi.com/v1/metro/22556-korsel-investasi-rp-8-triliun-untuk-pembangunan-pltu-tebo-.html Korsel Investasi Rp 8 Triliun untuk Pembangunan PLTU Tebo], Metro Jambi, 15 Oct. 2013.</ref><ref>Jon Afrizal, [http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2013/05/22/south-korean-investors-build-steam-power-plant-jambi.html South Korean investors to build steam power plant in Jambi], ''Jakarta Post'', 22 May 2013.</ref>

In November 2014, with permitting for the project stalled, Jambi Gov. Hasan Bagri Agus and South Korean businesspeople travelled to Jakarta and met with Indonesia Vice Pres. Muhammad Jusuf Kalla, urging him to help speed approval of the plant. The project was apparently waiting for approval by [[PLN]], which needed to agree to purchase the plant's power.<ref>[http://harianjayapos.com/detail-7827-gubernur-jambi-terus-perjuangkan-izin-pembangunan-pltu-tebo.html Gubernur Jambi Terus Perjuangkan Izin Pembangunan PLTU Tebo], Jayapos, 8 Nov. 2014.</ref><ref>[http://www.antarajambi.com/berita/305852/pembangunan-pltu-tebo-tunggu-rekomendasi-bkpm Pembangunan PLTU Tebo tunggu rekomendasi BKPM], Antara News, 13 Feb. 2015.</ref> In February 2015, a KOSEP executive reiterated the company's willingness to build the plant.<ref>[http://jambi.tribunnews.com/2015/02/12/pengusaha-korea-selatan-serius-bangun-pltu-tebo Pengusaha Korea Selatan Serius Bangun PLTU Tebo], ''Tribun Jambi'', 12 Feb. 2015.</ref>

According to a February 2015 news release, Jambi is waiting for a recommendation from the Investment Coordinating Board (BKPM). The Governor of Jambi, Hasan Basri Agus, said he is committed to developing the plant. According to Hasan, there has been approval from the central government as well as a feasibility study process at the BKPM. The missing step has been a license from PLN.<ref>[http://www.onlinebusinessbureau.com/newsDetails.cfm?id=02-13-2015_38873 "Jambi Invites South Korean Investor,"] Online Business Bureau, February 13, 2015</ref>

In June 2016, it was reported that the project remained in limbo and still lacked permits. Otto Riadi, the head of BPMD-PPT, the regional investment and licensing board, said that more study of the arrangements between the sponsor and the government was needed, in order to clarify who would be the focal point for the project.<ref>[http://economy.okezone.com/read/2016/06/07/320/1408648/pembangunan-pltu-tebo-belum-ada-kejelasan "Pembangunan PLTU Tebo Belum Ada Kejelasan,"] Okezone Finance, 7 June 2016</ref> 

As of December 2018 there is no additional news about the project and it appears to be cancelled.

==Background on Project==

Jiexiu Chongguang power station is a proposed 2 x 350 MW waste coal-fired power plant in Shanxi Province.<ref>[http://bit.ly/1qdCpv3 "山西首定五个低热值煤发电项目"], 人民网, 2013-11-18</ref> In 2015 the power station was under construction.<ref>[http://www.zbyyts.net/show/31764.html "介休 低热值煤发电项目正式开工建设,"] 2015-08-31</ref>

==Project suspended, then revived==

===July 2017: Plant postponed by government===
In July 2017 China's National Energy Administration (NEA) postponed or halted 185 coal-burning units across 21 provinces, totaling nearly 107 gigawatts (GW). 114 coal units totaling 65 GW are postponed for consideration until after the end of the 13th 5-year plan, in 2020. In addition, 71 coal units totaling nearly 42 GW were halted indefinitely for regulation violations. NEA said its goal is to eventually suspend or halt 150 GW of coal capacity during the 13th 5-year plan (2016-2020).<ref name=july17>[https://www.sohu.com/a/161854870_651522 "16部委联合发文防范化解煤电产能过剩风险,"] Sohu.com, 2017-08-03</ref>

Jiexiu Chongguang power station Units 1-2 are among the postponed coal-burning units.<ref name=july17>[https://www.sohu.com/a/161854870_651522 "16部委联合发文防范化解煤电产能过剩风险,"] Sohu.com, 2017-08-03</ref>

For more information, see [[China's 2016/2017 Restrictions on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity]].

===September 2017: Suspension lifted===
After political negotiations, China's National Energy Administration (NEA) released an updated list of postponed and halted coal projects on September 26, 2017. The new list contained 151 units totaling 95 gigawatts (GW). Jiexiu Chongguang power station was no longer on the list, suggesting the plant is not suspended.<ref>[https://www.sohu.com/a/197969653_279604 "2017年分省煤电停建和缓建项目名单,"] Sohu, 2017-10-12</ref>

In early 2018 it was reported the plant is planned for commissioning in late 2018.<ref>[http://www.cnpowerbid.com/news/show-49555.html "山西崇光发电有限责任公司介休2×35万千瓦低热值煤发电新建项目劳务综合服务招标公告,"] CN Power, 2018-02-26</ref>

==2020-2021: Plant commissioned==

Unit 1 was commissioned in December 2020.<ref>[ "介休2×35万千瓦低热值煤发电新建项目1号机组一次通过168小时试运行,"] 中国火力发电网, 2021-01-04</ref> Unit 2 was commissioned in February 2021.<ref>[http://www.chinaepi.org.cn/show.asp?id=250728 "中国能建设计承建山西介休低热值煤发电新建项目建成投产,"] 2021-02-08</ref>

==Background==

In April 2013, the Energy Commission (EC) shortlisted five consortia to tender for the 2,000 MW Project 3B coal-fired power plant, to be developed at the respective consortium's proposed site. The five shortlisted consortia were 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), Formis Resources Bhd, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), Malakoff Corp Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd. 1MDB had proposed the plant to be located at Jimah, Negri Sembilan, while Malakoff had proposed Pulau Carey, Selangor. Both Formis and YTL Power had proposed Tanjung Tohor, Johor. TNB had proposed Tanjung Hantu - Segari, Perak.<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/Business/Business-News/2013/04/19/Energy-Commission-shortlists-5-for-2000MW-power-plant/ "Energy Commission shortlists 5 for 2,000MW power plant,"] The Star, April 19, 2013</ref> 

In March 2013, it was announced that 1Malaysia Development Bhd and partner Mitsui Co Ltd had been selected to build the project, offering a levelised tariff of 25.33 sen a kWh. The project would use IHI ultra-supercritical technology steam generator and two units of Toshiba turbo generator.<ref name="sun">[http://www.thesundaily.my/news/973005 "IMDB clinch Project 3B coal fired plant,"] The Sun Daily, March 3, 2014</ref> The plant would be built in Mukim Jimah, Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan near the existing Jimah power station.<ref name="sun">[http://www.thesundaily.my/news/973005 "IMDB clinch Project 3B coal fired plant,"] The Sun Daily, March 3, 2014</ref><ref name="intense">Gurmeet Kaur, [http://bit.ly/1cm703Z "Intense lobbying has stalled decision-making for the 2,000MW coal-fired power plant under Project 3B,"] The Star Online, February 8, 2014</ref> 

The selection followed an intense period of lobbying for the project by the two front runners, YTL Power and 1MDB.<ref name="intense">Gurmeet Kaur, [http://bit.ly/1cm703Z "Intense lobbying has stalled decision-making for the 2,000MW coal-fired power plant under Project 3B,"] The Star Online, February 8, 2014</ref>

In February 2015, 1MDB said it expected to withdraw from the 3B power project due to lack of funding, thereby allowing Malaysia's largest power group Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to take over the project.<ref>[http://www.reuters.com/article/2015/02/07/malaysia-sukuk-1mdb-idUSL6N0VG2HT20150207 "Malaysia's 1MDB calls off $2.4 bln sukuk for power project-sources,"] Reuters, February 7, 2015</ref> Due to the transfer, Project 3B was postponed from the originally proposed October 2018 start date to June 2019.<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/Business/Business-News/2015/06/30/Project-3B-plant-operation-date-postponed/?style=biz "Project 3B plant ops date delayed due to transfer from 1MDB to TNB,"] The Star, June 30, 2015</ref>

In August 2016, it was reported that construction had begun on the project.<ref>[http://asian-power.com/ipp/news/construction-kicks-off-rm12b-jimah-east-power-project-in-malaysia "Construction kicks off on RM12b Jimah East Power Project in Malaysia,"] Asia Power, August 2, 2016</ref>

In March 2017, it was reported the plant was on-track for completion in December 2019.<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2017/03/27/tnbs-jimah-project-on-track-for-completion-by-december-2019/ "TNB's Jimah project on track for completion by December 2019,"] The Star, March 27, 2017</ref>

Construction was 75% complete as of April 2018.<ref>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2018/04/04/tnb-completes-75-of-works-in-jimah-east-power-plant/ TNB completes 75% of works in Jimah East Power plant], The Malaysian Reserve, April 4, 2018</ref>

In May 2019, it was reported that Unit 1 would be commissioned in June 2019, and Unit 2 would be commissioned in December 2019.<ref>[https://www.bharian.com.my/bisnes/korporat/2019/05/563833/tnb-peruntuk-perbelanjaan-modal-lebih-rendah TNB peruntuk perbelanjaan modal lebih rendah], BH Online, May 14, 2019</ref>

Unit 1 was commissioned on August 21, 2019.<ref>Chong Jin Hun, [https://www.theedgemarkets.com/article/tnb-jimah-easts-first-power-plant-starts-commercial-operations "TNB Jimah East's First Power Plant Starts Commercial Operations,"] The Edge Markets, August 22, 2019</ref> Unit 2 was commissioned on December 27, 2019.<ref>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2019/12/31/tnbs-jimah-east-power-plant-now-fully-operational/ TNB’s Jimah East Power plant now fully operational], The Malaysian Reserve, December 31, 2019</ref>

According to an August 2025 report, a "major overhaul" of Unit 2 was planned for May 2026.<ref>[https://www.midf.com.my/sites/corporate/files/2025-08/tnb-vn-jimah_east_power-mbsbr-260825.pdf Visit Note: Jimah East Power], MBSB Investment Bank, August 26, 2025</ref>

==Planned Retirement==

In August 2022, TNB announced that they would be retiring selected coal plants earlier than planned and would be replacing the generation with renewable energy alternatives. The President and CEO of the firm stated: "TNB is very much in the driver’s seat when it comes to delivering the nation’s energy transition, and this responsibility is the impetus for TNB to accelerate our ESG initiatives". Subject to approval, the power stations initially targeted for early retirement were Jimah East power station, [[Sultan Aziz power station]] and [[Manjung power station]].<ref>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2022/08/02/tnb-to-retire-selected-coal-plants-earlier-than-scheduled/ TNB to retire selected coal plants earlier than scheduled], The Malaysian Reserve, August 2, 2022</ref>

In May 2023, it was reported that TNB had committed to retiring the coal plant in 2044.<ref name=cofirehm23>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2023/05/31/malaysias-potential-in-re-transition/ Malaysia’s potential in RE transition], The Malaysian Reserve, May 31, 2023</ref>

In December 2025, TNB reiterated that all of its coal plants would be retired by 2045.<ref name=dec25>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/annual_report/TNB_IAR2025_Sustainability_Statement.pdf TNB Sustainability Statement 2025], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, December 31, 2025</ref>

===Possible emissions reduction technologies in the plant's future===
A May 2023 news article reported that feasibility studies were underway to assess options for co-firing ammonia and biomass with coal at the power plant.<ref name=cofirehm23>[https://themalaysianreserve.com/2023/05/31/malaysias-potential-in-re-transition/ Malaysia’s potential in RE transition], The Malaysian Reserve, May 31, 2023</ref>

In October 2023, co-firing feasibility studies for hydrogen, ammonia, and biomass were "ongoing".<ref>[https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2023/10/26/tnb-quickens-move-into-renewable-energy TNB quickens move into renewable energy], The Star, October 26, 2023</ref>

In June 2024, a carbon capture and utilization project, called "Project Dragon", was initiated at Jimah East power station.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/sustainability/esg-stories-urgency-of-carbon-emission-management Calling for Action: The Urgency of Carbon Emission Management for a Sustainable Future], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, September 26, 2024</ref>

In April 2025, TNB's 2024 Annual Report stated that the demonstration carbon capture unit at Jimah East power station was 30% complete. The report also stated that a pilot ammonia co-firing demonstration was "gaining momentum" at the power station, along with exploration of green hydrogen production.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/annual_report/TNB_IAR_2024.pdf Integrated Annual Report 2024], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, April 2025</ref>

In July 2025, TNB's Sustainability Report 2024 stated that a trial burn of empty fruit bunch (EFB) pellets was conducted at the power station.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/annual_report/TNB_Sustainability_Report_2024.pdf Sustainability Report 2024], Tenaga Nasional Bhd, July 2, 2025</ref>

In December 2025, TNB's "Sustainability Statement 2025" stated that "Project REACH", a green hydrogen production project, had been initiated at Jimah East power station. The venture would include a 500 kWp rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) system and battery storage.<ref name=dec25/>

==Ownership==

Jimah East Power (JEP) is the sponsor of the project. TNB held a 70% stake in JEP while Mitsui & Co Ltd owned the remaining 30% through 3B Power. In July 2015, TNB said Chugoku Electric Power Co Inc, one of Japan’s biggest regional power utilities, might take up half of Mitsui's interest in 3B Power,<ref>[http://www.thestar.com.my/Business/Business-News/2015/07/09/New-shareholder-may-emerge-in-Project-3B-under-by-TNB-and-Mitsui/?style=biz "New shareholder may emerge in Project 3B under by TNB and Mitsui,"] The Star, July 9, 2015</ref> a deal announced in January 2016.<ref>[https://www.mitsui.com/jp/en/release/2016/1217087_8910.html "Partial Sale of Equity in 2,000MW Ultra Super Critical Coal-fired Power Project in Malaysia,"] Mitsui, January 20, 2016</ref>

In October 2021, Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) was recognized as the "Clean Coal Technology Utilization for Large Power Generation" category winner at the ASEAN Energy Awards.<ref>[https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2021/10/10/tnb-jimah-plant-wins-asean-energy-award-for-clean-coal-technology/ "TNB Jimah Plant Wins ASEAN Energy Award For Clean Coal Technology,"] Business Today, October 10, 2021</ref> The month prior, TNB announced that the Jimah East power station would be the company's final coal endeavor.<ref>[https://www.tnb.com.my/assets/newsclip/11092021a.pdf "TNB's ambitious green energy plans,"] The Star, September 11, 2021</ref>

==Financing==

In November 2015, a financing agreement for this project was closed. HSBC, CIMB Group, and Maybank agreed to arrange US$2,065 million in bonds. Mitsui & Co and Tenaga Nasional agreed to provide US$610.53 million in equity. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, PwC, and HSBC acted as financial advisers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/29438/jimah-east-coal-fired-power-plant-2000mw|title=Preview of Jimah East Coal Fired Power Plant (2000MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-16}}</ref>

==Environmental Degradation and Local Opposition==

A December 2021 narrative article discussed the environmental, social, and public health risks around coal-fired power production in Malaysia. One quote reads: "For Noh [a fishmonger in Chuah, Negeri Sembilan], the commissioning of the nearby Jimah Power Station in 2005 has made life much worse for him and the other fishers. Then a second plant, Jimah East Power Station, fired up in 2019. Since the power plants, fishing yields have crashed. When Noh started his trade in 1997, he worked with about 20 fishers. The yields then were high, with each fisher catching up to RM400 worth of fish a day, he recalls. But they can hardly haul up one-fourth of that now. The fishing community pulls in lighter and lighter nets, even empty ones. “We can no longer find prawns here,” says Noh." The article also mentions that the nearby seabed is now blackened and that crabs could no longer be found in the area either.<ref>[https://www.macaranga.org/coal-impact-fishermen-indigenous-malaysia/ "Coal Can Be Costly—Who's Paying?",] Macaranga, December 22, 2021</ref>

In 2023, it was reported that Jimah East Power Plant officials had offered monetary compensation to each local fishing boat in the amount of RM20,000, but the community of fisherpeople found the compensation a meager exchange for the damage inflicted on their homes, health, and livelihoods.<ref name=nofish23>[https://maritimefairtrade.org/too-little-and-very-late-screamed-kampung-chuah-against-environment-damage/ "Too Little And Very Late!” Screamed Kampung Chuah Against Environment Damage",] Maritime Fairtrade, March 16, 2023</ref> One local fisher said that the money was "nothing compared to the destruction of nature and depletion of fishing resources we live with in Kampung Chuah."<ref name=nofish23>[https://maritimefairtrade.org/too-little-and-very-late-screamed-kampung-chuah-against-environment-damage/ "Too Little And Very Late!” Screamed Kampung Chuah Against Environment Damage",] Maritime Fairtrade, March 16, 2023</ref>

==Background==

In 2011 KEPCO Philippines Corp. (a subsidiary of the KEPCO|Korean Electric Power Company) announced it was planning to put up a 200- to 300-megawatt coal plant in the Subic Bay Freeport Zone, to supply electricity for ship builder Hanjin Heavy Industries located in Subic Bay.<ref name=ab>Anthony Bayarong, [http://www.sunstar.com.ph/pampanga/local-news/2011/11/22/another-coal-powered-plant-eyed-subic-191998 "Another coal-powered plant eyed in Subic,"] Sun Star, November 22, 2011.</ref> (This project is separate from another proposed plant in the area, the 600 MW [[Subic power station]] by Redondo Peninsula Energy.)

In Nov. 2011, an official with the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) confirmed that KEPCO Philippines Corp. had applied to build a coal plant in Subic Bay -- in addition to [[Redondo Peninsula Energy]]'s [[Subic power station]], which was already proposed and facing public opposition.<ref>[http://subictimes.com/2011/11/22/another-coal-plant-eyed-in-subic/ Another Coal Plant Eyed in Subic], ''Subic Times'', Nov. 22, 2011.</ref> The official confirmed that SBMA received a request for a feasibility study for the project, but said, “I doubt it is feasible to produce power for one locator only."<ref name=ab>Anthony Bayarong, [http://www.sunstar.com.ph/pampanga/local-news/2011/11/22/another-coal-powered-plant-eyed-subic-191998 "Another coal-powered plant eyed in Subic,"] Sun Star, November 22, 2011.</ref>

On Dec. 6, 2012, at an energy investment summit, KEPCO Philippines President Kyu-Beng Hwang stated that the company was still planning on building a coal plant in the Philippines — although he did state that the project site "has yet to be determined."<ref>[http://business.inquirer.net/96933/kepco-to-push-through-with-200-mw-power-project KEPCO to Push Through with 200 MW Power Project], ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'', Dec. 7, 2012.</ref> Several days later, the chair of the SBMA, Roberto Garcia, stated that the construction of KEPCO's additional coal plant in Subic Bay was "not going to happen. We won't allow that." Garcia also stated that "as I understand it, they have already changed the location of the project to Bataan."<ref>[http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/320971/sbma-coal-plant-means-subics-death SBMA: Coal Plant Means Subic's Death], ''Inquirer'', Dec. 8, 2012.</ref>
In 2013 it was reported that a memorandum of understanding allowing the proposed power station was signed between the Philippine and Korean governments in 2011, but KEPCO later decided to consider another location for its proposed coal facility, and was looking at potential sites in Luzon, the largest island in the Philippines.<ref>[http://business.inquirer.net/117847/kepco-in-search-of-power-plant-site#ixzz2oF2sEi6F "Kepco in search of power plant site,"] Philippine Daily Inquirer, April 21, 2013.</ref>

In March 2015, after several years without any mention of this project, KEPCO again stated that it was planning on pursuing the project. It is unclear whether the difficulties that faced the plant earlier have been surmounted.<ref>Ritchie Horario, [http://www.manilatimes.net/2-new-kephilco-power-plants-to-add-500-mw/169599/ 2 new Kephilco power plants to add 500 MW], ''Manila Times'', 15 Mar. 2015.</ref>

According to a March 2015 article in ''Philippine Star'', KEPCO is "keen on" working with Hanjin Heavy Industries and Construction Co. to build a 200 MW coal plant that will cater to the electricity requirements of Hanjin in the Subic Bay Economic Zone.<ref>Iris C. Gonzales, [http://www.philstar.com/business/2015/03/16/1434029/kepco-gears-new-philippine-project "Kepco gears up for new Philippine project,"] Philippine Star, March 16, 2015</ref>

However, as of May 2019 there have been no developments on the project. With only an expression of interest in March 2015, the project appears to be cancelled.

==Opposition==

With President Benigno Aquino III supporting the KEPCO (Korean Electric Power Corporation) power plant, environmental activists expressed strong opposition. For example, the national coordinator of Kalikasan People’s Network for the Environment, Clemente Bautista, said that “the Aquino administration is 100% promoting and supporting dirty and pollutive coal power plants as a source of energy in the country.” Cebu residents and environmental groups, such as the Central Visayas Fisherfolk Development Center, Inc (FIDEC) and the Network Opposed to Coal Fired Power Plant (NO to Coal Power) also led protests against the KEPCO plant, citing risks for the environment and local populations’ health.<ref>[https://www.bulatlat.com/2011/07/01/aquino-support-for-coal-fired-plants-slammed-groups-say-he-lacks-environmental-leadership/ “Aquino support for coal-fired plants slammed; groups say he lacks ‘environmental leadership’”], Bulatlat, July 1, 2011.</ref>

==Background==

The '''Kamanga power station''' (also known as the '''Southern Mindanao power station''' or the '''SM200 project''') is a 210-megawatt (MW) coal-fired power station owned by [[Sarangani Energy Corp]] on the coast of Sarangani province, Mindanao, the Philippines. The proponent of the power station is [[Conal Holdings]], a 40:60 joint venture between Electricity Generating Public Company Limited of Thailand and the [[Alcantara Group]]. 

The power station is located just 500 meters from the Kamanga marine ecotourism park.<ref>[https://www.cao-ombudsman.org/sites/default/files/downloads/CAO%20Compliance%20Investigation_RCBC-01_Philippines_Nov%202021.pdf "Compliance Investigation Report"], Office of the Compliance Advisor Ombudsman, November 19, 2021.</ref>

===Initial announcement===
In 2008 it was reported that Conal had reached an agreement with the Sultan Mining and Energy Development Corporation for the supply of coal for the project.<ref>[http://www.industrialinfo.com/showAbstract.jsp?newsitemID=135694 "Conal Holdings Plans $450 Million, 200-Megawatt Coal-Based Power Project in Philippines"], ''Industrial Info Resources'', July 21, 2008.</ref>

In June 2008, Gregorio Gonzales, Conal's project manager for the plant, announced that Conal would begin building the $450-million 200-MW coal-fired plant in mid-2010; this schedule was significantly delayed.<ref>[http://www.gmanetwork.com/news/story/98890/economy/200-mw-coal-power-plant-to-rise-in-saranggani 200-MW coal power plant to rise in Saranggani], GMA News, 3 June 2008.</ref> In October 2010, [[Conal Holdings]] Vice President Joseph C. Nocos announced the company will start construction of the $450-million Kamanga power station in the first quarter of 2011 to plug a "chronic power supply deficit" expected to hit Mindanao by 2014, as well as address an expected rise in the power of electricity due to the privatization of local hydropower plants. Nocos said the coal-fired power plant, which is staunchly opposed by the local Catholic Church and environmental groups over human health and the environmental concerns, can be developed in three to five years.<ref name=bw>[http://www.bworldonline.com/main/content.php?id=20009 "Conal Holdings to start work on coal plant early next year"] Business World, Oct. 24, 2010.</ref>

===Unit 1===
Financing for Unit 1 was secured in December 2012, and the notice to proceed was issued shortly thereafter.<ref name=DOE>[http://www.doe.gov.ph/doe_files/pdf/01_Energy_Situationer/2014-Private-Sector-Initiated-Power-Projects-Mindanao%20Committed-September-30.pdf Private Sector Initiated Power Projects (Mindanao),] Philippines Department of Energy, Sept. 2014.</ref> In March 2013, Korean company Daelim Industrial took over the project as engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contractor; construction began shortly thereafter.<ref>[http://www.alcantaragroup.com/news.php?news_id=14&start=0&category_id=0&parent_id=0&arcyear=2013&arcmonth=3 105 Mega Watts from Sarangani Energy Plant Assured by September 2015], Alcantara Group press release, 22 Mar. 2013.</ref> Construction was 54% complete as of September 2014. A June 2015 press report stated that the first unit was "on target" for completion by the end of 2015.<ref>Edwin Espejo, [http://www.rappler.com/business/industries/173-power-and-energy/96193-sarangani-coal-fired-power-plant-completed-end-2015 "Sarangani to be completed end-2015,"] Rappler, June 12, 2015</ref>

In April 2016, Alsons reported that key tests had been completed in the commissioning of the first 105 MW unit of the plant and that it was now waiting for the certificate of compliance (COC) from the Energy Regulatory Commission.<ref>[http://www.bworldonline.com/content.php?section=Corporate&title=alsons-sarangani-coal-plant-awaits-erc-go-signal&id=126173 "Alsons' Sarangani coal plant awaits ERC go-signal,"] BusinessWorld Online, April 18, 2016</ref> 

Unit 1 started commercial operations in April 2016. The plant was ceremonially switched on by Pres. Duterte in January 2017, after it had already been operating for eight months.<ref name=minda>[http://www.mindanews.com/top-stories/2017/02/firm-begins-construction-of-coal-fired-power-plant-in-sarangani/ Firm begins construction of coal-fired power plant in Sarangani], Minda News, 17 Feb. 2017.</ref><ref>[http://conceptnewscentral.com/index.php/2017/01/26/duterte-switch-power-plant-sarangani/ Duterte to switch on power plant in Sarangani], Concept Central, 26 Jan. 2017.</ref>

===Unit 2===
In May 2016, company executive vice president and COO Tirso Santillan said that Alsons expected to award the engineering procurement and construction contract for Unit 2 "within the next few days."<ref>Daneesa Rivera, [http://www.philstar.com/business/2016/05/28/1587543/alsons-keen-starting-3-power-projects-mindanao-year-end "Alsons keen on starting 3 power projects in Mindanao by year-end,"] Philippine Star, May 28, 2016</ref>

In August 2016 Alsons signed a US$280 million (P13.17 billion) deal with Japan’s JGC Corp. for the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) development of the second unit. Unit 2 was planned for operation in 2019.<ref>[http://www.ibtimes.ph/jgc-inks-deal-develop-alsons-210-mw-power-plant-sarangani-280-m-3275 "JGC Inks Deal To Develop Alsons’ 210-MW Power Plant In Sarangani For $280-M,"] International Business Times, Aug 4, 2016</ref>

Construction on Unit 2 began in February 2017. The second unit was then scheduled to be brought online Q1 2019.<ref name=minda>[http://www.mindanews.com/top-stories/2017/02/firm-begins-construction-of-coal-fired-power-plant-in-sarangani/ Firm begins construction of coal-fired power plant in Sarangani], Minda News, 17 Feb. 2017.</ref> In January 2018 Power Philippines listed a target date for commissioning the plant of December 2018 and a target date for commercial operations of January 2019.<ref>[http://powerphilippines.com/2018/01/31/big-impact-power-projects-2018/ Here are the big impact power projects for 2018], Power Philippines, Jan. 31, 2018</ref>

The DOE's list of new power projects for September 2018 listed a target commissioning date of February 2019.<ref>[https://www.doe.gov.ph/sites/default/files/pdf/electric_power/mindanao_committed_sept_2018.pdf PRIVATE SECTOR INITIATED POWER PROJECTS AS OF SEPTEMBER 2018], Department of Energy, Republic of the Philippines, September 2018</ref>

The DOE's list of new power projects for March 2019 listed a target commissioning date of June 2019.<ref>[https://www.doe.gov.ph/sites/default/files/pdf/electric_power/mindanao_committed_march_2019.pdf PRIVATE SECTOR INITIATED POWER PROJECTS (MINDANAO) COMMITTED], Philippine Department of Energy, March 2019</ref> Unit 2 was commissioned in October 2019.<ref>[http://www.manilastandard.net/business/power-technology/307170/sarangani-energy-opens-another-105-mw-coal-plant.html Sarangani Energy opens another 105-MW coal plant], Manila Standard, Oct. 11, 2019</ref>

===Rate issues and local power market===
According to Nocos, currently the South Cotabato Electric Cooperative (Socoteco) II charges about P6.00 per kilowatt-hour to its consumers in the city, the whole of Sarangani province and parts of South Cotabato province. Mr. Nocos said higher power rates would take a toll on consumers with the privatization of National Power Corporation’s power plants as required by the Electric Power Industry Reform Act of 2001 (Republic Act 9136). Nocos said privatization of the Agus and Pulangi hydropower plants will lead to higher power costs as new power plant investors will have to recover their investment. More than half of Mindanao’s power requirement comes from the hydropower plants, thus consumers in the area depend on lower power rates compared with Luzon and the Visayas.<ref name=bw>[http://www.bworldonline.com/main/content.php?id=20009 "Conal Holdings to start work on coal plant early next year"] Business World, Oct. 24, 2010.</ref> 

Secretary Lualhati R. Antonino, chairwoman of the Mindanao Development Authority, said the government has not arrived on a firm decision to sell the hydropower plants to the private sector. She cited the proposal of the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry to stop the privatization of the hydropower plants. Once Conal Holdings’ coal-fired power plant goes on stream, consumers in the service area of Socoteco II will enjoy at least a peso reduction in power rates as the company will directly connect to the transmission facilities of the cooperative, Mr. Nocos said.<ref name=bw>[http://www.bworldonline.com/main/content.php?id=20009 "Conal Holdings to start work on coal plant early next year"] Business World, Oct. 24, 2010.</ref>

==Public opposition==

On November 21, 2010, a 75-boat flotilla and a human banner formed by around 800 villagers from the town of Maasim in Sarangani province in Mindanao spelled out the words "No To Coal" on the grounds of a local elementary school. The activities were part of a campaign by Maasim People’s Coalition on climate change (MP3C) and [[Greenpeace International]]. The flotilla was composed of outrigger-boats of local fishers while the human banner that spelled out "NO TO COAL" was composed of students, activists and residents.<ref name=lp>Louie O. Pacardo, [http://www.bworldonline.com/main/content.php?id=21594 "Residents oppose coal-fired power plant project"] BusinessWorld, Nov. 22, 2010.</ref> 

Amalie Conchelle H. Obusan, climate and energy campaigner of Greenpeace, said collaboration with local groups is part of the campaign to localize the advocacy against the use of coal as industrial fuel: "Greenpeace seeks for 50% renewable energy efficiency in the country by the year 2020," adding it "will ask President [Benigno S. C.] Aquino’s support to achieve this." Fr. Apollo G. Salazar of the Iglesia Filipina Independiente, a religious group opposing the coal plant, said in his talk at the event that there is a need to augment sources of power in Mindanao but "it must be from a sustainable and clean source, not coal."<ref name=lp>Louie O. Pacardo, [http://www.bworldonline.com/main/content.php?id=21594 "Residents oppose coal-fired power plant project"] BusinessWorld, Nov. 22, 2010.</ref>

The coal-fed plant is said to stabilize the energy grid in Mindanao that currently relies on hydropower, or over 50% as power source. Conal Holdings’ officials claimed on the Sarangani provincial government’s Web site that "the P20-billion facility... is the answer to [a] projected power shortage on the island in 2012." Nerissa B. Tongco, MP3C officer said: "The coal project is part of what is called the holy trinity of development aggression in Soccsksargen (South Cotabato, North Cotabato, Sultan Kudarat, Sarangani, General Santos)." The other two are the Tampakan copper project of Sagittarius Mines, Inc. and a coal-mining project under San Miguel Corp. in Lake Sebu, both in South Cotabato.<ref name=lp>Louie O. Pacardo, [http://www.bworldonline.com/main/content.php?id=21594 "Residents oppose coal-fired power plant project"] BusinessWorld, Nov. 22, 2010.</ref>

In May 2014, local scuba divers reported that the ongoing construction of the Kamanga plant was destroying pristine coral reefs in Sarangani Bay. The project manager said he would "look into the matter."<ref>Edwin Espejo. [http://www.interaksyon.com/article/86538/ongoing-construction-of-power-plant-in-sarangani-destroying-corals-divers-say Ongoing construction of power plant in Sarangani destroying corals, divers say]. Inter Aksyon, 11 May 2014.</ref>

===Complaints Filed by Community===
In February 2023, it was reported that the Philippine Movement for Climate Justice (PMCJ) and the people’s organization Sanlakas had filed a complaint against Sarangani Energy Corporation (SEC) for environmental violations committed by the Kamanga coal-fired power plant.<ref name=localcomplaints>[https://mindanaogoldstardaily.com/archives/135975 "Sarangani B’laans file plaint vs power plant"] Mindanao Gold Star Daily, Feb. 14, 2023.</ref> The local people's groups also decried the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) for "its inaction in holding SEC accountable" for violations against the Environmental Compliance Certificate issued by the DENR.<ref name=localcomplaints>[https://mindanaogoldstardaily.com/archives/135975 "Sarangani B’laans file plaint vs power plant"] Mindanao Gold Star Daily, Feb. 14, 2023.</ref> The environmental violations stated in the complaint included constant noise violations and mismanagement of soot and coal ash emissions, which locals would consistently find settled on their furniture and walls of their homes.<ref name=localcomplaints>[https://mindanaogoldstardaily.com/archives/135975 "Sarangani B’laans file plaint vs power plant"] Mindanao Gold Star Daily, Feb. 14, 2023.</ref>

==Plant ownership==

The Kamanga power station is operated by Sarangani Energy Corporation (SEC), which has undergone several changes in ownership over the lifetime of the project. SEC was initially a wholly owned subsidiary of Conal Holdings Group, which was a joint venture between EGCO International Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Thailand's Electricity Generating Public Co. Ltd, and Alsons Consolidated Resources (ACR), a subsidiary of the Alcantra Group.<ref>[https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/101537/sarangani-traders-hail-coal-fired-power-plant https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/101537/sarangani-traders-hail-coal-fired-power-plant], Mindanao Inquirer, Nov. 28, 2011</ref>. In 2012, Toyota Tsusho purchased a 25% stake in SEC and provided $25 million twoard the construction of Unit 1.<ref>Amy R. Remo, [https://business.inquirer.net/97779/toyota-trading-unit-buys-stake-in-sarangani-plant Toyota trading unit buys stake in Sarangani plant], Philippine Daily Inquirer, Dec. 12, 2012</ref> In 2013 ACR bought out its Thai partner to become the sole owner of Conal Holdings Group, thereby attaining full ownership of Conal's 75% stake in SEC.<ref>Iris Gonzales, [https://www.philstar.com/business/2013/07/10/963539/alsons-buys-out-thai-partner-conal-holdings Alsons buys out Thai partner in Conal Holdings], Philstar Global, July 10, 2013</ref> In 2017, Global Business Power Corp. acquired a 50% stake in Alsons Consolidated Resources, which included 50% of ACR's stake in SEC.<ref>Chrisee Dela Paz, [https://www.rappler.com/business/global-business-power-acquire-stake-alsons-consolidated-resources Global Business Power to acquire 50% stake in Alsons], Rappler, Jun. 5, 2017</ref>. Then, in December of 2020, Meralco PowerGen Corp. announced that it had purchased full ownership of Global Business Power Corp. for P34.466 billion (approx. 720 million USD).<ref>Alena Mae S. Flores, [https://www.manilastandard.net/business/power-technology/343089/meralco-says-sale-price-of-gbpc-is-fair-reasonable.html Meralco says sale price of GBPC is fair, reasonable], Manila Standard, Dec. 28, 2020</ref> As a result of these transfers, Saragani Energy Corporation's parent companies are now: Alcantara Group, parent of Alsons Consolidated Resources, with a 37.5% stake; Meralco PowerGen Corp., parent of Global Business Power Corp., with a 37.5% stake; and Toyota Tsusho Inc. with a 25% stake.

==Financing==

In November 2014, Alsons announced that it had received US$73.5 million loan from a consortium of Philippine and foreign banks, which it would use to partially fund its power development projects in Mindanao - the Zamboanga and [[Kamanga power station|Kamanga]] coal-fired power stations. Alsons would also use the loan to repay some of its debts. UBS Singapore acted as the lead arranger for the transaction.<ref name = fin>[https://alsonspower.com/alsons-consolidated-resources-inc-secures-73-5-million-loan/ Alsons Consolidated Resources, Inc. Secures $73.5 Million Loan], Alsons Power Group, November 2014</ref> This transaction appears to be separate from the full project financing arrangement.

In May 2017, Sarangani Energy Corp. (SEC) signed a P10.5-billion (approximately US$210 million) syndicated loan with a consortium of local banks for the construction of Unit 2 of the Kamanga power station. The consortium of local banks was comprised of BDO Universal Bank (BDO), Asia United Bank (AUB), Rizal Commercial Banking Corp. (RCBC), United Coconut Planters Bank (UCPB), Philippine Business Bank, China Bank Savings and Robinsons Bank Corp.<ref>[https://energycentral.com/news/sarangani-energy-corp-signs-p105-b-loan-local-banks Sarangani Energy Corp. signs P10.5-B loan with local banks], Business Mirror, May 11, 2017</ref>

In 2017, the Philippine Movement for Climate Justice lodged a formal complaint against the International Finance Corporation (IFC) for its involvement in Philippine coal-fired power stations. The complaint alleged that the IFC had funded these projects through its financial support to Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation (RCBC). The Kamanga power station was one of 11 power stations for which the IFC's involvement was found to be sufficient to trigger the IFC's internal accountability process.<ref>[http://www.cao-ombudsman.org/cases/document-links/documents/CAOAssessmentReport_RCBC-01_Philippines_April2019_English.pdf CAO ASSESSMENT REPORT Regarding Concerns in Relation to IFC’s Investment in Rizal Commercial Banking Corporation (RCBC) – 01 (#30235, #32853, #34115, #37489) in the Philippines], IFC Compliance Advisor Ombudsman, April 2019</ref>

==Financing==

*'''Source of financing:''' KEPCO and the Korean Development Bank

==Background==

In January 2012, Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) announced an accord with Senegal for a 250 MW coal-fired power station at a cost of US$582.52 million. Under the agreement, KEPCO and the Korean Development Bank would have entirely financed the building of the plant but in return would have had the right to sell its energy output back to Senegal.<ref>[http://leeuniversal.blogspot.com/2012/01/skoreas-kepco-signs-582-mln-senegal.html "S.Korea's KEPCO signs $582 mln Senegal power deal,"] Reuters, January 18, 2012</ref><ref name=tar>[http://www.theafricareport.com/West-Africa/senegals-dakar-out-of-the-dark.html "Senegal's Dakar out of the dark,"] Theafricareport.com, June 29, 2015</ref> Operation was planned for 2017.<ref>[http://www.reuters.com/article/2013/05/16/senegal-kepco-idUSL6N0DX2YD20130516 "South Korea's KEPCO to build coal-fired power plant in Senegal,"] Reuters, May 16, 2013</ref>

After the agreement was signed, KEPCO said that it was abandoning most of its international projects, including the one in Senegal. The government said it was looking for a new partner to pick up where KEPCO left off.<ref name=tar>[http://www.theafricareport.com/West-Africa/senegals-dakar-out-of-the-dark.html "Senegal's Dakar out of the dark,"] Theafricareport.com, June 29, 2015</ref>

An August 2016 report on the 125 MW [[Sendou power station]] said the 250 MW KEPCO project had been called off.<ref>[https://www.afdb.org/fileadmin/uploads/afdb/Documents/Compliance-Review/Management_response_on_the_request_filed_against_the_Sendou_coal_fired_power_plant_project_in_Senegal.pdf "Management Response: Sendou Coal Power Plant Project,"] Africa Development Bank Group, September 26, 2016</ref>

==Background==

Shanxi International Energy Group and partners have proposed a power station of two units of 350 MW each. The project submitted tenders for construction in 2014.<ref>[http://sxi.bidnews.cn/caigou/9320.html "山西灵石启光2×350MW低热值煤发电项目 EPC总承包招标公告,"] 中国电力招标网, 2014-03-10</ref>

The project was originally called Hejin No. 2 power station, but while seeking permitting the proposed location was moved to Lingshi County. Once permitted, the plant name changed as well.<ref>[http://www.sxdrc.gov.cn/xxlm/nyfz/zhdt/201406/t20140626_72411.htm "第四批低热值煤发电项目公示,"] 山西日报, June 26, 2014</ref> 

Construction began in June 2015. Operation was planned for 2017.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20150629/635731.shtml "山西灵石启光2×350MW低热值煤发电项目开工,"] 来源:北极星电力网, 2015/6/29</ref>

==Project suspended, then revived==

===July 2017: Plant halted by government===
In July 2017 China's National Energy Administration (NEA) postponed or halted 185 coal-burning units across 21 provinces, totaling nearly 107 gigawatts (GW). 114 coal units totaling 65 GW are postponed for consideration until after the end of the 13th 5-year plan, in 2020. In addition, 71 coal units totaling nearly 42 GW were halted indefinitely for regulation violations. NEA said its goal is to eventually suspend or halt 150 GW of coal capacity during the 13th 5-year plan (2016-2020).<ref name=july17>[https://www.sohu.com/a/161854870_651522 "16部委联合发文防范化解煤电产能过剩风险,"] Sohu.com, 2017-08-03</ref>

Lingshi Qiguang power station Units 1-2 are among the halted coal-burning units, suspended indefinitely.<ref name=july17>[https://www.sohu.com/a/161854870_651522 "16部委联合发文防范化解煤电产能过剩风险,"] Sohu.com, 2017-08-03</ref>

===September 2017: Suspension lifted===
After political negotiations, China's National Energy Administration (NEA) released an updated list of postponed and halted coal projects on September 26, 2017. The new list contained 151 units totaling 95 gigawatts (GW). Lingshi Qiguang power station was no longer on the list, suggesting the plant is not suspended.<ref>[https://www.sohu.com/a/197969653_279604 "2017年分省煤电停建和缓建项目名单,"] Sohu, 2017-10-12</ref>

For more information, see [[China's 2016/2017 Restrictions on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity]].

===2019: Plant commissioned===
Unit 1 was commissioned in April 2019.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20190429/977732.shtml "启光电厂（2x350MW）#1机组顺利通过168试运,"] 北极星电力网新闻中心, 2019/4/29</ref>

Unit 2 was commissioned in September 2019.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20190912/1006788.shtml "2×350MW！启光电厂#2机组顺利通过168试运,"] 北极星电力网新闻中心, 2019/9/12</ref>

==Background==

The Litos project's 2020 environmental impact report ([http://licenciamento.ibama.gov.br/Termeletricas/UTE%20s%20%20%20%20LITOS/ RIMA]) estimated construction start dates of 2021 for Litos 1, 2023 for [[Litos 2 power station|Litos 2]], and 2025 for [[Litos 3 power station|Litos 3]] and [[Litos 4 power station|Litos 4]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://litosenergia.com.br/RIMA_Litos.pdf|title=RIMA (Relatório de Impacto Ambiental)|last=|first=|date=June 2020|website=Oiti Consultoria Ambiental|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> A public hearing for the Litos power stations was held on September 30, 2020 to address concerns raised by the report.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://audienciaspublicas.org/cases/audiencia-publica-virtual-sobre-o-projeto-das-usinas-termeletricas-litos-1-2-3-e-4/|title=Audiência Pública Virtual sobre o projeto das Usinas Termelétricas Litos 1, 2, 3 e 4|last=|first=|date=|work=UPtime / Audiências Públicas|access-date=2023-10-04|language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.gov.br/ibama/pt-br/assuntos/notas/2020/ibama-realiza-audiencia-publica-para-o-projeto-das-usinas-termeletricas-litos-1-2-3-e-4|title=Ibama realiza audiência pública para o projeto das Usinas Termelétricas Litos 1, 2, 3 e 4|work=IBAMA|access-date=|language=|last=|first=|date=September 29, 2020}}</ref>

As of March 2022, the parent company website offered no updates on the status of the Litos power station.<ref name="ref_B">{{cite web |url=https://litosenergia.com.br/sobre/ |title=Sobre |date= |website=Litos Energia |access-date=2022-03-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210512165559/https://litosenergia.com.br/sobre/ |archive-date=May 12, 2021 |url-status=live|last=|first=}}</ref> In September 2021, Litos 1, 2 and 3 were listed as participants in Brazil's A-5 national energy auction<ref name=":02">{{Cite web|url=https://in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/portaria-n-937/spe/mme-de-14-de-setembro-de-2021-345097967|title=PORTARIA Nº 937/SPE/MME|last=|first=|date=September 14, 2021|website=Ministério de Minas e Energia/Secretaria de Planejamento e Desenvolvimento Energético|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> but did not emerge victorious.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ccee.org.br/mercado/leilao-mercado|title=Leilões - Agenda e Resultados|last=|first=|date=|website=CCEE|language=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2022-11-29}}</ref> As of October 2023, Litos continued to be mentioned in press accounts as one of several active power projects in the Macaé region<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energiaeambiente.org.br/moradores-de-macae-rj-ja-respiram-ar-poluido-e-estao-pressionados-por-novos-projetos-termeletricos-mostra-novo-estudo-do-iema-20211215|title=Moradores de Macaé (RJ) já respiram ar poluído e estão pressionados por novos projetos termelétricos, mostra novo estudo do IEMA|last=|first=|date=2021-12-15|website=Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente (IEMA)|language=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://oeco.org.br/reportagens/novas-termeletricas-acendem-o-sinal-de-alerta-em-macae/|title=Novas termelétricas acendem o sinal de alerta em Macaé|last=Emanuel Alencar|first=|date=July 17, 2023|work=((o))eco|access-date=|language=}}</ref>, but it largely dropped out of the news in 2024, leading GEM to conclude that the project had been shelved. 

In September 2025 Litos Energia submitted a formal request to Brazil's environmental agency Ibama for renewal of the preliminary environmental licenses (Licenças Prévias) for all four Litos units.<ref>[https://pesquisa.in.gov.br/imprensa/servlet/INPDFViewer?captchafield=firstAccess&data=02%2F09%2F2025&jornal=530&pagina=252 Litos Energia Ltda: Aviso de Renovação de Licença], Diário Oficial da União, September 2, 2025.</ref> In early May 2026, Ibama granted new 5-year preliminary licenses for all four units, reviving the Litos project's prospects for future development.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

==Opposition==

In November 2022, the Brazilian environmental group Arayara filed a public civil action against Brazil's national environmental authority IBAMA, Rio de Janeiro state environmental authority INEA and four private companies. The filing alleged that the Litos 1, 2, 3 and 4 power stations, along with several other proposed power plants, would have a detrimental impact on water supply and air quality in the region, and requested that additional environmental studies be undertaken prior to further development of the power plants.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://arayara.org/litigancia-climatica-arayara-org-entra-com-novas-acoes-judiciais-contra-complexo-termeletrico-em-macae-rio-de-janeiro/|title=Litigância Climática: ARAYARA.ORG entra com novas Ações Judiciais contra Complexo Termelétrico em Macaé, Rio de Janeiro|last=|first=|date=January 26, 2023|website=Arayara|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://epbr.com.br/ambientalistas-tentam-barrar-na-justica-projetos-termeletricos-em-macae/|title=Ambientalistas tentam barrar na Justiça projetos termelétricos em Macaé|last=|first=|date=November 4, 2022|work=EPBR|access-date=|language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://climate.law.columbia.edu/news/september-2023-updates-climate-case-charts|title=September 2023 Updates to the Climate Case Charts|last=|first=|date=September 13, 2023|website=Sabin Center for Climate Change Law|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

==Background==

The proposal was initially a 1,200 (MW) coal plant, with a second phase of 1,600 MW. In October 2018 the central government conceded to provincial government opposition to using coal as the fuel for the plant. The provincial government is supporting the use of LNG for the proposed plant.<ref name="oct18">[https://vietnamnews.vn/society/468524/southern-provinces-want-environmentally-friendly-lng-power-not-coal-power.html "Southern provinces want environmentally-friendly LNG power, not coal power"], ''Viet Nam News'', October 25, 2018.</ref>

In 2007, ITA-Power Company, a subsidiary of the [[Tan Tao Group]], announced that it was planning to build a 600-MW coal power plant in the Cần Đước district of Long An province, scheduled for completion in 2013. In August, 2007, the Vietnam Infrastructure Limited investment fund announced that it would be responsible for 40% of the $700-800 million required to build the plant, and in October ITA-Power stated that it would be investing $270 million of its own funds in the project.<ref>[http://vccinews.com/news_detail.asp?news_id=11366 ITA-Power to Build 600-MW Thermo-Power Plant in Southern Vietnam], ''Vietnam Business Forum'', Oct. 4, 2007.</ref><ref>[http://www.reuters.com/article/2007/08/14/vietnam-fund-power-idUKB27643220070814 Vietnam Infrastructure, ITACO to Build Power Plant], ''Reuters'', Aug. 14, 2007.</ref>

In July 2009, a 218-hectare site for the proposed plant, in Long Hựu Tây commune, was approved by Vietnam Deputy Prime Minister Hoang Trung Hai.<ref>[http://www.qdnd.vn/qdndsubsite/en-US/75/72/182/156/189/82266/Default.aspx 2 More Thermo-Power Projects to Be Erected in Bac Giang and Long An], ''People's Army Newspaper'', July 1, 2009.</ref> For years afterwards, there were no further reports on the project's progress.

In April 2015, the project was revived, now as a two-unit, 1,200-MW coal-fired plant, after the provincial government threw its support behind a new proposal by [[Daewoo Engineering & Construction]], following a visit by Daewoo E&C representatives to the province. Provincial officials stressed that the plant must include environmental controls, however.<ref>[http://www.vir.com.vn/daewoo-ec-proposes-long-an-thermal-power-plant.html Daewoo E&C proposes Long An thermal power plant], Vietnam Investment Review, 21 Apr. 2015.</ref> 

In July 2016, following a meeting between Daewoo and provincial officials, both parties said they would be moving forward with the proposal. A different location was chosen for the plant, in Phuoc Vinh Dong Commune, Can Giuoc District. The new site is significantly closer to Ho Chi Minh City — now only about 20 km from the center of the city.<ref name="nangluong">[http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/thong-nhat-dia-diem-xay-dung-du-an-nhiet-dien-long-an-i.html Thống nhất địa điểm xây dựng dự án nhiệt điện Long An I], Nang Luong Vietnam, 30 July 2016.</ref> The proposal would cost $2.7 billion, with completion scheduled for 2020.<ref>[http://www.tmhpp.com.vn/d4/news/Han-Quoc-dau-tu-nha-may-nhiet-dien-than-27-ti-USD-tai-Long-An-1-2599.aspx Hàn Quốc đầu tư nhà máy nhiệt điện than 2,7 tỉ USD tại Long An], EVN Electrical Industry News, 1 Aug. 2017.</ref><ref>[http://baolongan.vn/long-an-lam-viec-voi-tap-doan-daewoo-e-c-han-quoc-a22624.html Long An làm việc với Tập đoàn Daewoo E&C Hàn Quốc], Bao Long An, 29 July 2016.</ref>

In March 2017, in consultations with the Ministry of Industry & Trade, Long An provincial officials again recommended the Phước Vĩnh Đông site — but Ho Chi Minh City officials pushed back against the site, fearing that it would expose the city to pollution.<ref>[http://moitruong.net.vn/xay-nhiet-dien-5-ty-usd-o-long/ Xây nhiệt điện 5 tỷ USD ở Long An], Moi Truong, 17 Mar. 2017.</ref>

In May 2017, the Long An provincial government proposed switching the plant from coal to liquefied natural gas (LNG).<ref>[http://bluevn.info/de-nghi-chuyen-nhiet-dien-long-tu-sang-khi.html Đề nghị chuyển nhiệt điện Long An từ than sang khí], Blue VN, 13 May 2017.</ref>

After initially refusing to allow Long An Province to block the plants, Vietnam's powerful Ministry of Energy and other agencies conceded in October 2018 that they “respect” the decision to oppose the plants by provincial authorities. The decision follows the national government agreeing in late 2016 to scrap the proposed 1200 MW Than Bạc Lieu power station after the province stated its opposition to the coal plants and its preference for an LNG fired project. The Long An provincial government is in discussions with companies potentially interested in building a US$5 billion plant run on liquified natural gas at the same site.<ref name="oct18">[https://vietnamnews.vn/society/468524/southern-provinces-want-environmentally-friendly-lng-power-not-coal-power.html "Southern provinces want environmentally-friendly LNG power, not coal power"], ''Viet Nam News'', October 25, 2018.</ref>

In 2020, VinaCapital Group Ltd. and other investors were put in charge of the gas project. In March 2021, it was announced that the province of Long An had licensed the 3,000 MW liquefied natural gas power plant to be built by South Korea's GS Energy and fund management company VinaCapital. With an overall cost of US$3 billion, it will comprise two combined-cycle power plants, Long An 1 and 2, with a capacity of 1,500 MW each. Long An 1 is anticipated to go on stream in December 2025, and Long An 2 a year later.<ref name=VNE> Thuy Thien, [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/business/industries/long-an-province-licenses-3-bln-lng-power-plant-4252076.html Long An Province licenses $3-bln LNG power plant], VNE Express International, Mar. 22, 2021</ref> In 2021, the two unit, 3,000 MW Long An liquefied natural gas power plant was licensed by the province of Long An.<ref name=VNE> Thuy Thien, [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/business/industries/long-an-province-licenses-3-bln-lng-power-plant-4252076.html Long An Province licenses $3-bln LNG power plant], VNE Express International, Mar. 22, 2021</ref>

However, draft PDP8 from February 2021 pushed the first phase's start year to 2029-2030 and notes the proposal hasn't "yet had enough investment". There is no discussion of the second phase so its status is now shelved.<ref name='draftPDP8'>[https://moit.gov.vn/upload/2005517/20210707/du-thao-dien-viii35c6.rar Draft National Power Development Plan for the period of 2021-2030, with a vision to 2045], Vietnamese Ministry of Ministry of Industry and Trade, February 2021</ref>

==Financing==

In June 2023, the Export-Import Bank of Korea signed a memorandum of understanding with Vietnam’s VinaCapital Group and Korea’s GS Energy to finance the US$3.13 billion Long An 1 and 2 gas units.<ref>Nguyen Thuy, [https://theinvestor.vn/korea-eximbank-to-fund-3-bln-lng-power-complex-in-southern-vietnam-d5513.html Korea Eximbank to fund $3 bln LNG power complex in southern Vietnam], The Investor, Jun. 23, 2023</ref> As of October 2024, financing deals for the project did not appear to have been concluded but it was reported that Long An province had completed site clearance for the project.<ref>Tri Duc, [https://theinvestor.vn/southern-vietnam-province-completes-site-clearance-for-3-bln-lng-power-project-d12917.html Southern Vietnam province completes site clearance for $3 bln LNG power project], The Investor, Oct. 17, 2024</ref>

==Alternate location==

[[File:Long An.jpg|thumb|right|upright=2|Photo courtesy of ilovemountains.org.]]
In response to concerns about the proposed location of the project in Cần Giuộc district, the People's Committee of Ho Chi Minh City has supported a new location in Cần Đước, as shown in the map.<ref>[http://www.bbc.com/vietnamese/vietnam-39288571 "Nhiệt điện Long An: Bộ Công Thương trấn an dư luận?"] BBC, 20 March 2017.</ref>

==Opposition==

Prof. Nguyen Dinh Tuan, a professor at the Ho Chi Minh City University of Natural Resources and Environment, argued against the plant's construction in March 2017, arguing that its location — about 20 km from the center of Ho Chi Minh City — would mean that the plant would cause respiratory disease for people living in the city. The Ministry of Industry & Trade was apparently open to the idea of considering alternate locations.<ref>[http://www.baomoi.com/xay-nha-may-nhiet-dien-o-long-an-se-anh-huong-den-nguoi-dan-quan-1-8-va-phu-my-hung/c/21816428.epi Xây nhà máy nhiệt điện ở Long An sẽ ảnh hưởng đến người dân quận 1, 8 và Phú Mỹ Hưng], Bao Moi, 21 Mar. 2017.</ref> Local officials, as well as officials in Ho Chi Minh City, have also expressed concerns.<ref>[http://cafef.vn/ban-khoan-du-an-nhiet-dien-ty-do-tai-long-an-2017040407092993.chn Băn khoăn dự án nhiệt điện tỷ đô tại Long An], Cafe F, 4 Apr. 2017.</ref><ref>[http://vnexpress.net/tin-tuc/thoi-su/tp-hcm-lo-ngai-nhiet-dien-5-ty-usd-o-long-an-gay-o-nhiem-3556218.html TP HCM lo ngại nhiệt điện 5 tỷ USD ở Long An gây ô nhiễm], VN Express, 16 Mar. 2017.</ref><ref>[http://tuoitre.vn/tin/chinh-tri-xa-hoi/20170427/cu-tri-long-an-lo-lang-viec-xay-nha-may-nhiet-dien/1305501.html Cử tri Long An lo lắng việc xây nhà máy nhiệt điện], Tuoi Tre, 27 Apr. 2017.</ref>

==Background==

According to a May 2014 report in Dhaka's ''Daily Sun,'' Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) showed interest in setting up a 1,320 MW coal-fired power plant at Maheshkhali. In August 2016, the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) signed a memorandum of understanding to install the power station. The plant was expected to be commissioned on June 23, 2023.<ref>[http://www.thebangladeshpost.com/supplement/779/pdf "Power subsidy to go by 2023,"] The Bangladesh Post, April 22, 2017</ref>

In August 2017, it was reported that the BPDB had signed memoranda of understandings to build four coal-fired power plants of 1320 MW each at the [[Maheshkhali power complex]], with China Huadian, a Malaysian Consortium of Tenaga Nasional Berhad, Korean KEPCO, and China SEPCO:<ref>[http://www.thebangladeshpost.com/supplement/14395/pdf "PDB plans 13,500MW at Moheshkhali Power Hub,"] Bangladesh Post, November 18, 2017</ref> 
*[[Maheshkhali power station (BPDB/TNB)]] (Malaysian Consortium)
*[[Maheshkhali power station (Huadian)]]
*[[Maheshkhali power station (KEPCO)]]
*[[Maheshkhali power station (PowerChina)]] (SEPCO)


In March 2018, it was reported that primary work on the KEPCO project had not started, and that there were discussions of South Korea helping set up a gas plant in the country rather than a coal plant.<ref name=bpprogress>[http://www.thebangladeshpost.com/national/23320 "No progress in 19 power plants yet,"] The Bangladesh Post, March 9, 2018</ref>

According to ''Energy and Power'' in April 2019, the Pre-MoU agreements for [[Maheshkhali power station (BPDB/TNB)]], [[Maheshkhali power station (PowerChina)]], and Maheshkhali power station (KEPCO) had not advanced further "as foreign companies failed to get approval from their respective governments".<ref>[https://ep-bd.com/view/details/article/MzM4Nw%3D%3D/title?q=Dream+Islands "Dream Islands,"] ''Energy and Power'', April 19, 2019</ref> 

===November 2018 government plan===
The plant appeared to be listed in the Bangladesh 2016 Master Plan "Revisited", released in November 2018, as "Moheshkhali 1200 MW USCPP JV of BPDB & KEPCO, South Korea." It had a planned commissioning date of 2029.<ref>[https://powerdivision.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/powerdivision.portal.gov.bd/page/4f81bf4d_1180_4c53_b27c_8fa0eb11e2c1/Revisiting%20PSMP2016%20%28full%20report%29_signed.pdf 2016 Master Plan "Revisited",] Bangladesh Power Division, November 2018</ref>

==Cancellation news==

On November 19, 2020, ''The Daily Star'' reported that Bangladesh's power, energy and mineral resources ministry had finalized an energy plan that cancelled all coal plants except five under construction.<ref>[https://www.thedailystar.net/frontpage/news/future-not-coal-power-1997305 "Future not coal power,"] The Daily Star, November 19, 2020</ref> The power station would likely be cancelled as a result.

In June 2021, the Bangladesh State Minister for Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources announced the government was officially dropping ten coal plant projects in its master energy plan totaling over 8 GW of power due to delays in implementation. Two 1,320 MW Maheshkhali coal plants were cancelled, but the Maheshkhali power station (KEPCO) was not clearly among the ten cancelled coal plants.<ref>[https://unb.com.bd/category/bangladesh/10-coal-fired-power-projects-scrapped-as-part-of-master-plan-revision-nasrul-hamid/74546 "10 coal-fired power projects scrapped as part of master plan revision,"] UNB, June 27, 2021</ref>

In October 2021, the Bangladesh Working Group on External Debt (BWGED) and News Founded also wrote that the Government of Bangladesh (GOB) was expected to cancel six additional coal-fired power plants planned to be developed on the Maheshkhali Islands. The government was reportedly planning to convert the six power plants from coal to LNG and renewable energy.<ref>[https://bwged.blogspot.com/2021/10/gob-is-to-cancel-6-more-coal-power.html “GOB is to cancel 6 more coal power plants,”] BWGED, Hasan Mehedi, October 29, 2021</ref><ref>[https://newsfounded.com/bangladesh/six-other-coal-fired-power-plants-were-canceled/ "Six other coal-fired power plants were canceled,"] News Founded, undated (referencing October 8, 2020 letter)</ref>

Based on this news, the power station appears cancelled.

==Background on Maheshkhali power complex==

Maheshkhali power station was part of a large multi-plant complex being organized by the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB). In August 2013, Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) announced that it intended to develop a multi-plant power complex at Cox's Bazaar, including both coal-fired plants and combined cycle gas-fired plants. The announcement stated that the BPDB "intends to build 6000 MW Ultra Super Critical Coal Based Thermal Power Plant and 3000 MW LNG Based Combined Cycle Power Plant in different phases at Maheshkhali Upazila in Cox’s Bazar District." The announcement stated that the fuel for the projects would be imported coal and liquified natural gas. Five thousand acres were in the process of acquisition, situated within Amabassaya, Honanok and Panir Chhara mouza of Hoanok Union and Gharibhanga mouza of Kutubjhom union under Maheshkhali upazila, Cox’s Bazar. 

Additional information is available at [[Maheshkhali power complex]].

==Background==

As of early 2022, the Marlim Azul power station was the most advanced of several recently proposed gas plant projects in the Macaé region.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energiaeambiente.org.br/wp-content/uploads/2021/12/20211214_notatecnicamacaequalidadedoar.pdf|title=Qualidade do Ar em Macaé (RJ)|date=December 2021|access-date=|website=IEMA|last=|first=|archive-url=|archive-date=|url-status=live}}</ref> Construction of the power station began in 2021 with the arrival of new equipment to the site.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://clickpetroleoegas.com.br/em-macae-a-usina-termeletrica-marlim-azul-inicia-nova-fase-de-construcao-com-a-chegada-de-novos-equipamentos/|title=Em Macaé, a Usina Termelétrica Marlim Azul inicia nova fase de construção com a chegada de novos equipamentos|date=2021-08-18|work=CPG Click Petroleo e Gas|access-date=2021-09-09|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

In April 2023, the Marlim Azul plant was authorized to begin test operations<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.canalenergia.com.br/noticias/53243877/aneel-libera-5655-mw-da-ute-marlim-azul-para-teste|title=Aneel libera 565,5 MW da UTE Marlim Azul para teste|last=|first=|date=April 17, 2023|website=CanalEnergia|language=pt-BR|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>, and in July 2023 the plant received its operating license from the Rio de Janeiro state environmental authority.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://oeco.org.br/reportagens/novas-termeletricas-acendem-o-sinal-de-alerta-em-macae/|title=Novas termelétricas acendem o sinal de alerta em Macaé - ((o))eco|last=Emanuel Alencar|first=|date=July 17, 2023|work=((o))eco|access-date=|language=}}</ref>

As of July 2023, the plant was reported to be in a pre-operational state<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://oeco.org.br/reportagens/novas-termeletricas-acendem-o-sinal-de-alerta-em-macae/|title=Novas termelétricas acendem o sinal de alerta em Macaé|last=Emanuel Alencar|first=|date=July 17, 2023|work=((o))eco|access-date=|language=}}</ref>, with full commercial operations set to begin between late September and early November 2023.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://fusoesaquisicoes.com/acontece-no-setor/patria-estuda-saida-da-termica-marlim-azul/|title=Pátria estuda saída da térmica Marlim Azul|last=|first=|date=September 12, 2023|website=Fusões & Aquisições|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> 

Marlim Azul has been touted as Brazil's first power plant to operate full-time using gas from the country's offshore "pre-salt" formation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://valor.globo.com/empresas/noticia/2023/09/12/patria-estuda-saida-da-termica-marlim-azul.ghtml|title=Pátria estuda saída da térmica Marlim Azul|last=|first=|date=September 12, 2023|website=Valor|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>

==Background==

Japanese MITSUI and Company Limited and the Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Limited (CPGCBL) will jointly build a regasified liquefied natural gas power plant.<ref>Aminur Rahman Rasel [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/power-energy/2017/07/18/govt-plans-build-600mw-power-plant-matarbari Govt plans to build 600MW LNG-based power plant at Matarbari], ''Dhaka Tribune'', Jul 18, 2017</ref>

'''In April 2019''', CPGCBL put out a request for financial advisory services for the project.<ref>[https://cpgcbl.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/cpgcbl.portal.gov.bd/page/9c33abb5_e666_4a96_95b9_1e1a80f6720b/Final-FAS-EOI-Notice-r4.pdf REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EoI) FOR SELECTION OF CONSULTANT FOR FINANCIAL ADVISORY SERVICES (FAS).], CPGCBL website, Apr 4, 2019</ref>

By the end of '''2019''', CPGCBL had purchased the land for the power plant.<ref name=name/>

One of the deals involves the local Summit Group, Japan's Mitsubishi Corporation and the US's General Electric Company, Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) and GE Switzerland. At an event in Bidyut Bhaban, BPDB and GE Switzerland decided to form a joint venture company to implement the project. The joint venture will conduct a feasibility study, develop 5,600 acres of land, construct and operate the power plant, and construct an LNG import terminal and infrastructure.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/74b-deals-inked-produce-6000mw-1603933|title=$7.4b deals inked to produce 6,000MW|date=2018-07-12|work=The Daily Star|access-date=2022-08-17|language=en}}</ref> 

The estimated project cost includes US $1.6 billion for land development and US $2.8 billion for the power plant. The expected completion time is 36 months.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/business/74b-deals-inked-produce-6000mw-1603933|title=$7.4b deals inked to produce 6,000MW|date=2018-07-12|work=The Daily Star|access-date=2022-08-17|language=en}}</ref>

==Background==

'''In July 2018''', Reuters reported that U.S. General Electric, Japan’s Mitsubishi Corporation, and Bangladesh-based Summit will build a 2,400 megawatt (MW) thermal power plant and related oil and LNG terminals.<ref name=reut>[https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bangladesh-energy-investment/bangladesh-signs-deal-with-general-electric-mitsubishi-to-invest-3-billion-in-energy-idUSKBN1K11SI Bangladesh unveils $5.8 billion energy investment, two JV's with General Electric], ''Reuters'', Jul 11, 2018</ref> At the time, the $3 billion agreement was "the biggest ever private foreign direct investment (FDI) in the power sector in Bangladesh".<ref>[https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/power-energy/2018/07/11/summit-signs-3-billion-investment-deal-with-ge-and-mitsubishi Summit signs $3 billion investment deal with GE and Mitsubishi], ''Dhaka Tribune'', Jul 11, 2018</ref>

'''In July 2018,''' Reuters reported that approximately 30% of Bangladesh's population does not have access to electricity. The country relies on its gas resources for 70 percent of its energy production, but as demand has risen, its supply has struggled to keep up, and the country is now becoming an LNG importer.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://reuters.com/article/us-bangladesh-energy-investment/bangladesh-signs-deal-with-general-electric-mitsubishi-to-invest-3-billion-in-energy-idUSKBN1K11SI|title=Bangladesh unveils $5.8 billion energy investment, two JV's with General Electric|last=Serajul Quadir|work=U.S.|access-date=2022-08-17|language=en-US}}</ref>

The proposed plant is expected to come online in 2023.<ref name=":0">[https://www.asiaoutlookmag.com/outlook-features/summit-power-international Power to the People], ''Asia Outlook Magazine'', Oct 12, 2018</ref>

Summit will be the majority owner of the project, while Mitsubishi and GE will share the rest of the ownership.<ref name="Platts">[https://summitpowerinternational.com/bigger-projects-funds-singapore Bigger projects with funds from Singapore], Summit Power International website, Aug 8, 2018</ref>
