Mông Dương-2: '''US$1,461.29 million''' in debt from HSBC, ING Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, BNP Paribas, Standard Chartered Bank, CIC Bank, Natixis, Societe Generale, Credit Agricole Group, UniCredit, DZ Bank, Mizuho Financial Group, and Export-Import Bank of Korea; '''US$487 million''' in equity from POSCO, AES Corporation, and China Investment Corporation;<ref name = ij>{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/17814/mong-duong-2-coal-fired-power-plant-124gw-ipp|title=Preview of Mong Duong 2 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1.24GW) IPP {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-30}}</ref> '''US$1,163.91 million''' in refinancing debt from HSBC, SMBC Nikko Securities, Citigroup, and Standard Chartered Bank<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/47453/mong-duong-2-coal-fired-power-plant-124gw-refinancing-2019|title=Preview of Mong Duong 2 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1.24GW) Refinancing 2019 {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-30}}</ref>

==Background==

===Mông Dương-1===
In 2006, the Vietnamese government applied for a loan from the [[Asian Development Bank]] for the construction of Mông Dương-1, a proposed two-unit, 1,080-MW, mine-to-mouth coal-fired power plant in the Mông Dương district of Cẩm Phả city, in the heart of Vietnam's coal mining region. At the time, [[Electricity of Vietnam]] (EVN), the sponsor of Mông Dương-1, was going through privatization.<ref>[https://www.devex.com/projects/tenders/mong-duong-1-thermal-power-project-in-vietnam/40828 Mong Duong 1 Thermal Power Project In Vietnam], Devex website, accessed Jan. 2014.</ref><ref>[http://www.amchamvietnam.com/1697/adb-electric-power-investment-in-vietnam/ ADB Electric Power Investment in Vietnam], U.S. Chamber of Commerce Vietnam, Sept. 21, 2007.</ref> 

In October 2011, after years of apparent delays, construction on Mông Dương-1 broke ground, with Hyundai Construction & Engineering, a subsidiary of [[Hyundai Motor Group]], serving as engineering & construction contractor.<ref>[http://www.pecc1.com.vn/Nhiet-dien_34/Nhiet-dien-Mong-Duong-1_691.aspx Nhiệt điện Mông Dương 1], Power Engineering Consulting JSC I website, accessed Jan. 2014.</ref> The first unit went online in March 2015, and the second unit in October 2015.<ref>[http://www.quangninh.gov.vn/en-us/Pages/Tin%20chi%20ti%E1%BA%BFt.aspx?newsid=1226&dt=2013-08-30&cid=1 Mong Duong 1 Thermal-Power Plant: 1B Steam Drum Successfully Installed], Quanh Ninh provincial website, Aug. 30, 2013.</ref><ref>[http://vneconomictimes.com/article/business/mong-duong-thermal-power-plant-1-to-soon-connect-to-grid Mong Duong Thermal Power Plant 1 to soon connect to grid], Vietnam Economic Times, 10 Jan. 2015.</ref> By May 2015, both units had been successfully tested;<ref>[http://www.genco3.com/d4/news/To-may-so-2-Du-an-Nhiet-dien-Mong-Duong-lan-dau-hoa-luoi-dien-Quoc-gia-thanh-cong-1-255.aspx Tổ máy số 2 Dự án Nhiệt điện Mông Dương lần đầu hòa lưới điện Quốc gia thành công], EVN press release, 29 May 2015.</ref> however, both units were apparently still under construction at that point.

In December 2014, a financing agreement for the project was closed. The Asian Development Bank and Export-Import Bank of Korea provided US$1,440.85 million in loans.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/16009/mong-duong-1-thermal-power-plant|title=Preview of Mong Duong 1 Thermal Power Plant {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-30}}</ref>

Unit 1 was completed in September 2015 and Unit 2 was completed in December 2015.<Ref>Jung Min-hee, [http://businesskorea.co.kr/english/news/industry/13604-vietnamese-thermal-power-plant-hyundai-ec-completes-mong-duong-1-thermal-power "Vietnamese Thermal Power Plant - Hyundai E&C Completes Mong Duong 1 Thermal Power Plant Construction in Vietnam,"] Business Korea, 19 January 2016</ref>

In August 2025, Mông Dương-1 Unit 1 was reportedly undergoing a 60 day mechanical overhaul.<ref>[https://www.evn.com.vn/d/vi-VN/news/To-may-S1-Nhiet-dien-Mong-Duong-1-se-duoc-dai-tu-trong-60-ngay-60-14-503805 Tổ máy S1 Nhiệt điện Mông Dương 1 sẽ được đại tu trong 60 ngày], Tập đoàn Điện lực Việt Nam, July 24, 2025</ref> In March 2026, a major overhaul was planned for the second generator.<ref>[https://tuoitre.vn/nha-may-nhiet-dien-mong-duong-1-san-sang-cho-cao-diem-dien-mua-kho-20260314182314687.htm Nhà máy nhiệt điện Mông Dương 1 sẵn sàng cho cao điểm điện mùa khô], Tuổi Trẻ, March 14, 2026</ref>

===Mông Dương-2===
In December 2008, the Vietnamese government agreed to grant an investment license to AES-VCM Mong Duong Power Company — a joint venture of U.S. company [[AES]], Korea's [[POSCO]], and [[China Power Investment Corporation]] — to build the 1,200-MW Mông Dương-2.<ref>[http://www.reuters.com/article/2008/12/29/vietnam-aes-plant-idUSHAN41981920081229 Vietnam to Approve AES Coal-Fired Power Plant], ''Reuters'', Dec. 28, 2008.</ref> The project is also listed at 1240 MW (2 x 620 MW).<ref name=Power>[http://www.power-eng.com/articles/2010/12/doosan-heavy-to-build.html Doosan Heavy to Build 1240 MW Coal Power Plant in Vietnam], ''Power Engineering'', Dec. 14, 2010.</ref> In Dec. 2010, with all necessary permits in hand, AES hired Korea's Dooson Heavy Industries, a subsidiary of the [[Doosan Group]], to build the plant, with completion scheduled for 2015.<ref name=Power>[http://www.power-eng.com/articles/2010/12/doosan-heavy-to-build.html Doosan Heavy to Build 1240 MW Coal Power Plant in Vietnam], ''Power Engineering'', Dec. 14, 2010.</ref> 

AES began construction in Sept. 2011, after gaining $1.5 billion in financing from 14 banks & credit agencies for the $2 billion project.<ref>[http://energyasia.com/public-stories/vietnam-aes-starts-building-mong-duong-ii-power-plant-after-securing-us15-billion-financing/ AES Starts Building Mong Duong II Power Plant After Securing US$1.5 billion Financing], EnergyAsia, Sept. 2, 2011.</ref><ref name=bao>[http://baoquangninh.com.vn/chinh-tri/201402/to-may-so-1-nha-may-nhiet-dien-mong-duong-ii-tien-hanh-dot-dau-lan-dau-vao-ngay-27-va-28-2-2221756/ Tổ máy số 1, Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Mông Dương II tiến hành đốt dầu lần đầu vào ngày 27 và 28-2], Bao Quang Ninh, Feb. 15, 2014.</ref> Korea Trade Insurance Corporation (K-Sure) provided US$839 million in coverage for the portion of the financing provided by private banks, leaving US$280 million uninsured. The Export-Import Bank of Korea provided US$342 million of the total debt financing.<ref name = ij>{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/17814/mong-duong-2-coal-fired-power-plant-124gw-ipp|title=Preview of Mong Duong 2 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1.24GW) IPP {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-30}}</ref> 

The plant will revert to Vietnamese government ownership after 25 years of operation.<ref>[http://www.vietnambreakingnews.com/2013/10/bot-power-plant-to-start-operation-next-year/#.UtRR9GRDvmE BOT Power Plant to Start Operation Next Year], Vietnam Breaking News, Oct. 17, 2013.</ref> Unit 1 was completed in March 2015,<ref name=times>[http://www.vinacomin.vn/en/news/Home-News/Mong-Duong-coal-fired-power-plant-enters-operation-1910.html Mong Duong coal-fired power plant enters operation], Vinacomin press release, 12 Mar. 2015.</ref> and Unit 2 was completed in May 2015.<ref name=Korea>[http://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20150511005348/en/AES-Achieves-Commercial-Operation-1240-MW-Mong#.VeJfwVNViko AES Achieves Commercial Operation of 1,240 MW Mong Duong 2 Plant in Vietnam], AES Corp press release, 11 May 2015.</ref>

In August 2019 a refinancing package for Mông Dương-2 was announced.<ref>[https://www.globalcapital.com/article/b1gp9r3rqdpl69/mong-duong-finance-eyes-$485m-to-take-out-project-financing Mong Duong Finance eyes $485m to take out project financing], Global Capital Asia, 12 Aug 2019.</ref> This involves a US$1.1 billion new debt package aimed at refinancing the remaining outstanding loan for the plant, whereby the proceeds from a new loan and bond issue will be used by AES-VCM Mong Duong Power Company to purchase the original project loan from the existing lenders. Citi, HSBC, Standard Chartered and Sumitomo Mitsui Finance Group are the main arranging banks on the refinancing package.

In January 2021, AES announced its intention to sell the entirety of its 51% equity stake in the Mong Duong II power station, in line with its goals to make its operations more sustainable. The purchaser was said to be "a consortium led by a U.S.-based investor", but specific entities were not named. The transaction was expected to be finalized by late 2021 or early 2022.<ref>[https://e.vnexpress.net/news/business/economy/us-energy-giant-to-pull-out-of-northern-coal-fired-power-plant-4216917.html US energy giant to pull out of northern coal-fired power plant], VnExpress, Jan. 7, 2021</ref>

According to AES' annual SEC report, published in February 2022, the sale was expected to close in early 2023. The agreement was subject to approval by the Vietnam government.<ref>[https://sec.report/Document/0000874761-22-000022/ Form 10-K Aes Corp], United States Securities and Exchange Commission, February 28, 2022</ref>

AES' 2022 annual report, published in May 2023, stated that the transaction had not closed in time and was therefore terminated. AES retained its majority interest in Mông Dương-2.<ref>[https://www.aes.com/sites/aesvault.com/files/2023-05/2022%20Annual%20Report.pdf 2022 Annual Report], AES, May 15, 2023</ref>

In November 2023, AES was negotiating the potential sale of its 51% stake in the power station to Sev.en Global Investments, a part of the Czech energy firm Sev.en Group. POSCO was reportedly also considering selling its 30% stake in the power station.<ref name=Reuters_1123>[https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/aes-talks-sell-major-coal-fired-power-plant-vietnam-sources-2023-11-17/ Exclusive: AES in talks to sell major coal-fired power plant in Vietnam - sources], Reuters, November 17, 2023</ref> Later in the month, AES announced it had agreed to sell its stake in Mông Dương-2 to Sev.en Global Investments. Pending approval from the Vietnamese government, AES anticipated the sale would be finalized by the end of 2025.<ref>[https://aescorporation2023cr.q4web.com/press-releases/news-details/2023/AES-Announces-Sale-of-Mong-Duong-2-Plant-in-Vietnam-in-Next-Decarbonization-Milestone/default.aspx AES Announces Sale of Mong Duong 2 Plant in Vietnam in Next Decarbonization Milestone], AES Corporation, November 30, 2023</ref> The plan to sell by the end of 2025 was reiterated in AES' 2023 Annual Report.<ref>[https://s202.q4cdn.com/986265382/files/doc_financials/2023/ar/2023-annual-report-wrap-10-K-FINAL.pdf 2023 Annual Report], AES, accessed May 10, 2024</ref>

As of June 2024, Mông Dương-2 reportedly had 273 employees.<ref>[http://nhietdiencaongan.vn/tham-quan-hoc-hoi-kinh-nghiem-tai-nha-may-nhiet-dien-mong-duong-2/ THAM QUAN, HỌC HỎI KINH NGHIỆM TẠI NHÀ MÁY NHIỆT ĐIỆN MÔNG DƯƠNG 2], Nhiệt điện cao ngạn, June 4, 2024</ref>

As of January 2025, the sale to Sev.en was not yet final.<ref>[https://theleader.vn/ve-dep-cua-nhiet-dien-mong-duong-2-trong-mat-nha-dau-tu-sec-d38667.html Vẻ đẹp của nhiệt điện Mông Dương 2 trong mắt nhà đầu tư Séc], The Leader, January 11, 2025</ref> In March 2025, the sale was expected to be completed in early 2026.<ref>[https://theinvestor.vn/aes-earns-34-mln-from-coal-fired-power-plant-in-vietnam-in-2024-3rd-consecutive-fall-d15003.html AES earns $34 mln from coal-fired power plant in Vietnam in 2024, 3rd consecutive fall], The Investor, March 25, 2025</ref> As of August 2025, however, the sale agreement would reportedly expire in November.<ref>[https://cafef.vn/dai-gia-nang-luong-my-do-be-ke-hoach-thoai-von-nha-may-nhiet-dien-21-ty-usd-tai-quang-ninh-18825081007055086.chn Đại gia năng lượng Mỹ đổ bể kế hoạch thoái vốn nhà máy nhiệt điện 2,1 tỷ USD tại Quảng Ninh?], CafeF, August 10, 2025</ref>

In September 2025, Vietnam’s Ministry of Finance proposed exempting the foreign owners of seven coal power plants from the requirement to pay a 15% global minimum corporate tax rate set by the OECD. The list of coal plants, which were developed under “build-operate-transfer” (BOT) contracts, included Mông Dương-2, [https://www.gem.wiki/Vinh_Tan_power_station Vĩnh Tân-1], [https://www.gem.wiki/Nghi_Son_coal_power_station Nghi Sơn-2], [https://www.gem.wiki/Van_Phong_power_station Vân Phong-1], [https://www.gem.wiki/Vung_Ang_power_station Vũng Áng-2], [[Hai Duong Thermal Power Plant]], and [https://www.gem.wiki/Duyen_Hai_Power_Generation_Complex Duyên Hải-2].<ref>[https://vneconomy.vn/de-xuat-mien-tru-thue-toi-thieu-toan-cau-cho-du-an-bot-dien-co-bao-lanh-chinh-phu.htm “Đề xuất miễn trừ thuế tối thiểu toàn cầu cho dự án BOT điện có bảo lãnh Chính phủ,”] VnEconomy, September 11, 2025</ref> The Ministry argued that imposing the 15% minimum tax could trigger compensation obligations that “would expose the Vietnamese government to the risk of having to pay compensation that exceeds the tax revenues.”<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/vietnam-exempt-mitsubishi-kepco-other-coal-power-plant-operators-global-tax-2025-09-12/ “Vietnam to exempt Mitsubishi, Kepco, other coal power plant operators from global tax, document shows,”] Reuters, September 11, 2025</ref>

In April 2026, nearby residents alleged that a local road being used to transport fly ash from Mông Dương-2 was causing frequent dust and noise pollution.<ref>[https://vtv.vn/quang-ninh-lam-ro-phan-anh-ve-viec-su-dung-tuyen-duong-van-chuyen-tro-xi-tai-xa-hai-hoa-100260401173957759.htm Quảng Ninh: Làm rõ phản ánh về việc sử dụng tuyến đường vận chuyển tro xỉ tại xã Hải Hòa], VTV.vn, April 4, 2026</ref>

==Typhoon Yagi==

In September 2024, Mông Dương-1 and Mông Dương-2 were proactively taken offline in anticipation of Typhoon Yagi. The units were out of service and were not immediately brought back into operation.<ref>[https://baotintuc.vn/kinh-te/som-dua-cac-to-may-phat-dien-tro-lai-nhanh-nhat-20240908130812019.htm Sớm đưa các tổ máy phát điện trở lại nhanh nhất], Tin tức, September 8, 2024</ref>

==Background==

In September 2014, the Burma Ministry of Electric Power, the A1 Group of Companies, and a consortium of Japanese companies including Mitsubishi announced they would partner to build the Nga Yoke Kaung coal power plant, with a total installed capacity of 300 MW.<ref name=irr>[http://www.irrawaddy.org/business/locals-block-coal-plant-survey-mitsubishi-promises-japan-study-trip.html "After Locals Block Coal Plant Survey, Mitsubishi Promises Japan Study Trip,"] The Irrawaddy, February 3, 2015</ref> 

In February 2015, employees of the A1 Group of Companies were met by more than 200 residents of the coastal region of Nga Yoke Kaung. The employees left the area before completing the preliminary project survey work after being told the project did not have local support. Around 200 acres of land would have been required to build the power plant, and affected villagers would have needed to be relocated.<ref name=irr>[http://www.irrawaddy.org/business/locals-block-coal-plant-survey-mitsubishi-promises-japan-study-trip.html "After Locals Block Coal Plant Survey, Mitsubishi Promises Japan Study Trip,"] The Irrawaddy, February 3, 2015</ref>

In July 2015, Irrawaddy Division’s Electricity and Industry Minister confirmed feasibility studies on the project had been suspended due to local opposition, although the chairman of the A1 Group of Companies said it was due to the monsoon season.<ref>[http://www.irrawaddy.org/burma/irrawaddy-division-coal-power-plant-grounded-on-local-pushback.html "Irrawaddy Division Coal Power Plant Grounded on Local Pushback,"] Irrawaddy, July 6, 2015</ref>

==Funding==

The Japanese consortium and A1 Group were set to fund 30 percent of the power plant, with the remainder to be funded by loans from the World Bank (WB) and Asian Development Bank (ADB), according to A1 Group chairman Yan Win in 2015. However, the WB and ADB did not confirm their involvement.<ref name=irr>[http://www.irrawaddy.org/business/locals-block-coal-plant-survey-mitsubishi-promises-japan-study-trip.html "After Locals Block Coal Plant Survey, Mitsubishi Promises Japan Study Trip,"] The Irrawaddy, February 3, 2015</ref>

==Coal source==

Coal for the plant was to be imported from Indonesia and Australia, with A1 announcing that a deep sea port catering to bulk carriers of up to 80,000 tonnes capacity would be built next to the power station.<ref name=irr>[http://www.irrawaddy.org/business/locals-block-coal-plant-survey-mitsubishi-promises-japan-study-trip.html "After Locals Block Coal Plant Survey, Mitsubishi Promises Japan Study Trip,"] The Irrawaddy, February 3, 2015</ref>

==Background==

The Nghi Sơn Economic Zone was created in 2005, and its future plans called for a power plant project totaling 1,800 MW.<ref>[http://vietnamnews.vn/economy/159578/new-nghi-son-zone-calls-for-investment.html New Nghi Son Zone Calls for Investment], Viêt Nam News, Nov. 28, 2006.</ref> 

Additionally, within the Nghi Sơn Economic Zone is the nearby [[Cong Thanh power station]], which is also currently under development; several miles to the south, across the provincial border in Nghệ An province, is the [[Quynh Lap power station]] project site.

===Nghi Sơn-1===
In June 2010, project sponsor [[Electricity of Vietnam]] awarded the construction contract for the 600-MW, $1.2 billion [[Nghi Son 1 power station|Nghi Sơn-1 coal-fired power plant]] to Japan's [[Marubeni Corporation]]. Construction began in July.<ref>[http://www.pennenergy.com/articles/pennenergy/2010/07/construction-of-nghi.html Construction of Nghi Son 1 Thermoelectric Plant Begins in Vietnam], PennEnergy, July 7, 2010.</ref> The plant's first 300-MW unit went online in June 2013; the second unit came online in June 2014.<ref>[http://talkvietnam.com/2013/06/first-turbine-of-nghi-son-1-thermoelectric-plant-to-be-operational-in-june/#.UtWHUmRDvmE First Turbine of Nghi Son 1 Thermoelectric Plant to Be Operational in June], TalkVietnam, June 9, 2013.</ref><ref>[http://www.thanhnien.com.vn/doi-song/nhiet-dien-nghi-son-1-da-san-sang-van-hanh-thuong-mai-81140.html Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1 đã sẵn sàng vận hành thương mại], Thanh Nien Online, 2 May 2014.</ref>

In June 2023, Unit 1 was offline for 10 days following an incident that required repairs.<ref>[https://moit.gov.vn/tin-tuc/phat-trien-nang-luong/ca-2-to-may-nhiet-dien-nghi-son-1-dang-phat-dien-toi-da.html Cả 2 tổ máy Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1 đang phát điện tối đa], Bộ Công Thương, June 14, 2023.</ref> In September 2023, Unit 2 was taken offline for planned maintenance.<ref>[https://tapchicongthuong.vn/bai-viet/dam-bao-van-hanh-an-toan-on-dinh-nha-may-nhiet-dien-nghi-son-1-111823.htm Đảm bảo vận hành an toàn, ổn định Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1], Công Thương, October 5, 2023.</ref> In February 2024, Unit 1 was reconnected to the grid following additional repairs.<ref>[https://www.evn.com.vn/d6/news/Cong-ty-Nhiet-dien-Nghi-Son-chuan-bi-nhu-the-nao-truoc-cao-diem-mua-kho-nam-2024-6-14-123407.aspx Công ty Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn chuẩn bị như thế nào trước cao điểm mùa khô năm 2024?], EVN, February 23, 2024</ref> As of May 2024, both units were operating normally.<ref>[https://congthuong.vn/nha-may-nhiet-dien-nghi-son-1-gop-phan-dam-bao-cung-ung-dien-trong-dip-le-304-15-318222.html Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1: Góp phần đảm bảo cung ứng điện trong dịp lễ 30/4 - 1/5], Công Thương, May 4, 2024</ref>

In September 2025, contract bidding was underway for the installation of technical upgrades at Nghi Sơn-1 power station.<ref>[https://baodauthau.vn/goi-thau-55-ty-dong-tai-nhiet-dien-nghi-son-1-vi-sao-tiep-tuc-gia-han-moi-thau-post184319.html Gói thầu 55 tỷ đồng tại Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1: Vì sao tiếp tục gia hạn mời thầu?], Báo Đấu thầu, September 3, 2025</ref> Unit 1 was slated to undergo scheduled maintenance to "replace equipment and improve operational reliability" (Google translate).<ref>[https://nghison.evn.vn/d4/news/Nha-may-Nhiet-dien-Nghi-Son-1-bao-dam-moi-truong-trong-dot-dai-tu--1-3575.aspx Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 1 bảo đảm môi trường trong đợt đại tu], Công ty Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn, November 14, 2025</ref>

===Financing for Nghi Sơn-1===
In March 2007, the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) agreed to provide a US$772 million loan to the project.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://sekitan.jp/jbic/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/List-of-Coal-Power-Investments-by-JBIC-NEXI-JICA_0718.pdf|title=List of Coal Power Plants funded by JBIC, NEXI and JICA (2003-2019)|last=|first=|date=2019|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> JICA provided two additional loans in 2011, one for approximately US$361 million<ref name = jica1>[http://web.archive.org/web/20201024180611/https://www.jica.go.jp/english/news/press/2010/110124.html Japanese ODA Loan Signed with Vietnam], Japan International Cooperation Agency, Jan. 24, 2011, Archived Oct. 24, 2020</ref> and the other for approximately US$516 million.<ref name = jica2>[http://web.archive.org/web/20201224230714/https://www.jica.go.jp/english/news/press/2011/111102.html Signing of Japanese ODA Loan with the Socialist Republic of Vietnam], Japan International Cooperation Agency, November 2, 2011, Archived Dec. 24, 2020</ref>

===Nghi Sơn-2===
In March 2013, the Vietnamese Ministry of Industry and Trade awarded a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract for the 1,320 MW gross (1,200-MW net) [[Nghi Son 2 power station|Nghi Sơn-2 coal-fired power plant]] to a consortium consisting of [[Marubeni Corporation]] and [[Korea Electric Power Company]] (KEPCO).<ref>[http://www.moit.gov.vn/en/News/225/ministry-of-industry-and-trade-awards-nghi-son-2-thermal-power-plant--contract-to-marubeni--kepco-consortium.aspx Ministry of Industry and Trade Awards Nghi Son 2 Thermal Power Plant Contract to Marubeni – KEPCO Consortium], Vietnam Ministry of Industry & Trade website, March 25, 2013.</ref> The plant is scheduled to come online in 2018; the two companies will then own and operate the plant for 25 years, after which ownership will revert to [[Electricity of Vietnam]].<ref>[http://www.marubeni.com/news/2013/release/00011.html Receipt of Notification of Award for Vietnam, Nghi Son 2 Coal-Fired Power Project], Marubeni Corporation press release, March 25, 2013.</ref>

In August 2014, the project's developers and provincial authorities pushed to accelerate the plant's development process, in order to ensure that it would be able to be built on schedule. At that time, some financial, and contract details were still outstanding.<ref>[http://baodautu.vn/day-nhanh-tien-do-du-an-nhiet-dien-nghi-son-2.html-21448 Đẩy nhanh tiến độ Dự án Nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 2], Báo Đầu tư, 23 Aug. 2014.</ref> As of April 2015, construction was expected to begin in August.<ref>[http://truyenhinhthanhhoa.vn/web/trang-chu/tin-tuc-su-kien/chinh-tri/dong-chi-le-hong-anh-uy-vien-bo-chinh-tri-thuong-truc-ban-bi-thu-tham-khu-kinh-te-nghi-son.html Đồng chí Lê Hồng Anh, Ủy viên Bộ Chính trị, Thường trực Ban bí thư thăm khu kinh tế Nghi Sơn], TTV, 9 Apr. 2015.</ref>

Land clearing began on the project in September 2015.<ref>[https://www.talkvietnam.com/2015/09/construction-starts-at-nghi-son-2-coal-fired-power-plant/ "Construction starts at Nghi Son 2 coal-fired power plant,"] Talk Vietnam, September 18, 2015</ref> The project did not begin actual construction at that date, however, as the project was still being negotiated.

In November 2016, Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade approved a new build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract by Marubeni and KEPCO. The project would cost US$2.3 billion, with 50% coming from the two companies and 50% from a consortium of banks. Unit 1 was scheduled to come online by Sept. 2019, and Unit 2 by March 2020.<ref>[http://vietnamfinance.vn/thi-truong/marubeni-bat-tay-kepco-lam-nhiet-dien-nghi-son-2-tri-gia-23-ty-usd-20161108171537404.htm Marubeni bắt tay KEPCO làm nhiệt điện Nghi Sơn 2 trị giá 2,3 tỷ USD], VietNam Finance, 8 Nov. 2016.</ref>

In November 2017, KEPCO finalized the US$2.3 billion (2.56 trillion won) contract with Electricity of Vietnam (EVN). KEPCO said it will break ground this year and complete the project in 2021. Once completed, KEPCO will operate it for 25 years before transferring it to the Vietnamese.<ref>[http://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/nation/2017/11/693_239011.html "KEPCO to build coal-fired power plant in Vietnam,"] Biz and Tech, Nov 9, 2017</ref>

In July 2018, Doosan Heavy Industries & Construction Co. said it had commenced the delayed construction on the plant after it received an advanced payment of US$170 million for the US$1.6 billion deal it secured in 2014. The plant is planned for operation in 2022.<ref>[https://pulsenews.co.kr/view.php?year=2018&no=469625 "Doosan Heavy Industries begins construction of thermal power plant in Vietnam,"] Pulse News, 2018.07.26</ref>

[https://www.planet.com/stories/nghi-son-power-station-YgLXr6wmg Planet satellite photos] show physical construction began in late 2018.

In February 2020, the National Steering Committee on power development reported that construction was 52.35% complete and that Unit 1 was scheduled to be commissioned in February 2022 and Unit 2 in August 2022.<ref name="vl">[http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/tinh-hinh-thuc-hien-cac-du-an-dien-theo-hinh-thuc-bot-o-viet-nam.html Tình hình thực hiện các dự án điện theo hình thức BOT ở Việt Nam], Feb. 14, 2020</ref> Unit 1 was commissioned in March 2022.<ref>[https://en.vietnamplus.vn/thanh-hoa-province-wants-to-enhance-cooperation-with-korean-partners/224090.vnp Thanh Hoa province wants to enhance cooperation with Korean partners], Vietnam Plus, Mar. 25, 2022</ref>

As of July 2022, Nghi Sơn-2 appeared to be at a full 1,200 MW capacity.<ref>[https://ns2pc.com/ Nghi Son 2 Power Thermal Plant], NS2PC, accessed July 25, 2022</ref><ref>[https://kemlu.go.id/hanoi/en/news/19727/ambassador-denny-abdi-visited-nghi-son-2-power-thermal-plant Ambassador Denny Abdi visited Nghi Son 2 Power Thermal Plant], Ministry of Foreign Affairs Republic of Indonesia, accessed June 18, 2022</ref> On Aug. 28, 2022, an official inauguration and commissioning ceremony for the plant was held.<ref>[https://nangluongvietnam.vn/khanh-thanh-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-nghi-son-2-29330.html Khánh thành Nhà máy Nhiệt điện BOT Nghi Sơn 2], Nang Luong Vietnam, Aug. 28, 2022</ref>

In September 2025, Vietnam’s Ministry of Finance proposed exempting the foreign owners of seven coal power plants from the requirement to pay a 15% global minimum corporate tax rate set by the OECD. The list of coal plants, which were developed under “build-operate-transfer” (BOT) contracts, included [https://www.gem.wiki/Mong_Duong_power_station Mông Dương-2], [https://www.gem.wiki/Vinh_Tan_power_station Vĩnh Tân-1], Nghi Sơn-2, [https://www.gem.wiki/Van_Phong_power_station Vân Phong-1], [https://www.gem.wiki/Vung_Ang_power_station Vũng Áng-2], [[Hai Duong Thermal Power Plant]], and [https://www.gem.wiki/Duyen_Hai_Power_Generation_Complex Duyên Hải-2].<ref>[https://vneconomy.vn/de-xuat-mien-tru-thue-toi-thieu-toan-cau-cho-du-an-bot-dien-co-bao-lanh-chinh-phu.htm “Đề xuất miễn trừ thuế tối thiểu toàn cầu cho dự án BOT điện có bảo lãnh Chính phủ,”] VnEconomy, September 11, 2025</ref> The Ministry argued that imposing the 15% minimum tax could trigger compensation obligations that “would expose the Vietnamese government to the risk of having to pay compensation that exceeds the tax revenues.”<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/vietnam-exempt-mitsubishi-kepco-other-coal-power-plant-operators-global-tax-2025-09-12/ “Vietnam to exempt Mitsubishi, Kepco, other coal power plant operators from global tax, document shows,”] Reuters, September 11, 2025</ref>

In June 2026, the Deputy General Director of Nghi Sơn-2 stated that the company was evaluating the potential future use of ammonia and biomass co-firing and carbon capture at the power station.<ref>[https://baothanhhoa.vn/nghi-son-truoc-co-hoi-hinh-thanh-trung-tam-nang-luong-quoc-gia-289861.htm Nghi Sơn trước cơ hội hình thành trung tâm năng lượng quốc gia], Báo Thanh Hóa, June 4, 2026</ref>

===Financing for Nghi Sơn-2===
In April 2018, the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) agreed to provide US$560 million in loan funding for the 1200 MW Nghi Son 2 plant in Vietnam.<ref>[https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2018/0413-010921.html "Project Finance and Political Risk Guarantee for Nghi Son 2 Coal-Fired Power Generation Project in the Republic of Vietnam,"] JBIC, Apr 13, 2018</ref> The Export-Import Bank of Korea is also providing US$560 million, while a coalition of banks from Japan, Singapore, and Malaysia, comprising DBS Bank, Mizuho Bank, Maybank, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, OCBC Bank, Shinsei Bank, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, are providing the remaining US$747.86 million.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/28855/nghi-son-2-coal-fired-power-plant-1200mw-ipp|title=Preview of Nghi Son 2 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1200MW) IPP {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-09-23}}</ref> Malaysia's Maybank agreed to finance the project in April 2018 after the withdrawal that month of Standard Chartered.<ref>Robin Hicks, [https://www.eco-business.com/news/1200-megawatt-vietnam-coal-plant-gets-funding-but-standard-chartered-pulls-out-over-climate-policy-conflict/ 1,200 megawatt Vietnam coal plant gets funding, but Standard Chartered pulls out over climate policy conflict], Eco-Business, Apr. 19, 2018</ref> Marubeni and KEPCO are providing US$432 million in equity to the project. Construction of the plant was complete and test operations were occurring in December 2021.<ref>[https://laodong-vn.translate.goog/kinh-te/nhiet-dien-nghi-son-2-hoan-thanh-dot-than-thanh-cong-to-may-so-2-985268.ldo?_x_tr_sl=vi&_x_tr_tl=en&_x_tr_hl=en&_x_tr_pto=sc Nghi Son 2 Thermal Power Plant successfully completed the coal burning of Unit 2], Lao Dong, Dec. 16, 2021</ref>

In July 2025, insurance company Chubb, one of the world’s largest insurers, backtracked on its climate policy and became the lead insurer for Nghi Sơn-2 Power. In 2019, Chubb released a climate policy that ruled out providing insurance cover for companies generating more than 30% of their energy from coal. The March 2025 version of the policy ruled out providing coverage for the construction and operation of coal plants and stated that it “began phasing out coverage of existing risks exceeding this [30%] threshold at the start of 2022 (accounting for the viability of alternative energy sources in the impacted region)”.<ref>[https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2025-07-23/us-insurer-chubb-breaks-climate-promise-to-back-coal-plant “US insurer Chubb breaks climate promise to back coal plant,”] The Bureau of Investigative Journalism, July 23, 2025</ref><ref>[https://about.chubb.com/content/dam/chubb-sites/chubb/about-chubb/citizenship/environment/pdf/chubb-corporate-climate-underwriting-criteria-for-high-emitting-industries.pdf “Chubb’s Corporate Climate Underwriting Criteria Summary,”] Chubb, March 2025</ref>

==Opposition==

On November 15, 2017, Japanese environmentalists released a statement opposing the Japanese and South Korean support for the Vietnamese Nghi Son power plant. They opposed for reasons of inefficient technology, air pollution, and premature deaths. The environmentalists included Friends of the Earth Japan, Kiko Network, Mekong Watch, and more.<ref>[https://www.foejapan.org/en/aid/171115.html “No Coal! Go Green!”], Friends of the Earth Japan, November 15, 2017.</ref>

In response to the financial support of the Nghi Son power plant by the Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc. (SMFG), environmental NGOs, such as 350.org Japan, Greenpeace Japan, and more, opposed their financial investments with a public statement. They identified the coal plant as having environmental and social risk, and urged SMFG to diverge its funding for the plan.<ref>[https://www.banktrack.org/article/environmental_ngos_respond_to_statement_by_sumitomo_mitsui_financial_group_ceo_on_restricting_coalfired_power_financing “Environmental NGOs respond to statement by Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group CEO on restricting coal fired power financing”], Banktrack, 2018.</ref> In March 2018, environmental groups also wrote a petition urging the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) to stop its financial investments into the Nghi Son power plant. They cited reasons such as the plant was not compatible with the Paris Agreement, the technology for the plant is against Japanese Government policy, and the plant would worsen Vietnamese air pollution.<ref>[https://www.foejapan.org/en/aid/pdf/180313.pdf “Urgent Petition”], Friends of Earth Japan, March 13, 2018.</ref> There were 61 groups from 23 countries that supported the revocation of JBIC’s finances in the Nghi Son power plant project.<ref>[https://www.foejapan.org/en/aid/180427.html “Press Release”], Friends of Earth Japan, April 27, 2018.</ref>

In May 2019, human rights issues about the Nghi Son power plant were brought to attention by environmentalist groups. Specifically, Nghi Son power plant was allegedly approved with no consultation from the project-affected communities. According to the Vietnamese community organizations, the residents’ resettlement has been “unsatisfactory.”<ref>[https://urgewald.org/sites/default/files/Talanx.pdf “Talanx: Seriously Clearing Up or Silently Continuing Support for Coal?”], Urgewald, May 2019.</ref>
In October 2019, the Renewable Energy Institute released a report around the benefits of replacing coal power with renewable energy. Problems around health and environment from coal plants, including the Nghi Son power plant, were discussed.<ref>[https://www.renewable-ei.org/pdfdownload/activities/SoutheastAsiaPowerReport_EN.pdf “Renewable Energy to Replace Coal Power in Southeast Asia”], Renewable Energy Institute, October 2019.</ref>

==Background==

The power station comprises four power plants. The O Mon 1 plant, which has a capacity of 660 MW, is already operational. O Mon 2, 3, and 4 are proposed.

O Mon I currently relies on fuel oil but will be switched to domestic natural gas in 2021.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thesaigontimes.vn/164876/nhiet-dien-o-mon-i-se-chuyen-sang-chay-khi.html|title=Nhiệt điện Ô Môn I sẽ chuyển sang chạy khí|last=|first=|date=September 21, 2017|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> The February 2021 draft PDP8 revised that year to 2024.<ref name='draftPDP8'>[https://moit.gov.vn/upload/2005517/20210707/du-thao-dien-viii35c6.rar Draft National Power Development Plan for the period of 2021-2030, with a vision to 2045], Vietnamese Ministry of Ministry of Industry and Trade, February 2021</ref>

In May 2019, ''VietnamNet'' reported that EVN was having difficulty arranging capital for this project.<ref name='vn'>Hà Duy, [https://vietnamnet.vn/vn/kinh-doanh/dau-tu/bo-cong-thuong-muon-giao-nhiet-dien-o-mon-2-cho-tu-nhan-lam-535091.html Nhiệt điện 26 ngàn tỷ: Chê quốc doanh yếu tiền, Bộ chuyển tư nhân làm], ''VietnamNet'', 29 May 2019</ref>

The power station has three proposed gas-burning combined cycle units totaling 3,150 MW, and the fuel-oil units are scheduled to be switched to natural gas, which would ultimately bring the total gas-fired capacity to 3,810 MW.

==O Mon 2==

O Mon 2 is a proposed 1,050-megawatt (MW) gas-fired power plant. It will be built in the O Mon Power Center alongside O Mon 1 Thermal Power Plant and the proposed O Mon 3 and O Mon 4 power stations.<ref name=sum>Thứ Ba, [http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/nhiet-dien-o-mon-1-se-chuyen-sang-chay-khi-thay-dau-fo.html Nhiệt điện Ô Môn 1 sẽ chuyển sang chạy khí thay dầu FO], ''Vietnam Energy Magazine'', 22 Sep 2017</ref><ref name=dau>Thanh Hương, [https://baodautu.vn/bo-cong-thuong-lung-tung-khi-duoc-giao-chi-dinh-chu-dau-tu-du-an-nhiet-dien-o-mon-ii-d108665.html Bộ Công thương lúng túng khi được giao chỉ định chủ đầu tư Dự án Nhiệt điện Ô Môn II], ''Đầu tư online'', 8 Oct 2019</ref>

Two investors sent proposals to the Ministry of Industry and Trade -- EVNGENCO2 (Vietnam Electricity Corporation) and Vietracimex (Marubeni Corporation) to build the power plant. In May 2019, Ministry of Industry and Trade recommended Vietracimex Joint Venture - Marubeni Group, which had begun operating many projects successfully in 2019, to the Prime Minister.<ref name=mon2>[https://baodauthau.vn/dau-tu/du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-o-mon-ii-nha-dau-tu-nao-lot-mat-xanh-bo-cong-thuong-96897.html Dự án Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Ô Môn II: Nhà đầu tư nào “lọt mắt xanh” Bộ Công Thương?], ''Báo Đấu Thầu'', 3 May 2019</ref><ref>[https://thoidai.com.vn/vi-sao-vietracimex-duoc-tien-cu-cho-du-an-khung-nhiet-dien-o-mon-ii-78041.html Vì sao Vietracimex được tiến cử cho dự án khủng Nhiệt điện Ô Môn II?], ''Vietnam Times'', 24 May 2019</ref>

In mid-2019, the Prime Minister and Ministry of Trade discussed increasing the output of the plant from 750 MW to 1,050 MW and having it begin operations in 2025.<ref name=dau>Thanh Hương, [https://baodautu.vn/bo-cong-thuong-lung-tung-khi-duoc-giao-chi-dinh-chu-dau-tu-du-an-nhiet-dien-o-mon-ii-d108665.html Bộ Công thương lúng túng khi được giao chỉ định chủ đầu tư Dự án Nhiệt điện Ô Môn II], ''Đầu tư online'', 8 Oct 2019</ref><ref>Vĩnh Chi, [https://vietnamfinance.vn/du-an-nhiet-dien-o-mon-ii-bo-cong-thuong-che-evngenco2-yeu-nang-luc-tai-chinh-20180504224223635.htm Dự án Nhiệt điện Ô Môn II: Bộ Công Thương chê EVNGENCO2 yếu năng lực tài chính], ''Vietnam Finance'', 15 May 2019</ref>

In February 2021, ''IJGlobal'' reported that Vietracimex and Marubeni had received approval to proceed with the project following a decision by Vietnam's prime minister Nguyen Xuan Phuc in January 2021 backing the investment planning for the project.<ref>[https://baodautu.vn/vay-24448-ty-dong-dau-tu-du-an-nhiet-dien-o-mon-ii-d136037.html Vay 24.448 tỷ đồng đầu tư Dự án Nhiệt điện Ô Môn II], Dautu Online, Jan 5, 2021</ref> The output of the project was confirmed as 1,050 MW and the companies are expecting the plant to commence operations in 2024-2025. The total project cost is about 30.56 trillion Vietnamese dong (US$1.33 billion). The Vietracimex - Marubeni consortium is planning to raise equity of approximately 6.11 trillion Vietnamese dong and finance the remaining 24.45 trillion Vietnamese dong with commercial loans.<ref name=IJG>Civi Yap, [https://ijglobal.com/articles/153133/vietracimex-and-marubeni-to-build-gas-fired Vietracimex and Marubeni to build gas-fired], IJGlobal, Feb. 11, 2021</ref>

As of the February 2021 draft PDP8, O Mon 2 has established a feasibility study.<ref name='draftPDP8'>[https://moit.gov.vn/upload/2005517/20210707/du-thao-dien-viii35c6.rar Draft National Power Development Plan for the period of 2021-2030, with a vision to 2045], Vietnamese Ministry of Ministry of Industry and Trade, February 2021</ref>

In May 2025, it was reported that a Maurbeni-led team was sounding out banks and export credit agencies to raise approximately US$800 million in loans for O Mon 2, with the aim of finalising the finance deals in 2026.<ref name=proximo>Max Thompson, [https://www.proximoinfra.com/news/70425/O-Mon-2-CCGT-out-to-banks O Mon 2 CCGT out to banks], Proximo, May 12, 2025</ref>

==O Mon 3==

O Mon 3 is a proposed 1,050-megawatt (MW) gas-fired power plant in Can Tho Province, Vietnam.<ref name=sum>Thứ Ba, [http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/nhiet-dien-o-mon-1-se-chuyen-sang-chay-khi-thay-dau-fo.html Nhiệt điện Ô Môn 1 sẽ chuyển sang chạy khí thay dầu FO], ''Vietnam Energy Magazine'', 22 Sep 2017</ref><ref name=jp>[https://www.meti.go.jp/meti_lib/report/H30FY/000209.pdf Study on Gas to Power Project Value Chain in the South Vietnam Final Report, p. 6-45], Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry website, March 2019</ref><ref name=raise>[https://vietnamnet.vn/vn/kinh-doanh/dau-tu/lo-gia-dien-tang-khi-dau-tu-nhiet-dien-o-mon-iii-va-o-mon-iv-456123.html Xây 2 nhiệt điện 50.000 tỷ đồng: Thận trọng những thách thức], ''VietnamNet'', 13 Jun 2018</ref>

As of the February 2021 draft PDP8, O Mon 3 is in loan negotiations.<ref name='draftPDP8'>[https://moit.gov.vn/upload/2005517/20210707/du-thao-dien-viii35c6.rar Draft National Power Development Plan for the period of 2021-2030, with a vision to 2045], Vietnamese Ministry of Ministry of Industry and Trade, February 2021</ref> The project is believed to have received US$432 million in equity from former owner EVN, and to be seeking development bank loans in the amount of US$668 million.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://vir.com.vn/petrovietnam-invests-in-o-mon-iii-and-iv-thermal-power-plants-105858.html&link=autochanger|title=PetroVietnam invests in O Mon III and IV thermal power plants|last=VIR|first=Vietnam Investment Review -|date=2023-10-10|work=Vietnam Investment Review - VIR|access-date=2025-09-16|language=en-US}}</ref>

==O Mon 4==

O Mon 4 is a proposed 1,050-megawatt (MW) gas-fired power plant.<ref name=sum>Thứ Ba, [http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/nhiet-dien-o-mon-1-se-chuyen-sang-chay-khi-thay-dau-fo.html Nhiệt điện Ô Môn 1 sẽ chuyển sang chạy khí thay dầu FO], ''Vietnam Energy Magazine'', 22 Sep 2017</ref><ref name=jp>[https://www.meti.go.jp/meti_lib/report/H30FY/000209.pdf Study on Gas to Power Project Value Chain in the South Vietnam Final Report, p. 6-45], Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry website, March 2019</ref><ref name=raise>[https://vietnamnet.vn/vn/kinh-doanh/dau-tu/lo-gia-dien-tang-khi-dau-tu-nhiet-dien-o-mon-iii-va-o-mon-iv-456123.html Xây 2 nhiệt điện 50.000 tỷ đồng: Thận trọng những thách thức], ''VietnamNet'', 13 Jun 2018</ref>

In 2011, following an extensive due diligence, project design, and public consultation period over several years, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved a loan totaling US$309.89 million for O Mon 4. The ADB's project cost figure of US$423.45 million for O Mon 4 dates back to 2011.<ref name=ADB>[https://www.adb.org/projects/43400-013/main Viet Nam : O Mon IV Combined Cycle Power Plant Project], Asian Development bank website, accessed May 12, 2025</ref>

In September 2019, the People's Committee of Can Tho City requested comments on the feasibility study report of O Mon IV Thermal Power Plant project from the State Capital Management Committee.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nksyGwRRhQ Cần Thơ kiến nghị phê duyệt Nhà máy nhiệt điện Ô Môn IV], ''THTPCT Can Tho Television'', 25 Sep 2019</ref>

In June 2025, South Korea's Doosan Enerbility and Vietnam's Power Engineering Consulting Joint Stock Company 2 (PECC2) signed, as a consortium, an engineering, procurement, and construction contract for O Mon 4. Doosan announced that the contract was worth approximately 900 billion won (about US$770 million), with the consortium responsible for main plant equipment supply, construction, and overall commissioning.<ref>Lee Jun-sung, [https://www.koreaittimes.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=142191 Doosan Enerbility Expands Global Gas-Fired Power Plant Construction Orders], Korea IT Times, Jun. 10, 2025</ref>

==Background==

Ordos Power Qipanjing power station is a ten-unit coal-fired power plant totaling 1,960 MW in Mengxi Town. It was commissioned from 2005 to 2013, and is owned by Ordos Share Holding Group.<ref name=ordos>[http://www.epjob88.com/vvip/e17510/ "鄂尔多斯电力（集团）有限责任公司企业简介,"] Ordos Share Holding Group, accessed Jan 2018</ref>

An additional 2 x 600 MW may have been considered at the site,<ref name=imnu>[http://jy.imnu.edu.cn/index.php?a=article&aid=993 "鄂尔多斯双欣电力有限公司招聘启事,"] Inner Mongolia Normal University, 2015-06-12</ref><ref>[http://www.mengxi.gov.cn/v.asp?unid=3727 "内蒙古双欣能源化工有限公司2×350MW低热值煤 发电工程环境影响评价公众参与第二次公示,"] 蒙西工业园区管委会 作者, 2015/7/31</ref><ref>[http://www.gczb.com/xmxx/xmdt/2015/09/0115295616690.html "棋盘井自备电厂二期扩建工程获核准,"] 2015-09-01</ref><ref>[http://www.epjob88.com/vvip/e17510/ "鄂尔多斯电力（集团）有限责任公司企业简介,"] Erdos, accessed September 2015</ref> but were presumed cancelled. Due to new restrictions announced during 2016 by the National Energy Administration and the National Development and Reform Commission, further capacity expansions at the location appeared to be on hold or cancelled. For details, see [[China's 2016 Restrictions on Development of Coal-Fired Power Capacity]].

==Background==

Construction for the Ordos Resources Qipanjing power station began in April 2013, with the plants beginning operation in 2015. The sponsoring company, Ordos High-Tech & New Material, was initially planning to build 4 units of 330,000 kilowatts. ==Background==

The 1,760MW gas-fired power plant is estimated to have cost US$1.4 billion out of a total investment of approximately US$1.8 billion that also includes the development and construction of the associated [[Jawa Satu FSRU]], an LNG import terminal that started operating in 2021.<ref name="NSEnergy">BV Swagath, [https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/news/pertamina-jawa-1-power-project/ Pertamina closes financing for $1.8bn Jawa 1 gas-to-power project], NS Energy, Dec. 10, 2018</ref>

A total debt financing package of US$1.312 billion for both the power plant and the FSRU reached financial close in December 2018. This comprised, from state-backed financial institutions, a US$604 million loan from Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), a US$185 million loan from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), and a US$120 million loan from Leading Asia's Private Infrastructure Fund (LEAP).<ref>[https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2018/1022-011485.html Project Financing for Jawa 1 Gas-to-Power Project in Indonesia], Japan Bank for International Cooperation press release, Oct. 22, 2018</ref><ref>[https://www.adb.org/projects/51112-001/main Indonesia : Jawa-1 Liquefied Natural Gas-to-Power Project], Asian Development Bank Project Data Sheet, last updated Dec. 9, 2024</ref> Five commercial banks contributed a US$403 million loan, a finance package covered by Nippon Export and Investment Insurance. The commercial banks are Mizuho, MUFG, Oversea Chinese Banking Corporation, Société Générale, and Crédit Agricole.<ref name="NSEnergy" /><ref>[https://equator-principles.com/report/credit-agricole-corporate-and-investment-bank-2019/ CRÉDIT AGRICOLE CORPORATE AND INVESTMENT BANK (2019)], Equator Principles EPFIs and reporting, accessed May 28, 2025</ref> The PT Jawa Satu Power special purpose vehicle comprising PT Pertamina (Persero), Marubeni, and Sojitz made an equity investment of US$463 million.<ref>[https://www.ijglobal.com/data/transaction/33879 Java 1 FSRU & CCGT Power Plant (1760MW) IPP], IJGlobal Transaction Data, last updated Sep. 2, 2024</ref>

==Financing==

*'''Source of financing:''' 70% bank loans; 30% equity<ref name=TEAM>[http://bit.ly/1mmGkmy "Pagbilao plant to add 400MW capacity,"] Rappler, September 29, 2013</ref>: Banco De Oro (BDO), Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), China Bank, First Metro Investment Corporation (FIC), PNB Capital, Philippine Savings Bank (PSB), and SB Capital Investment Corporation (SBC) (US$750 million total);<ref>[https://www.power-technology.com/projects/pagbilao-power-plant-expansion/ "Pagbilao Power Plant Expansion,"] Power Technology, accessed May 2018</ref> US$250 million in equity from Aboitiz Power Corp, Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO), and Marubeni<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/30749/pagbilao-coal-fired-power-plant-expansion-1135mw|title=Preview of Pagbilao Coal-Fired Power Plant Expansion (1135MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-12-01}}</ref>

==Background==

The two-unit, 735-MW Pagbilao coal-fired power plant was completed in 1996. The plant is operated by Team Energy, a joint venture of Japanese companies [[Tokyo Electric Power Company]] and Marubeni Corporation.<Ref>[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/41686 Pagbilao Coal Power Plant Philippines,] Global Energy Observatory, accessed May 2012</ref><ref>[http://www.edf.org/documents/9584_coal-plants-spreadsheet.xls "Coal-Fired Plants Financed by International Public Investment Institutions Since 1994"], Appendix to ''Foreclosing the Future: Coal, Climate and International Public Finance: Investment in coal-fired power plants hinders the fight against global warming'', Environmental Defense, April 2009.</ref> The plant is owned by Aboitiz Power, who took over the plant in 2009.<ref>[https://aboitizpower.com/about-us/our-businesses/power-generation/thermal/therma-luzon-inc Discover How Therma Luzon, Inc. Helps Power A Better Future], Aboitiz Power, Accessed: April 19, 2024</ref>
 
===Unit 3 Expansion===
In March 2012, Team Energy and the Aboitiz Group announced that they would partner on an additional 420-MW coal-fired unit at Pagbilao. The unit would run on lower-quality Philippine or Indonesian coal.<ref name=aksyon>Añonuevo, Euan. [http://www.interaksyon.com/business/28201/team-energy-aboitiz-power-to-expand-pagbilao-plant-capacity Team Energy, Aboitiz Power to expand Pagbilao plant capacity]. InterAksyon, 30 Mar. 2012.</ref> In 2013, Team Energy announced that Marubeni, one of its two owners, would handle engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC).<ref name=TEAM>[http://bit.ly/1mmGkmy "Pagbilao plant to add 400MW capacity,"] Rappler, September 29, 2013</ref>

Environmental permits were issued in June 2013.<ref name=DOE>[http://www.doe.gov.ph/doe_files/pdf/01_Energy_Situationer/2014-Private-Sector-Initiated-Power-Projects-Luzon%20Committed-September-30.pdf Private Sector Initiated Power Projects (Luzon)], Philippines Department of Energy, 30 Sept. 2014.</ref> In June 2014, the plant's owners announced that Japan's Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems and Korea's Daelim Industrial would be constructing the plant.<ref>[http://www.power-technology.com/news/newsmhps-wins-coal-fired-power-plant-construction-contract-from-pagbilao-energy-4283582 MHPS wins coal-fired power plant construction contract from Pagbilao Energy], power-technology.com, 3 June 2014.</ref> In June 2014, First Gen, a subsidiary of First Philippine Holdings Corporation, announced that it was considering buying a stake in the project.<ref>[http://www.miningconnection.com/coal_prep/news/article/first_gen_eyes_stake_in_pagbilao_coal-fired_power_plant_in_quezon_phillipin/ First Gen Eyes Stake in Pagbilao Coal-fired Power Plant in Quezon, Philippines], ''Mining Connection'', 11 June 2014.</ref> Ground was broken on the project in July 2014.<ref name=DOE>[http://www.doe.gov.ph/doe_files/pdf/01_Energy_Situationer/2014-Private-Sector-Initiated-Power-Projects-Luzon%20Committed-September-30.pdf Private Sector Initiated Power Projects (Luzon)], Philippines Department of Energy, 30 Sept. 2014.</ref> Total cost of the project will be $976 million, and the plant is expected to be completed in Q2 2017.<ref name=MSN>[http://www.msn.com/en-ph/news/other/pagbilao-expansion-to-cost-nearly-1b/ar-BB3cNiK Pagbilao expansion to cost nearly $1B], MSN News, 11 Sept. 2014.</ref> 

In September 2017, Aboitiz announced that the plant had been tested up to its 420 MW capacity and that it would begin commercial operations by the end of the year.<ref>[http://thestandard.com.ph/business/power-technology/247181/pagbilao-coal-plant-tests-full-capacity.html Pagbilao coal plant tests full capacity], ''Manila Standard'', 17 Sep 2017.</ref>

In January 2018 it was reported Unit 3 was still in the testing phase, and would begin operations in February 2018.<ref>[http://manilastandard.net/business/power-technology/255379/pagbilao-energy-set-to-operate-1-b-coal-fired-power-plant-in-february.html "Pagbilao Energy set to operate $1-b coal-fired power plant in February,"] Manila Standard, January 02, 2018</ref> On February 27, 2018, the Pagbilao council issued a cease-and-desist order (CDO) against Unit 3 because its owners had not signed a memorandum of understanding on corporate social responsibility (CSR) which, according to Aboitiz, would have required expenditures of "an amount above the company’s approved budget for CSR."<ref>[https://www.doe.gov.ph/energist/pagbilao-gets-court-reprieve-proceed-power-plant PAGBILAO GETS COURT REPRIEVE TO PROCEED WITH POWER PLANT], Department of Energy, Mar. 21, 2018</ref> The Pagbilao council lifted the CDO on March 7, 2018, and Unit 3 went into commercial operation.<ref>[http://powerlinks.news/article/667932/pagbilao-thermal-power-plant-starts-commercial-operations?fieldname=industryids&t=Power&query=&fieldvalue=42 Philippines’ Pagbilao Coal-fired Thermal Power Plant Starts Commercial Operations], Power Links, Mar. 15, 2018</ref>

===Financing for Unit 3===
In June 2014, a financing agreement for Unit 3 was closed. US$760.13 million in loans was provided by BDO Unibank, BPI Capital Corporation, First Metro Investment Corporation (FMIC), SB Capital Investment, Philippine National Bank, China Banking Corporation, and Security Bank. US$250 million in equity was provided by Aboitiz Power Corp, Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO), and Marubeni. ING Group acted as financial adviser to the sponsors.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/30749/pagbilao-coal-fired-power-plant-expansion-1135mw|title=Preview of Pagbilao Coal-Fired Power Plant Expansion (1135MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-12-01}}</ref>

===Possible LNG Addition===
In the DOE's March 2023 list of Indicative Power Projects, a 1,310 MW gas-fired power plant was listed by Therma Subic Inc. as "Pagbilao 4 & 5 CCGT Power Plant" with an expected commission date of July 2028.<ref>[https://www.doe.gov.ph/sites/default/files/pdf/electric_power/06_Luzon%20Indicative%20-%202023-03-31.pdf?withshield=1 "LUZON INDICATIVE POWER PROJECTS,"] Department of Energy, March 31, 2023</ref>
It was reported in May 2023 that AboitizPower was planning the LNG project in Pagbilao "to meet base load requirement[s] by 2028 to 2030" <ref>[https://www.manilatimes.net/2023/05/09/business/top-business/traditional-power-plants-still-needed/1890539 "Traditional power plants still needed,"] The Manila Times, May 9, 2023</ref>

In June 2026, LNG equipment originally intended for the Pagbilao power station addition was reportedly sold to the US-based Hallador Energy company.<ref>[https://ieefa.org/resources/gas-turbine-sale-signals-end-another-philippine-lng-project "Gas turbine sale signals the end of another Philippine LNG project,"] Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis, June 10, 2026</ref>

===Testing ammonia co-firing===
In June 2023, Aboitiz Power announced that in the following year, the company would study the potential of co-firing its coal plants with ammonia "possibly in collaboration" with the major Japanese utility JERA. Pagbilao power station was reportedly chosen as the candidate-facility for testing.<ref>[https://mb.com.ph/2023/6/29/aboitiz-power-to-study-ammonia-co-firing-by-next-year "Aboitiz Power to study ammonia co-firing by next year,"] Manila Bulletin, June 29, 2023</ref>

==Ownership==

In July 2024, reporting stated that TeaM Energy's Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) contracts at the Sual and Pagbilao power stations would expire in 2024 and 2025, respectively, as TeaM Energy partners Marubeni Corporation and JERA would move their sights toward renewable energy projects.<ref>[https://powerphilippines.com/marubeni-philippines-to-consider-re-as-coal-contracts-expire/ Marubeni Philippines to consider RE as coal contracts expire], Power Philippines, July 3, 2024</ref><ref>[https://www.bworldonline.com/corporate/2024/07/03/605697/marubeni-phl-shifts-focus-to-re-as-coal-contracts-near-end/ Marubeni PHL shifts focus to RE as coal contracts near end], Business World, July 3, 2024</ref> Ownership and control of the two coal plants would be transferred to Aboitiz Power and the San Miguel Corporation.

In July 2025, Marubeni Corp announced its intension to divest from Pagbilao-3.<ref>[https://mb.com.ph/2025/07/30/japanese-partner-marubeni-divesting-stake-in-pagbilao-3-plant Japanese partner Marubeni divesting stake in Pagbilao-3 plant], Manila Bulletin, July 30, 2025</ref>

In August 2025, the ownwership transfer of Units 1 and 2 from TeaM Energy to Aboitiz Power was official. TeaM Energy maintained its 50% stake in Unit 3.<ref>[https://mb.com.ph/2025/08/15/aboitizpower-unit-takes-over-pagbilao-plant-as-team-energys-contract-ends AboitizPower unit takes over Pagbilao plant as TeaM Energy's contract ends], Manila Bulletin, August 15, 2025</ref>

==Tropical Storm Paeng==

In October 2022, 4 million residents were left without power when tropical storm Paeng shut down [https://www.gem.wiki/Bac-Man_geothermal_power_plant Bacman geothermal power plant], [https://www.gem.wiki/Quezon_power_station#460_MW_Expansion Quezon power station] and Pagbilao power station. At the Pagbilao power station, two out of three units went offline temporarily.<ref>[https://manilastandard.net/news/314274196/3-power-plants-shut-4-million-meralco-clients-without-power-amid-storm.html "3 power plants shut, 4 million Meralco clients without power amid storm"], Manila Standard, October 31, 2022.</ref>

==Outages and impact on grid==

In May 2024, an analysis by the Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development found that coal- and gas-fired power plants were the leading cause of blackouts in the Philippines between 2019 and 2023. Over half of the forced outages in that time period were attributable to coal plants. Of the eight most unreliable plants, six were coal plants: [[Calaca power station]], [https://www.gem.wiki/Quezon_power_station San Buenaventura power station], [[Masinloc power station]], [[Limay power station]], [[Panay power station]], and Pagbilao power station. These power stations each had at least 10 incidents of forced outages. The amount of outages was not consistent with age; Masinloc power station Unit 3, which had only been operating for three years, was reportedly offline for 118 days.<ref>[https://ceedphilippines.com/cant-take-the-heat-report/ Can’t Take The Heat?: Examining the Philippines’ Perennial Power Outages Problem caused by Fossil Fuels], Center for Energy, Ecology, and Development, May 13, 2024</ref>

==Paiton power complex==

Paiton-2 is part of the 4,945-MW Paiton coal-fired power complex, including the two-unit, 800-MW [[PLN Paiton power station]], owned by PLN; the two-unit, 1,340-MW [[Paiton-1 power station]], operated by PT Paiton Energy; the single-unit, 825-MW [[Paiton-3 power station]], operated by PT Paiton Energy; and the single-unit, 660-MW [[PLN Paiton Baru power station]], owned by [[PLN]].

As of April 2024, Paiton power complex reportedly supplied 60% of East Java's total energy needs.<ref>[https://web.pln.co.id/cms/media/siaran-pers/2024/04/dirut-pln-kunjungi-pltu-paiton-pastikan-pasokan-listrik-aman-jelang-idul-fitri/ Dirut PLN Kunjungi PLTU Paiton, Pastikan Pasokan Listrik Aman Jelang Idul Fitri], PT PLN (Persero), April 6, 2024</ref>

In July 2025, the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (MEMR) announced that retirement planning for the Paiton power complex was underway. The MEMR Secretary General stated that rather than decommissioning the units, the complex would be transitioned to a different fuel. Converting the Paiton power complex into a nuclear power facility was a top candidate.<ref>[https://kumparan.com/kumparanbisnis/pltu-paiton-mulai-kaji-pensiun-dini-berpotensi-jadi-pembangkit-nuklir-25XB2ez0aHl/full PLTU Paiton Mulai Kaji Pensiun Dini, Berpotensi Jadi Pembangkit Nuklir], Kumparan, July 26, 2025</ref>

==Background==

Paiton-2 power station is a 1,320 MW coal-fired power station.<Ref>[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/form.php?pid=41521 Paiton II Coal Power Plant Indonesia,] Global Energy Observatory, accessed May 2012</ref><ref>[http://www.edf.org/documents/9584_coal-plants-spreadsheet.xls "Coal-Fired Plants Financed by International Public Investment Institutions Since 1994"], Appendix to ''Foreclosing the Future: Coal, Climate and International Public Finance: Investment in coal-fired power plants hinders the fight against global warming'', Environmental Defense, April 2009.</ref>

The Paiton-2 power station is operated by PT Jawa Power and consists of 2 x 660 MW units. It began construction in 1996 and began operating in 2000.<ref name=jawa>[http://www.jawapower.co.id/about-us-2/ About Us], PT Jawa Power, accessed June 25, 2021</ref>

As of December 2023, the power station co-fired with sawdust.<ref>[https://money.kompas.com/read/2023/12/04/182413326/lebih-hijau-pltu-paiton-pakai-biomassa-serbuk-kayu-dan-bertahap-kurangi-batu Lebih "Hijau", PLTU Paiton Pakai Biomassa Serbuk Kayu dan Bertahap Kurangi Batu Bara], Kompas, December 4, 2023</ref> As of August 2024, the power station reportedly co-fired bank note waste.<ref>[https://finance.detik.com/energi/d-7480495/pln-bakar-uang-jadi-biomassa-di-3-pltu-ini-mana-saja PLN 'Bakar Uang' Jadi Biomassa di 3 PLTU Ini, Mana Saja?], Detik Finance, August 8, 2024</ref>

==Impact and opposition==

In May 2017, it was reported that the Paiton power complex produced the largest amount of Hazardous and Toxic B3 waste of any facility in East Java, 153 million tonnes a year, a figure that represents 80% of the annual total of 170 million tonnes for East Java.<ref>[http://regional.kompas.com/read/2017/05/18/11280281/komplek.pltu.paiton.sumbang.limbah.beracun.terbesar.di.jatim Komplek PLTU Paiton Sumbang Limbah Beracun Terbesar di Jatim], ''Kompas'', May 18, 2017</ref> B3 waste is defined by Government Regulation 19 of 1994 as "any waste containing dangerous and/or toxic material, which due to its characteristics and/or concentration and/or amount, either directly or indirectly, may damage and/or pollute the living environment and/or endanger human health."<ref>[https://www.ecolex.org/details/legislation/government-regulation-of-the-republic-of-indonesia-regarding-hazardous-and-toxic-waste-management-no-19-of-1994-lex-faoc019486/ Government Regulation of the Republic of Indonesia regarding hazardous and toxic waste management (No. 19 of 1994)] Ecolex, accessed December 2017</ref>

In January 2024, an article described the changes to Bhinor Village caused by the Paiton power complex.<ref>[https://projectmultatuli.org/kisah-orang-orang-desa-bhinor-menanggung-nestapa-akibat-pltu-paiton/ Kisah Orang-Orang Desa Bhinor: Menanggung Nestapa Akibat PLTU Paiton], Project Multatuli, January 25, 2024</ref>

==Background==

The power station will use two GE 9HA.01 gas turbines, which are hydrogen capable but as December 2022 there were no plans for the plant to transition to using hydrogen.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ge.com/news/press-releases/ge-wins-order-for-12-gigawatts-of-power-equipment-in-malaysia|title=GE Wins Order for 1.2 Gigawatts of Power Equipment in Malaysia|last=|first=|date=March 24, 2021|website=GE|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=December 12, 2022}}</ref>

The overall construction cost for the power station was reported in March 2021 as MYR (Malaysian Riggitt) 3.3 billion, which converted to US$745 million in March 2025. Three Malaysian banks, the development bank Bank Pembangunan and two commercial banks, Maybank and United Overseas Bank, provided a joint loan facility totalling MYR 2.7 billion, or US$610 million in March 2025. The project sponsors Worldwide Holdings and KEPCO provided the remaining MYR 600 million in equity.<ref>[https://www.bpmb.com.my/bank-pembangunan-to-co-finance-rm3-3b-power-plant-project-in-pulau-indah/ Bank Pembangunan to co-finance RM3.3b power plant project in Pulau Indah], Bank Pembangunan press release, Mar. 29, 2021</ref>

==Location (existing Panay power station)==

The aerial photo below shows the location of the Panay diesel power plant (PDPP) in Dingle, Iloilo, the Philippines, as identified by Wikimapia.
{{#display_point:10.920334, 122.6726105|width=600|height=500|type=hybrid|zoom=12}}

==Background==

In 2009 Korean Electric Power Corp. said it plans to convert the Panay Diesel Power Plant (PDPP) in Dingle, Iloilo into a coal-fired power plant.

KEPCO is part owner of SPC Power Corp., the mother unit of SPC Island Power Corp. which bought PDPP and the Bohol diesel fired power plant in 2008 for US$5 million.

A coal plant was first proposed by KEPCO for the area in 2000: KEPCO first proposed to put up a 100-megawatt coal-fired power plant in Tibiao, Antique, but then moved to Iloilo, reportedly due to poor soil stability in Tibiao. KEPCO planned to locate the project in the town of Ajuy and later to Banate but ultimately built the coal plant in Cebu due to stiff opposition from environmental groups and the Catholic Church.<ref>[http://scrimgeour.wordpress.com/tag/kepco/ "Kepco plans to convert PDPP to coal-fired plant,"] Iloilo news, July 6, 2009.</ref>

As of 2012 the plant is still listed as diesel with a capacity of 66 MW by the Philippines DOE.<ref>[http://www.doe.gov.ph/doe_files/pdf/01_Energy_Situationer/2012-Power-Plants-Visayas.pdf "List of existing plants: Visayas,"] Philippines DOE, accessed Dec 2013.</ref> Since there has been no further development of this project since 2009, it can be concluded that the project has been abandoned.

==Background==

Pego power station was a two-unit coal-fired power plant with a total capacity of 628 MW. The plant was completed between 1992 and 1995, and was owned by [[Engie]] and [[Endesa]]. Coal was imported by CarboPego via the Port of Sines 290 km away and delivered by rail.<ref>[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/43560 "Pego Coal Power Plant Portugal,"] GEO, accessed April 2016</ref> 

In October 2019, the government announced Pego would be closed by the end of 2021.<ref>[https://www.publico.pt/2019/10/26/economia/noticia/zero-congratulase-antecipacao-fecho-centrais-carvao-pego-sines-1891491 "Zero satisfeita com antecipação do fecho das centrais a carvão do Pego e Sines,"] Publico, October 26, 2019</ref> The plant closed in late November, 2021.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/business/cop/portugals-power-production-goes-coal-free-long-before-deadline-2021-11-22/ "Portugal's power production goes coal-free long before deadline,"] Reuters, November 23, 2021</ref><ref>[https://www.publico.pt/2021/11/21/economia/noticia/acabou-producao-electricidade-partir-carvao-portugal-1985803 "Acabou a produção de electricidade a partir do carvão em Portugal,"] Publico, November 21, 2021</ref>

In addition, the [[Sines power station]], which was originally slated to close by September 2023, was retired in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.euractiv.com/section/energy/news/portugal-on-track-to-become-coal-free-by-year-end/|title=Portugal on track to become coal-free by year end|date=2021-01-15|work=www.euractiv.com|access-date=2021-06-22|language=en-GB}}</ref> 

There are now no operating coal-fired power plants in Portugal.

==Background==

In 2014, Electricity Generation Company of Bangladesh Limited (EGCBL) planned a coal plant for Cox's Bazar District, and the ministry of power approved the project in November 30, 2015. On November 17, 2016, EGCBL signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Japanese company Mitsui to install the coal plant. The plant would have had two units of 650 MW each, and would have used ultra-supercritical technology and imported coal through the [[Matarbari Port]]. The primary cost of the project was estimated at US$1.2 billion. Construction of the power plant was expected to start in mid-2018 and finish by 2023.<ref>[http://www.thebangladeshpost.com/national/3182/pdf "Work on 1300MW coal-fired plant at Pekua begins in 2018,"] Bangladesh Post, June 8, 2017</ref>

The plant was listed in Bangladesh's [https://powerdivision.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/powerdivision.portal.gov.bd/page/4f81bf4d_1180_4c53_b27c_8fa0eb11e2c1/Revisiting%20PSMP2016%20%28full%20report%29_signed.pdf 2016 Master Plan "Revisited",] an updated version of the country's energy plan released in November 2018. Under a scenario of high energy demand, the plant would be commissioned in 2025.<ref>[https://powerdivision.portal.gov.bd/sites/default/files/files/powerdivision.portal.gov.bd/page/4f81bf4d_1180_4c53_b27c_8fa0eb11e2c1/Revisiting%20PSMP2016%20%28full%20report%29_signed.pdf 2016 Master Plan "Revisited",] Bangladesh Power Division, November 2018</ref> The plan also listed a potential 1,200 MW expansion due for 2030 (Phase II).

In October 2019, it was reported that the project had been called off.<ref>[https://www.jagonews24.com/special-reports/news/535275 কয়লাভিত্তিক বিদ্যুৎকেন্দ্র নির্মাণ থেকে সরল সরকার "কয়লাভিত্তিক বিদ্যুৎকেন্দ্র নির্মাণ থেকে সরল সরকার,"] JagoNews24, October 26, 2019</ref> Phase II also does not appear to be moving forward.

==Background==

The Pingshuo Gangue power station was commissioned in 2004 and 2005 with two units of 50 MW and an initial investment of 714.25 million RMB from the Shanxi International Energy Group, ChinaCoal, and Gemeng International.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.qixin.com/company/a82861c2-ae1d-4e8f-9637-1bf0bb58707b?section=reports|title=山西平朔煤矸石发电有限责任公司|last=|first=|date=|website=Qixin|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref> The plant is located in Shanxi Province, China.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wikimapia.org/31292925/Pingshuo-Gangue-Power-Station|title=Pingshuo Gangue Power Station - Wikimapia|last=|first=|date=|website=Wikimapia|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref>
The Environmental Protection Bureau of Shanxi Province accepted the first phase project in March 2006. The second phase of the project's construction, which involved 2×300MW units, was put into trial operation in August 2009 and June 2009 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20150206/588832.shtml|title=山西平朔煤矸石发电有限责任公司2015年自行监测方案 - 北极星火力发电网|last=Polaris Power Network|date=February 6, 2015|website=BJX News|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref> The first two units were retired sometime between 2015 and 2020.<ref>[http://file.finance.sina.com.cn/211.154.219.97:9494/MRGG/BOND/2021/2021-1/2021-01-14/15434672.PDF 格盟国际能源有限公司2021 年度第一期超短期融资券募集说明书], 发行人：格盟国际能源有限公司, January 2021</ref> Units 3 and 4 have a shut-down date scheduled in 2037.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.qixin.com/company/a82861c2-ae1d-4e8f-9637-1bf0bb58707b?section=reports|title=山西平朔煤矸石发电有限责任公司|last=|first=|date=|website=Qixin|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref>

In 2021, the operating company of the plant (under Gemeng International) changed its name from the "China Coal Pingshuo #1 Coal Gangue Power Generation Co., Ltd." officially changed its name to "Sujin Shuozhou Coal Gangue Power Generation Co., Ltd."

==Pollution Controls==

In 2014, the Pingshuo Gangue power station operators hired consultants from the China Building Materials Industry Planning and Research Institute to deal with their ash emission overflow. The consultants decreased the cost of ash storage and advised using ash for other construction or domestic power generation projects.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbm.com.cn/index.php?m=home&c=View&a=index&aid=14433|title=中煤平朔第一煤矸石发电有限公司灰渣综合利用方案_咨询案例|last=|first=|date=May 28, 2020|website=China Development Strategy Institute for Building Materials Industry|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref> In 2015, the company completed the ultra-low emission transformation of its 2×300MW units, adding flue gas desulfurization and dust removal equipment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20151019/672657.shtml|title=清新环境与山西平朔煤矸石发电签署超低排放改造项目合同（附公告） - 北极星火力发电网|last=|first=|date=October 19, 2015|website=BJX News|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref>

==Background==

The first 88 MW gas-fired unit at Point Lisas was brought online in 1977. Two smaller units (20 MW each) were added in 1978, followed by three more 88 MW units and four 62.5 MW units between 1980 and 1982, and two 105 MW units in 2007.<ref name='ref_A'>{{cite web |url=https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |title=Point Lisas Power Station |date= |website=Powergen |access-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505203157/https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Proposed changes to the Point Lisas plant include the replacement of older gas turbines with new turbines and the use of steam from the plant for power generation. However, these plans remain vague and there appears to be no fixed timeline for implementing them.<ref name='ref_A'>{{cite web |url=https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |title=Point Lisas Power Station |date= |website=Powergen |access-date=May 4, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505203157/https://www.powergen.co.tt/Locations/Point-Lisas-Power-Station |archive-date=May 5, 2021 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energynow.tt/blog/powergen-upgrades-means-more-gas-for-energy|title=PowerGen upgrades means more gas for energy|last=|first=|date=March 10, 2017|website=Business Guardian|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref>
