==Quảng Trị-1==

In August 2013, Quảng Trị provincial officials announced that the company Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand ([[EGAT]]) had been licensed to build a $2.3 billion, 1,200-MW, two-unit coal-fired power plant in the Quang Tri Southeast Economic Zone. The project was originally scheduled to come online in 2019-20.<ref>[http://tuoitrenews.vn/business/12425/thailands-power-firm-to-set-up-226-bln-plant-in-central-vn Thailand's Power Firm to Set Up $2.26 Billion Plant in Central Vietnam], ''Tuoi Tre News'', Aug. 21, 2013.</ref> 

The company signed a memorandum of understanding with the Quang Tri provincial government in July 2014. Financial arrangements and land acquisition had not yet been completed at that time. The plant is being built under a build-own-transfer (BOT) scheme. Construction was scheduled to begin at the end of 2017; the first unit would go online in June 2021, and the second in December 2021.<ref>[http://www.nationmultimedia.com/business/Egats-power-plant-project-gets-go-ahead-in-Quang-T-30238472.html Egat's power plant project gets go-ahead in Quang Tri], Nation Multimedia, 15 July 2014.</ref><ref>[http://www.egat.co.th/en/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=207:egati-and-provincial-people-s-committee-of-quang-tri-signed-mou-to-develop-quang-tri-thermal-power-plant-in-vietnam&catid=11:news-release&Itemid=112 EGATI and Provincial People's Committee of Quang Tri signed MOU to develop Quang Tri Thermal Power Plant in Vietnam], EGATI press release, 21 July 2014.</ref>

According to the revised Power Development Plan VII (2016), the project will be completed in 2023 and 2024.<ref name=PDP>DANH MỤC CÁC DỰ ÁN NGUỒN ĐIỆN VÀO VẬN HÀNH GIAI ĐOẠN 2016 - 2030, Ban hành kèm theo Quyết định số 428/QĐ-TTg ngày 18 tháng 3 năm 2016 của Thủ tướng Chính phủ (''LIST OF POWER PROJECT IN OPERATION PERIOD 2016 - 2030, Issued together with Decision No. 428 / QD - TTg of March 18, 2016 by the Prime Minister'')</ref>

EGAT completed a feasibility study in July 2016; that feasibility study was later approved by the Ministry of Industry & Trade.<ref>[http://baodautu.vn/eagti-hoan-thanh-ho-so-nghien-cuu-kha-thi-du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-quang-tri-d47969.html EAGTi hoàn thành hồ sơ nghiên cứu khả thi Dự án Nhà máy nhiệt điện Quảng Trị], Dautu Online, 7 July 2016.</ref> In February 2017, EGAT said it planned to begin construction in mid-2019. The project would cost $2.2 billion.<ref>[http://baodautu.vn/aegti-du-kien-khoi-cong-nha-may-nhiet-dien-quang-tri-1-vao-giua-nam-2019-d58370.html AEGTi dự kiến khởi công Nhà máy nhiệt điện Quảng Trị 1 vào giữa năm 2019], Dautu Online, 3 Feb. 2017.</ref> In February, provincial officials pushed EGAT to begin construction in 2018.<ref>[http://m.icon.com.vn/vi-VN/c580/131959/Quang-Tri-Phan-dau-khoi-cong-xay-dung-Nha-may-Nhiet-dien-1-nam-2018.aspx Quảng Trị: Phấn đấu khởi công xây dựng Nhà máy Nhiệt điện 1 năm 2018], Icon, 20 Feb. 2017.</ref> In June 2017, EGAT said it would indeed begin construction in 2018.<ref>[http://www.baoquangtri.vn/Thời-sự/modid/445/ItemID/121976 UBND tỉnh Quảng Trị làm việc với Tổng cục Năng lượng - Bộ Công thương về dự án Nhà máy nhiệt điện Quảng Trị], Quang Tri Online, 22 June 2017.</ref>

On June 24, 2017, Quang Ninh Thermal Power Plant (EGATi) and the Department of Energy (MOIT) signed an a Memorandum of Understanding on the BOT project. According to the MoU, Units 1 and 2 will be put into commercial operation in 2021.<ref>[http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/buoc-tien-moi-trong-du-an-nhiet-dien-quang-tri.html "Bước tiến mới trong dự án Nhiệt điện Quảng Trị,"] NANGLUONG VIETNAM, 24 October 2017</ref>

In December 2018, EGAT announced that construction had been delayed but that it planned to begin by September 2019.<ref>[https://baodautu.vn/day-nhanh-tien-do-thuc-hien-du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-quang-tri-1-d92449.html Accelerate the implementation of the Quang Tri BOT Thermal Power Plant project 1], Dautur, Dec. 13, 2018</ref> In June 2019 the completion date for Unit 1 was delayed to 2026 and the completion date for Unit 2 was delayed to 2027 in the Ministry Of Industry And Trade's report on the implementation of the revised seventh Power Development Plan (PDP7).<ref>[http://vepg.vn/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/MOIT_Report_58_BC_BCT.pdf Implementation of Power Projects in the Revised Power Development Plan 7], Ministry of Industry and Trade, Republic of Vietnam, Jun. 4, 2019</ref> In November 2019 a ground-breaking ceremony for the plant was held and a 23.5-km road connecting the Quảng Trị Southeastern Industrial Park with Cửa Việt Port was inaugurated.<ref>[http://vietnamnews.vn/economy/548907/construction-on-quang-tri-1-thermal-power-plant-kicks-off.html#PxQgyG6cKctfrU5t.99 Construction on Quảng Tri 1 thermal power plant kicks off], Vietnam News, Nov. 25, 2019</ref>

In September 2020, Thailand's three leading energy companies EGATi, Ratch Group, and Electricity Generating Corp. (EGCO) signed an agreement to develop the plant.<ref name=vb>[https://vietnambiz.vn/ba-cong-ty-nang-luong-hang-dau-thai-lan-dau-tu-vao-nhiet-dien-quang-tri-1-20200918214747764.htm Ba công ty năng lượng hàng đầu Thái Lan đầu tư vào nhiệt điện Quảng Trị 1], VietnamBiz, Sep. 18, 2020</ref> In December 2020 the Provincial People's Committee Le Duc Tien asked EGATi to complete negotiations for a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract with the Vietnamese Industry and Trade Ministry before the end of 2020.<ref>[https://www.quangtri.gov.vn/chi-tiet-tin/-/view-article/1/13848241113627/1607097061184 Tin tức nổi bật UBND tỉnh Quảng Trị làm việc trực tuyến với Công ty Điện lực quốc tế Thái Lan (EGATi)], www.quangtri.gov.vn], Dec. 5, 2020</ref> Without a BOT contract negotiations would have to be restarted once Vietnam's new Public-Private Partnership (PPP) law takes effect in January 2021.<ref>[https://www.vietnam-briefing.com/news/vietnams-new-ppp-law-set-to-take-effect-january-2021.html/ Vietnam’s New PPP Law Set to Take Effect January 2021], Vietnam Briefing, Aug. 28, 2020</ref> According to GreenID the project had been permitted as of June 2021.<ref>Communication with GreenID, July 2021</ref> In August 2021 it was reported that the sponsors' inability to form a Build-Own-Transfer (BOT) company was one reason for the delay in starting construction.<ref>[https://vir.com.vn/construction-of-quang-tri-1-thermal-power-plant-deemed-unfeasible-86996.html Construction of Quang Tri 1 thermal power plant deemed unfeasible], Vietnam Investment Review, Aug. 25, 2021</ref>

An October 2021 report by GreenID lists the Quảng Trị-1 power station as one of 18 coal-fired power stations in Vietnam that was struggling to secure financing. Given that China, Japan, and South Korea have all committed to stop financing new coal-fired power stations, it will be extremely difficult for any of these projects to secure funding in the future.<ref>Trung Chanh, [https://thesaigontimes.vn/18-du-an-nhiet-dien-than-trong-quy-hoach-kho-tiep-can-von/ 18 dự án nhiệt điện than trong quy hoạch khó tiếp cận vốn], The Saigon Times, Oct. 3, 2021</ref> In March 2022, Report No. 1562 by the Office of the Government of Vietnam stated that the plant was financially troubled.<ref>[https://www.mondaq.com/investment-strategy/1192944/bot-projects-the-path-to-closure-in-vietnam Vietnam: BOT Projects--The Path To Closure In Vietnam], Mondaq, Jun. 9, 2022</ref>

On July 4, 2022, the Ministry of Industry and Trade appeared to provide an update on the draft PDP. The document’s list of major power projects planned for 2021-2030 (PDF pages 18-20) included the project.<ref>[https://ia601508.us.archive.org/4/items/pdp-8-jul-22/PDP8%20-%20jul%2022.pdf “Draft National Power Development Plan VIII,”] MOIT, July 4, 2022</ref>

In October 2022, the Thai Ministry of Energy announced that the project was cancelled following nearly a decade of delays. The decision was made following recommendations from the provincial People’s Committee, financial problems, and Vietnam's net zero emissions commitments. Official cancellation documents for the Vietnamese Ministry of Industry and Trade and Quảng Trị Province were on their way.<ref>[https://www.einnews.com/pr_news/594834526/thai-energy-ministry-terminates-1-320mw-thermal-power-project-in-qu-ng-tr “Thai Energy Ministry terminates 1,320MW thermal power project in Quảng Trị,”] Vietnam Economy News, October 8, 2022</ref>

As of February 2025, Power Generation JSC 1 (EVNGENCO 1), a subsidiary of state-owned utility Vietnam Electricity (EVN), was seeking to invest in the cancelled project. EVNGENCO 1 reportedly informed Quảng Trị provincial leaders of its interest in developing the project, though its preferred fuel was unclear.<ref>[https://theinvestor.vn/evn-seeks-to-invest-in-1320-mw-abolished-coal-fired-power-project-in-central-vietnam-d14477.html “EVN seeks to invest in 1,320 MW abolished coal-fired power project in central Vietnam,”] The Investor, February 11, 2025</ref>

In March 2025, the People's Committee of Quang Tri had a working session to discuss the revival of Quảng Trị-1. EVN stated that if they were the investor in the project, it would be developed using coal. If there was a different investor, the project would be proposed using a different fuel in Vietnam's upcoming adjusted Power Development Plan VIII.<ref>[https://baophapluat.vn/ai-lam-chu-dau-tu-nhiet-dien-22-ti-usd-o-quang-tri-post541866.html "Ai làm chủ đầu tư nhiệt điện 2,2 tỉ USD ở Quảng Trị?,"] Báo Pháp luật Việt Nam, March 8, 2025</ref> The plan was reiterated at a March 21 working session facilitated by Vietnam's Deputy Minister of Science and Technology.<ref>[https://baoquangtri.vn/chinh-phu-xu-ly-kien-nghi-cua-tinh-quang-tri-quang-binh-va-tp-hue-192440.htm "Chính phủ xử lý kiến nghị của tỉnh Quảng Trị, Quảng Bình và TP. Huế,"] Báo Quảng Trị, March 21, 2025</ref>

As of March 2025, the status of Quảng Trị-1 was updated from "cancelled" to "announced".

In June 2025, Quang Tri Provincial People's Committee proposed that MOIT formally request that EVN be assigned to the implementation of Quảng Trị-1. The proposal would consider the power station an "emergency power project" (Google translate) to be implemented between 2025 and 2030.<ref>[https://nhadautu.vn/quang-tri-de-nghi-giao-evn-lam-nha-may-nhiet-dien-55000-ty-d96880.html "Quảng Trị đề nghị giao EVN làm nhà máy nhiệt điện 55.000 tỷ,"] Nhà đầu tư, June 14, 2025</ref>

In September 2025, Quang Tri Provincial People's Committee was assigned to "analyze and clarify urgent requirements for project investment". EVNGENCO 1 stated that, if selected for the project, construction could begin in the second half of 2026. Commercial operation remained slated for 2030.<ref>[https://baomoi.com/quang-tri-xem-xet-danh-gia-de-xuat-tai-du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-quang-tri-c53245244.epi "Quảng Trị xem xét đánh giá đề xuất tại dự án Nhà máy nhiệt điện Quảng Trị,"] Báo Mới, September 15, 2025</ref>

In October 2025, an investment proposal was reportedly being prepared, and it was expected to be completed in November.<ref>[https://baoquangtri.vn/thoi-su/202510/day-nhanh-tien-do-thuc-hien-cac-du-an-tai-khu-vuc-my-thuy-fc57c61/ Đẩy nhanh tiến độ thực hiện các dự án tại khu vực Mỹ Thuỷ], Báo và phát thanh, truyền hình Quảng Trị, October 30, 2025</ref> In January 2026, investment procedures appeared to remain ongoing.<ref>[https://batdongsan.vtv.vn/news/quang-tri-lap-to-cong-tac-tang-toc-giai-phong-mat-bang-du-an-trong-diem Quảng Trị lập tổ công tác, tăng tốc giải phóng mặt bằng dự án trọng điểm], Thời báo VTV, January 9, 2026</ref>

==Quảng Trị-2==

In November 2016, KEPCO announced that it was looking at the possibility of building a second phase of the plant.<ref>[http://bqlkkt.quangtri.gov.vn/vi/news/tin-trong-tinh/tap-doan-dien-luc-han-quoc-nghien-cuu-dau-tu-nha-may-nhiet-dien-2-tai-khu-kinh-te-dong-nam-quang-tri-47.html Tập đoàn điện lực Hàn Quốc nghiên cứu đầu tư Nhà máy Nhiệt điện 2 tại Khu kinh tế Đông Nam Quảng Trị], Quảng Trị Province press release, 21 Nov. 2016.</ref> In January 2017, Korea Western Power Co., a subsidiary of [[KEPCO]], signed an agreement with Quảng Trị provincial officials to build the 1,200-MW, two-unit Quảng Trị-2. The project would cost $1.85 billion, and would be completed by the end of 2024.<ref>[http://icon.com.vn/vn-s83-131604-626/Han-Quoc-xay-nha-may-nhiet-dien-chay-than-tai-Quang-Tri.aspx Hàn Quốc xây nhà máy nhiệt điện chạy than tại Quảng Trị], Icon.com.vn, 20 Jan. 2017.</ref> The contract was a Build, Operate, Transfer (BOT) contract, meaning KEPCO will likely invest equity in the project.<ref>[https://lexcommvn.com/image/files/Vietnam%20BOT%20power%20projects%20-%20MOIT%20imposes%20tougher%20statutory%20remedies%20for%20delays.pdf Vietnam BOT power projects: MOIT imposes tougher statutory remedies for delays], LexComm, April 2017</ref>

In October 2018 the CEO of Korea Western Power, a KEPCO subsidiary, said the company would abide by international standards in developing the Quảng Trị-2 plant, and will consider converting the project into renewable power.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x1-pS3WgkZw "중부발전 사장, 국감에서 찌레본 3호기 중단하였다고 밝혀 - 중부발전/서부발전 국정감사 질의 응답,"] Youtube, 2018.10.18, at 4:10 minutes</ref> In January 2019 it was reported that a plan for a 2 x 600 MW Quảng Trị-2 plant had been submitted to the MOIT.<ref>[http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/bao-ton-nang-luong/trung-tam-nang-luong-cua-mien-trung-va-buoc-di-cua-tinh-quang-tri.html Trung tâm năng lượng của miền Trung và bước đi của tỉnh Quảng Trị], Nang Luong, Jan. 16, 2019</ref> In October 2020, facing criticism for investing in the [https://www.gem.wiki/Vung_Ang_power_station Vung Ang-2 power station], KEPCO declared that it would not develop any additional overseas coal power plants beyond Vung Ang-2 and three other projects in Indonesia, the Philippines, and South Africa.<ref>[http://www.businesskorea.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=54060 KEPCO Declares Exit from Overseas Coal Power Plant Market], Business Korea, Oct. 29, 2020</ref>

On July 4, 2022, the Ministry of Industry and Trade appeared to provide an update on the draft PDP. The document’s list of major power projects planned for 2021-2030 (PDF pages 18-20) did not include the project.<ref>[https://ia601508.us.archive.org/4/items/pdp-8-jul-22/PDP8%20-%20jul%2022.pdf “Draft National Power Development Plan VIII,”] MOIT, July 4, 2022</ref> On July 15, 2022, the Deputy Prime Minister appeared to request further review of the major power projects that had been included in the revised PDP VII but not in the draft PDP VIII.<ref>[https://laodong.vn/kinh-doanh/thiet-hai-ra-sao-neu-khong-lam-2430mw-dien-mat-troi-ngoai-quy-hoach-dien-8-1069783.ldo “Thiệt hại ra sao nếu không làm 2.430MW điện mặt trời ngoài quy hoạch Điện 8,”] Laodong, July 18, 2022</ref> The project is presumed shelved for now.

In October 2022, with four years since the last known update on the proposed expansion, it was presumed cancelled.

It is also known as Ras Laffan C power and desalination plant, Ras Qartas Energy Plant.

==Background==

''NS Energy'' reported that the original plan and amendments was approved in 2019:
"The Gulf PD independent power producer (IPP) project is being developed as part of Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) development plan, which envisions the industrial development of 13,285km² of coastal region spanning Thailand’s three eastern provinces including Chonburi, Rayong, and Chachoengsao."<ref name="nse">[https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/gulf-pd-power-plant-rayong-province/ Gulf PD Power Plant, Rayong Province], ''NS Energy'' website, accessed Dec 17, 2019</ref>

In November 2019, Mitsui announced it was investing in the Rayong power plant.<ref name="rmr">[https://www.reuters.com/article/mitsui-co-powerstation-thailand/japans-mitsui-to-invest-in-25-gw-gas-fired-power-plant-in-thailand-idUSL3N27Y027 Japan's Mitsui to invest in 2.5 GW gas-fired power plant in Thailand], ''Reuters'', Nov 18, 2019</ref> Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems, Ltd. will be the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor.<ref>[https://www.mhps.com/news/20180209.html MHPS Receives Order to Construct 5,300MW Power Plant Project in Thailand Incorporating Eight M701JAC Gas Turbines], MHPS website, Feb 9, 2018</ref>

In November 2019, the Asian Development Bank said that the power station would help replace "more than 8,500 MW of generating capacity – equivalent to about 20 per cent of current national energy capacity – of ageing power plants [that] will be retired between 2020 and 2025."<ref name="eec">[https://www.nationthailand.com/business/30378463 ADB, Gulf PD sign Bt5.4-bn deal to build power plant in Rayong], ''The Nation Thailand'', Nov 18, 2019</ref>

In December 2019, Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems shipped the first eight turbines to Bangkok, four for this plant and four for the [[Chonburi Ng Project power station]].<ref>[https://www.power-eng.com/2019/12/06/mhps-ships-jac-turbines-for-ccgt-plant-in-thailand/#gref MHPS ships JAC turbines for CCGT plant in Thailand], ''Power Engineering'', Dec 6, 2019</ref>

==Financing==

In November 2019, Gulf PD secured approximately US$1.7 billion in long-term debt from a group of 14 local and international financial institutions. Half of the loan amount is denominated in US dollars, while the other half is denominated in Thai baht. The major financiers of the project are the Japan Bank for International Cooperation with a loan of US$208 million<ref name="nse" /> and the Asian Development Bank with a loan of US$180 million.<ref>[https://www.adb.org/projects/53239-001/main#project-pds Thailand : Eastern Economic Corridor Independent Power Project], Asian Development Bank Project Data Sheet, last updated Nov. 22 , 2024</ref>

The other co-financers for the project are the Export-Import Bank of Thailand, Mizuho Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Bank of Ayudhy, Siam Commercial Bank, Bangkok Bank, Krung Thai Bank, Kasikornbank, CIMB Thai Bank, Government Savings Bank, and Land and Houses Bank.<ref>[https://hub.optiwise.io/en/documents/50814/644373571BDAC4302A43725E1ADAC538670F742D6FD3C53E1736742C6CD8CC49124007281CDCC43C13447B2A68D2B13167316C1E4E8DCF396E42735C1ADACC396F43775D1CDBC43F62366C1E4E8D_181120191905360174E.pdf Financial close of Gulf PD Company Limited, the operator of Independent Power Producer (IPP) with an installed capacity of 2,650 megawatts], Letter from Gulf PD Company Limited to the Stock Exchange of Thailand, Nov. 18, 2019</ref>

Gulf Energy and Mitsui together provided US$297.60 million in equity for the project.<ref>[https://www.ijglobal.com/data/transaction/48819 Gulf Pluak Daeng CCGT Power Plant (2.65GW) IPP], IJGlobal Transaction Data, last updated Sep. 17, 2024</ref>

==Background==

This project came out of a memorandum of understanding signed in 2015 between India and Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina to set up 3,000 MW gas-based combined cycle power project in phases in Bangladesh. In this first phase, Reliance Power will relocate one module of equipment from its combined cycle power project at Samalkot in Andhra Pradesh for the project in Bangladesh.<ref name=IT>[https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/reliance-power-inks-pact-with-japans-jera-to-set-up-750-mw-power-project-in-bangladesh/articleshow/70956086.cms?from=mdr Reliance Power inks pact with Japan's JERA to set up 750 MW power project in Bangladesh], ''Economic Times'', Sep 3, 2019</ref> The Samalkot unit had been "rendered defunct due to lack of gas."<ref>[https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/reliance-power-partners-with-jera-for-project-in-bangladesh/articleshow/70969106.cms?from=mdr Reliance Power partners with JERA for project in Bangladesh], ''Economic Times'', Sep 4, 2019</ref>

The plant will be situated on a 100-acre parcel of land that also hosts three more power plants -- Meghnaghat combined-cycle power plant (450 MW), Summit Meghnaghat Power Company (335 MW) and Orion Power Meghnaghat Power Plant (100MW). NS Energy reports:
:"It will feature two 242MW GE 9FA gas turbines, electrical generators, two horizontal-type heat recovery steam generators (HRSG), and a 269MW steam turbine generator. It is expected to be operated at an efficiency of more than 60%."<ref name=NSM>[https://www.nsenergybusiness.com/projects/reliance-meghnaghat/ Reliance Meghnaghat Combined-Cycle Power Project], NS Energy website, accessed Dec 23, 2019</ref>
The plant was expected to come online in August 2022,<ref name=IT>[https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/reliance-power-inks-pact-with-japans-jera-to-set-up-750-mw-power-project-in-bangladesh/articleshow/70956086.cms?from=mdr Reliance Power inks pact with Japan's JERA to set up 750 MW power project in Bangladesh], ''Economic Times'', Sep 3, 2019</ref><ref name=":0">Serajul Quadir, [https://www.reuters.com/article/bangladesh-power-india/bangladesh-signs-deal-with-indias-reliance-power-to-buy-electricity-idUSL3N25S074 Bangladesh signs deal with India's Reliance Power to buy electricity], ''Reuters'', Sep 1, 2019</ref>however, the progress in construction stood at 69 per cent as against the targeted 77.3 per cent until March 2022.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/trade/meghnaghat-plant-may-miss-deadline-1654396676|title=Meghnaghat plant may miss deadline|last=The Financial Express|work=The Financial Express|access-date=2022-12-06|language=en}}</ref>

==Financing==

The US$1 billion plant is being financed by loans chiefly from Japanese public and private institutions. In July 2020, ''Nikkei Asian Review'' reported that US$644 million in loans was being provided to the project by the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC), the Japan-led Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the three Japanese commercial megabanks Mizuho, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation and MUFG. The state-owned Nippon Export and Investment Insurance is guaranteeing the private sector loans along with JERA's stake in the power plant. The ''Nikkei'' specified only JBIC's US$266 million contribution to the lending package.<ref name=Nikkei> Shiori Goso, [https://asia.nikkei.com/Business/Energy/Bangladesh-LNG-power-plant-backed-by-645m-in-Japanese-lending "Bangladesh LNG power plant backed by $645m in Japanese lending"], ''Nikkei Asian Review'', Jul. 15, 2020</ref>

Additional finance information shows the plant's construction cost totalling US$1.83 billion. JBIC announced on July 31, 2020 that it had signed a loan agreement with Reliance Bangladesh LNG & Power Limited involving the provision of project financing up to US$265 million.<ref name=JBIC>[https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2020/0731-013532.html "Project Financing for Meghnaghat Natural Gas-Fired Combined Cycle Power Plant Project in Bangladesh"], JBIC press release, Jul. 31, 2020</ref> The ADB awarded US$200 million in financing for the project. The lending package comprises a US$100 millon loan from the ADB and a further US$100 million loan from the Leading Asia’s Private Infrastructure Fund, which is administered by the ADB.<ref name=ADB>[https://www.adb.org/projects/50253-001/main#project-pds "Bangladesh : Reliance Bangladesh Liquefied Natural Gas and Power Project"], ADB Project Data Sheet, last updated Apr. 11, 2025</ref> Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI), like JBIC a Japanese government entity, will guarantee private-sector loans along with JERA's stake in the power plant. The arrangement will cover losses in the event of conflict or nonpayment of power fees. NEXI noted that it was covering US$177 million in loans provided collectively by the following commercial banks: Mizuho, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, MUFG, and Societe Generale.<ref name=NEXI>[https://www.nexi.go.jp/en/topics/newsrelease/2020072102.html "People’s Republic of Bangladesh/NEXI to Provide Investment and Loan Insurance to Support Meghnaghat 718MW Natural Gas Combined Cycle Power Plant Project"], NEXI press release, Jul. 31, 2025</ref> Reliance Power, Chubu Electric Power, and Tokyo Electric Power have together made an equity investment of US$541 million.<ref name=IJG>[https://www.ijglobal.com/data/transaction/36019?name=Meghnaghat%20Gas-Fired%20Power%20Plant%20Phase%20I%20(745MW)%20IPP&link=%2Farticles%2F143110%2Fsponsors-seek-debt-on-bangladesh-rlng-ccgt "Meghnaghat Gas-Fired Power Plant Phase I (745MW) IPP"], IJGlobal, last updated Sep. 3, 2024</ref>

===Death and disease attributable to fine particle pollution from Rio Bravo Jasmin Power Plant===
In 2010, Abt Associates issued a study commissioned by the Clean Air Task Force, a nonprofit research and advocacy organization, quantifying the deaths and other health effects attributable to [[Particulates and coal|fine particle pollution]] from coal-fired power plants.<ref>[http://www.catf.us/resources/publications/files/The_Toll_from_Coal.pdf "The Toll from Coal: An Updated Assessment of Death and Disease from America's Dirtiest Energy Source,"] Clean Air Task Force, September 2010.</ref> Fine particle pollution consists of a complex mixture of [[soot]], [[Heavy metals and coal|heavy metals]], [[Sulfur dioxide and coal|sulfur dioxide]], and [[Nitrogen oxide|nitrogen oxides]]. Among these particles, the most dangerous are those less than 2.5 microns in diameter, which are so tiny that they can evade the lung's natural defenses, enter the bloodstream, and be transported to vital organs. Impacts are especially severe among the elderly, children, and those with respiratory disease. The study found that over 13,000 deaths and tens of thousands of cases of chronic bronchitis, acute bronchitis, asthma, congestive heart failure, acute myocardial infarction, dysrhythmia, ischemic heart disease, chronic lung disease, and pneumonia each year are attributable to fine particle pollution from U.S. coal plant emissions. These deaths and illnesses are major examples of coal's [[External costs of coal|external costs]], i.e. uncompensated harms inflicted upon the public at large. [[Coal plants near residential areas|Low-income and minority populations]] are disproportionately impacted as well, due to the tendency of companies to avoid locating power plants upwind of affluent communities. To monetize the health impact of fine particle pollution from each coal plant, Abt assigned a value of $7,300,000 to each 2010 mortality, based on a range of government and private studies. Valuations of illnesses ranged from $52 for an asthma episode to $440,000 for a case of chronic bronchitis.<ref>[http://www.catf.us/resources/publications/files/Abt-Technical_Support_Document_for_the_Powerplant_Impact_Estimator_Software_Tool.pdf "Technical Support Document for the Powerplant Impact Estimator Software Tool,"] Prepared for the Clean Air Task Force by Abt Associates, July 2010</ref>

==Background==

The power station, also known as Rugeley B, is 1,000 MW and was commissioned in 1972.<ref>Department of Energy and Climate Change, [http://www.decc.gov.uk/media/viewfile.ashx?filetype=4&filepath=Statistics/source/electricity/dukes5_11.xls&minwidth=true "Power stations in the United Kingdom, May 2012"], Department of Energy and Climate Change, May 2012. (This link is to an Excel spreadsheet).</ref> 

Rugeley “A” station, built on the same site in the 1950s, was decommissioned in 1996. Rugeley Power Station is jointly owned by ENGIE (75%) and Mitsui & Co. Ltd. (25%).<ref name=engie>[http://www.rugeleypower.com/?article=19 "Rugeley Power Station expected to cease operations this summer,"] Engie, 8 February 2016</ref>

==Closure==

In February 2016 Engie said the power station is expected to cease market operations in early summer 2016 due to the "deterioration in market conditions for UK coal-fired power generation."<ref name=engie>[http://www.rugeleypower.com/?article=19 "Rugeley Power Station expected to cease operations this summer,"] Engie, 8 February 2016</ref>

A May 2016 Engie press release stated: "Following consultation with employees and unions, ENGIE is now confirming that Rugeley will cease operations by the end of June 2016."<ref>[http://www.rugeleypower.com/?article=21 "RUGELEY POWER STATION - UPDATE,"] Engie, 20 May 2016</ref>

The site of the old coal power station was set to be transformed into a “sustainable village” of 2,000 homes powered by solar panels.<ref>[https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2018/nov/19/rugeley-coal-plant-to-be-transformed-into-a-sustainable-village?utm_source=Greenhouse+Morning+News&utm_campaign=a4388c8f30-Greenhouse_Morning_News_November19th_2018_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_e40c447c1a-a4388c8f30-123999169 "Rugeley coal plant to be transformed into a sustainable village,"] Guardian, November 19, 2018</ref>

==Background==

GDF Suez (now Engie) and Nareva won the US$2.68 billion tender to build and operate the plant in 2010, and Mitsui joined the venture in 2013, and became the Safi Energy Company. In September 2013, L'Office National de l’Electricité et de l’Eau Potable (ONEE) and Safi Energy Company entered into a 30-year "Power Purchase Agreement" for the Safi coal-fired power project. The project includes the construction and operation of a 2 × 693 MW ultra-supercritical coal-fired power plant in the coastal Safi region and the sale of electricity to Morocco's national utility ONEE for 30 years following completion of the plant.<ref>[http://www.gdfsuez.com/en/journalists/press-releases/power-purchase-agreement-signed-for-safi-independent-power-project-morocco/ "Power Purchase Agreement signed for Safi independent power project (2x693 MW) in Morocco,"] GDF Suez, September 10, 2013</ref>

Construction began in 2015 and was carried out by Daewoo Engineering & Construction, with O&M provided by Safi Energy Company. The total investment was US$2.6 billion.<ref>[http://www.heidelbergcement.com/en/safi-power-plant "Safi Power Plant, Morocco,"] Heidelberg Cement, accessed May 2017</ref> This plant is the first coal-fired power station in Africa to use ultra-supercritical technology.<ref>[https://lkakhadma.com/Entreprises/safiec-safi-energy-company/ "SAFIEC (SAFI ENERGY COMPANY),"] lkakhadma, August 17, 2021</ref>

In February 2018, it was reported that plant contractor Daewoo Engineering and Construction was expected to face losses of up to US$400 million in the US$1.8 billion project as the heating facilities of the plant broke during test operations under construction.<ref>[https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/tech/2018/02/693_243812.html "Daewoo E&C faces big loss in Morocco,"] Korea Times, February 8, 2018</ref>

The plant began operation in December 2018.<ref>[https://www.montelnews.com/de/story/spain-to-build-700-mw-cable-with-morocco-amid-import-surge/981521 "Spain to build 700 MW cable with Morocco amid import surge,"] Montel, February 15, 2019</ref><ref>[https://www.spglobal.com/platts/en/market-insights/latest-news/electric-power/050919-spain-could-use-by-pass-clause-to-fend-off-moroccan-power-exports "Spain could use by-pass clause to fend off Moroccan power exports,"] S&P Global, May 9, 2019</ref>

In November 2022, Reclaim Finance reported that Engie was considering selling its stake in the Safi power station.<ref>[https://reclaimfinance.org/site/en/2022/11/16/engie-replacing-one-problem-with-another/ "ENGIE’s dirty coal phase-out: replacing one problem with another,"] Reclaim Finance, November 16, 2022</ref>

In April 2024, Engie stated that they intended to sell their 33% stake in the Safi coal plant by 2027.<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/engie-divest-moroccos-safi-coal-plant-before-2027-2024-04-26/ "Engie to divest from Morocco's Safi coal plant before 2027,"] Reuters, April 26, 2024</ref>

In January 2025, Engie finalized the sale of 15.66% of its stake in the Safi Energy Company to another shareowner, Nareva. Engie retained a 17.67% stake in the project, and reportedly reaffirmed its commitment to exit coal worldwide by 2027.<ref>[https://lematin.ma/economie/centrale-thermique-de-safi-engie-cede-1566-de-sa-participation-a-nareva/269443 “Centrale thermique de Safi : Engie cède 15,66% de sa participation à Nareva,”] Le Matin, March 21, 2025</ref><ref>[https://www.engie.com/sites/default/files/assets/documents/2025-03/Rapport%20d%27activit%C3%A9%20et%20Etats%20financiers%20consolid%C3%A9s%20annuels%202024.pdf “Rapport d’Activité et États Financiers Consolidés Annuels 2024,”] Engie, March 2025</ref> In October 2025, it was indicated by African Intelligence that full control of the Safi plant would be taken by the Moroccan holding company Al Mada following ENGIE’s withdrawal.<ref>[https://www.africaintelligence.com/north-africa/2025/10/21/al-mada-set-to-extend-stranglehold-on-safi-coal-fired-power-station,110537314-art, "Al Mada set to extend stranglehold on Safi coal-fired power station,"] African Intelligence, November 10, 2025</ref>

==Financing==

In September 2014, a financing agreement for the project closed. US$2,103 million in loans were provided by Japan Bank for International Cooperation, Mizuho Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Societe Generale, Credit Agricole Group, BNP Paribas, MUFG Bank, Islamic Development Bank, Attijariwafa Bank, and Banque Centrale Populaire de Maroc. US$520 million in equity was provided by Nareva Holding, Engie, and Mitsui & Co. HSBC acted as the financial adviser to the National Electricity Office.<ref name=":0">[https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/17640/safi-coal-fired-power-plant-ipp-1320mw|title=Preview of Safi Coal-fired Power Plant (IPP) (1320MW),"] IJGlobal, accessed December 10, 2020</ref> The private banks participating in the financing package received insurance coverage from Nippon Export and Investment Insurance.<ref>[http://web.archive.org/web/20160804193237/http://nexi.go.jp/topics/newsrelease/005476.html "モロッコ王国/Safi高効率火力発電プロジェクト(融資保険の引受),"] Nippon Export and Investment Insurance, September 30, 2014</ref>

In November 2021, it was reported that Safi Energy Company (Safiec) failed to renew the guarantee that Standard Chartered Bank had made available to it at the time of the syndicated financing.<ref>[https://mobile.ledesk.ma/2021/11/21/centrale-thermique-de-safi-la-garantie-de-standard-chartered-bank-na-pas-ete-renouvelee/ "Centrale thermique de Safi : la garantie de Standard Chartered Bank n’a pas été renouvelée,"] le Desk, November 21, 2021 (paywall)</ref>

==Opposition==

On March 29, 2014, hundreds demonstrated on the Atlantic coast of Morocco, against the establishment of the Safi power station. Protestors argued that it could increase air pollution for years. The Safi power station is near one of the most important ports country as well as an industrial complex of transformation of phosphate.<ref>[https://observers.france24.com/fr/20140402-installation-une-centrale-thermique-usine-trop-marocains-safi "The thermal power station which revolts the Moroccans of Safi,"] France 24, April 2, 2014</ref> On September 21st, 2014, the Network for the Defense of the Environment organized a protest against the Safi plant, in relation to a United Nations Climate Summit. The Environmental Defense Network also denounced the Safi thermal project and called on citizens to join the opposition. They cited concerns for carbon emissions and chemical gases.<ref>[https://www.hespress.com/%d8%b4%d8%a8%d9%83%d8%a9-%d9%85%d8%ad%d9%84%d9%8a%d8%a9-%d8%aa%d9%86%d8%aa%d9%82%d8%af-%d9%85%d8%b4%d8%b1%d9%88%d8%b9-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%b7%d8%a7%d9%82%d8%a9-%d8%a7%d9%84%d8%ad%d8%b1%d8%a7%d8%b1%d9%8a-187905.html "A local network criticizes the Safi Thermal Power Project,"] Ibrahim Maghraoui, September 22, 2014</ref>

In mid-2017, residents near the Safi power plant opposed the plant in fear of the greed of companies and seizure of lands. They also feared mysterious fumes in the neighborhood.<ref>[https://lakome2.com/societe/24466 "The coal burning experiments at the Safi Thermal Station raise residents’ fears of their mysterious fumes,"] Lakome2, September 19, 2017</ref>

In 2019, private citizens also posted on Facebook, regarding the Safi power plant and opposition.<ref>[https://www.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=705894789896297&id=307104036442043 "Facebook Posts,"] حملة خنقتونا بآسفي, October 18, 2019</ref>

A private citizen also released an article, highlighting how they are tired of pollution and exploitations from the city of Safi, resulting in unemployment and lack of political action. They cite that a number of city activists have protested the Safi thermal station as an extreme danger to the environment and a possible cause of air pollution.<ref>[https://anwalpress.com/ثالوث-التلوث،-انھیار-المآثر-والبطالة/ "Triad of pollution…,"] Anwal Press</ref>

In June 2023, a human rights group in Safi announced that they were suing the general director of the Safi Energy Company for “systematic abuse of the environment and the population” caused by the power station.<ref>[https://al3omk.com/852807.html “حقوقيون يقاضون مدير“آسفي للطاقة” ويدرسون رفع دعوى أمام القضاء البلجيكي,”] June 25, 2023</ref>

==Background==

The four existing coal-fired units of Shanxi Hepo power station, totaling 300 MW, were brought online between 1991 and 2000. The plant is owned by [[Shanxi International Electricity Group]].<ref>[http://bit.ly/1CObppU "关于山西河坡发电有限责任公司“上大压小”热电联产异地新建工程(变更)补充环境影响报告书的批复"], 中华人民共和国环境保护部, 2014-04-14</ref> 

The 4 units were retired in 2016 after the expansion units went operation.<ref>[http://www.sxgjny.com/hpfd/SubComInfo.aspx?comId=58&catalogId=115&tp=Pro&SubCatalogID=22&menuid=1"山西河坡发电有限责任公司企业简介,"] International Energy Group, accessed Jan 2018</ref>

==Description of Expansion==

Shanxi International Electricity Group is currently building two additional coal-fired units at this plant, with a total planned capacity of 700 MW. The new units are scheduled to be completed in 2015.<ref>[http://bit.ly/1AvjLPf "山西河坡电厂2×350兆瓦超临界热电联产项目开工"], 阳泉市政府, 2012-09-24</ref><ref>[http://www.huanqiu803.com/sell/show-htm-itemid-40528.html "山西河坡发电公司北侧大门及煤场管理站建筑安装工程招标,"] 015-06-10</ref>

The new units were completed in 2016.<ref>[http://mt.sohu.com/it/d20170111/123985066_131990.shtml "[独家]2016年12月电力项目情况:涉及核准、开工、并网等,"] Sohu, Jan 10, 2017</ref>

==Background==

Shanxi Liulin power station originally consisted of four units totaling 1400 MW. The first two units of 100 MW each were put into operation in 1995 and 1996, respectively, at a total investment of 1.1 billion yuan. The units were funded through loans from the Asian Development Bank (ADB).<ref>[http://en.sxgjny.com/llfd/SubComInfo.aspx?comId=55&catalogId=80&tp=Pro&SubCatalogID=22&menuid=1 "Shanxi Liulin Power Generation Co. Ltd,"] Shanxi International Energy Group website, accessed October 2014</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20230721125406/https://www.mee.gov.cn/gkml/sthjbgw/spwj1/201408/t20140825_288226.htm 关于山西柳林联盛煤矸石综合利用电厂二期工程], mee.gov.cn, 2014-08-20</ref>

In 2008 two more units of 600 MW each began operation.<ref>[http://www.sxgjdl.com/english/history/ "Development History,"] Shanxi International Energy Group website, accessed October 2014</ref>

New units were also built at the related [[Liulin Liansheng power station]].

==Description of Expansion==

Shanxi International Energy Group is currently planning to build two additional coal-fired units at this plant, with a total planned capacity of 1,200 MW.<ref>[http://bit.ly/1tt2Ji9 "瑞光热电1号机组圆满通过168小时试运行"], 国际能源网, 2011-12-23</ref>

However, with no developments since 2011, the expansion appears to be cancelled.

==Background on Project==

[[Shanxi International Electricity Group]] and [[ChinaCoal]] are currently planning to build a four-unit coal-fired power plant with a total planned capacity of 1,300 MW in Shanxi Province. The first two units began operating in 2012.<ref>[http://bit.ly/1rOZdwt "昱光发电厂2号机组通过168小时试运行"], 中国能源建设集团有限公司, 2012-5-29</ref><ref>[http://bit.ly/1pcegih "4火电项目获环保部环评公示"], 中国能源报人民网, 2012-05-14</ref><ref>[http://bit.ly/1wjOW2r " 企业简介"], 山西昱光发电有限责任公司</ref>

==Expansion==

Two more units of 350 MW each have been permitted.<ref>[http://bit.ly/1rYoA4Z "我院签订山西昱光发电有限公司二期2×350MW工程EPC总承包合同"], 西北电力设计院, 2014-05-29</ref><ref>[http://zgdlhg.com/xwzx/201507233079.html "山西省环境保护厅批复四个火电项目,"] 2015-07-23</ref><ref>[http://www.zmsxhy.com/n47/n84/c47508/content.html "中煤华昱昱光发电厂,"] China Coal, 2014-03-16</ref> 

They were reported as under construction in November 2015, and planned for operation in 2017.<ref>[http://epaper.sxrb.com/shtml/sxrb/20151116/294192.shtml "李小鹏在朔州忻州调研时强调：深入贯彻落实五中全会精神努力实现经济社会全面发展,"] Nov 11, 2015</ref>

Unit 4 was commissioned on June 6, 2019.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20190606/984692.shtml "昱光电厂#4机组顺利通过168小时试运行,"] 北极星电力网新闻中心, 2019/6/6</ref> Unit 3 was commissioned on June 17, 2019.<ref>[http://news.bjx.com.cn/html/20190617/986482.shtml "山阴电厂二期项目3号机组通过168小时试运行,"] 北极星电力网新闻中心, 2019/6/17</ref>

==Background==

The power station has a total capacity of 1,800 MW.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%B1%B1%E8%A5%BF%E5%85%86%E5%85%89%E5%8F%91%E7%94%B5%E6%9C%89%E9%99%90%E8%B4%A3%E4%BB%BB%E5%85%AC%E5%8F%B8|title=山西兆光发电有限责任公司|last=|first=|date=2019|website=Baidu|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-04}}</ref>
The first phase of construction for the Shanxi Zhaoguang power station consisted of two 300 MW units that were commissioned in 2005, with an initial investment of 2.54 billion RMB. Owned by Gemeng International, construction for the plant began in 2004. The second phase of the project included two additional 600MW units that were commissioned in 2009; together, all four units represented a total investment of 7.1 billion RMB. The total planned capacity for this plant is 3,000 MW. The third phase of the project, which has yet to be proposed or completed, will consist of another two 600 MW units.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E5%B1%B1%E8%A5%BF%E5%85%86%E5%85%89%E5%8F%91%E7%94%B5%E6%9C%89%E9%99%90%E8%B4%A3%E4%BB%BB%E5%85%AC%E5%8F%B8|title=山西兆光发电有限责任公司|last=|first=|date=2019|website=Baidu|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-06-04}}</ref> 

Emission control retrofits were completed by 2016 for all four units. The facility is equipped with desulfurization, denitrification, and dust removal facilities, and uses online flue gas monitoring technology.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.163.com/news/article/C241K2RU00014SEH.html|title=山西国际能源集团有限公司2016年上半年财务等重大信息|last=网易|first=|date=2016-09-29|work=WangYang XinWen|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref>

In 2016, the Shanxi Zhaoguang power station was fined two million RMB by the Huozhou municipal government after an onsite investigation revealed that the height of their coal-fired stack was higher than their wind-shield and dust-suppression nets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.huozhou.gov.cn/contents/12295/123290.html|title=霍州市环境保护局行政处罚决定书 霍环罚字[2016]17号-环境保护-霍州市人民政府|last=|first=|date=October 20, 2017|website=Huozhou Municipal Government|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref>

In 2021, Zhejiang Thermal Power was contracted for the daily maintenance and operation of all units from 2021-2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://power.in-en.com/html/power-2386266.shtml|title=中标 {{!}} 中国能建浙江火电中标山西兆光电厂4台机组日常维护工程-国际电力网|last=Hu|first=Yiyu Aiding|date=April 9, 2021|website=Power|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2021-06-04}}</ref>

==Background==

In November 2021, the winner of the tender for construction of this new power station was announced: it will be commissioned by a consortium of companies EDF (France), Nebras (Qatar), Sojitz Corporation (Japan) and Kyuden International Corporation (Japan)<ref name="ref_5">{{cite web |url=https://uz.sputniknews.ru/20211122/obyavlen-pobeditel-tendera-na-stroitelstvo-tes-v-syrdare-21458685.html |title=Объявлен победитель тендера на строительство ТЭС в Сырдарье |date= |website=Sputnik Узбекистан |access-date=July 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220709155956/https://uz.sputniknews.ru/20211122/obyavlen-pobeditel-tendera-na-stroitelstvo-tes-v-syrdare-21458685.html |archive-date=July 9, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ref_6">{{cite web |url=https://fergana.media/news/123914/ |title=Третью крупную ТЭС в Сырдарье построят компании из трех стран |date= |access-date=July 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220514055314/https://fergana.media/news/123914/ |archive-date=May 14, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>. ENERSOK, a newly formed project company, will be tasked with carrying out construction and management of Syrdarya II. As part of the sales purchase agreement, Nebras will control 33.3% of Enersok, while the remaining shares will be divided amongst EDF, Sojitz and Kyuden.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nebras-power.com/media/news/2022/03/nebras-power-uzbekistan?language_content_entity=en|title=Nebras Power signs agreement to build and operate large-scale CCGT power project in Uzbekistan|last=|first=|date=March 29, 2022|website=Nebras Power|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref> On March 16, 2023 the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) signed a loan agreement in project financing amounting up to approximately USD393 million with ENERSOK. The loan is co-financed with Mizuho Bank, Ltd., Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Societe Generale and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI) will provide insurance for the loan from the private financial institutions<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2022/0324-017573.html|title=Project Financing for Syrdarya II Natural Gas-Fired Combined Cycle Power Plant Project in Uzbekistan|last=|first=|date=March 24, 2023|website=JBIC|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref>. The overall cost of the project is estimated at approximately US$950 million<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/45205/syrdarya-ccgt|title=Syrdarya CCGT|last=|first=|date=March 16, 2023|website=IFC PROJECT INFORMATION & DATA PORTAL|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref>. 

The electricity produced by the plant will be sold to Uzbek state-owned power company JSC National Electricity Grid of Uzbekistan for a duration of 25 years<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2022/0324-017573.html|title=Project Financing for Syrdarya II Natural Gas-Fired Combined Cycle Power Plant Project in Uzbekistan|last=|first=|date=March 24, 2023|website=JBIC|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref>. It will be one of the nation’s largest power generating facilities upon completion and will be instrumental in helping the country meet its growing energy demands from both industry and residential sectors. The power station will be built in the Bayaut district, approximately 2 km northeast of the city of Shirin, in the Syrdarya region of Uzbekistan, approximately 150 km south of Tashkent. The project site is adjacent to the [[Syrdarya I power station]] and approximately 1.5 km north of an existing gas-fired thermal power plant [[Syrdarya power station]] established in the 1970s<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/45205/syrdarya-ccgt|title=Syrdarya CCGT|last=|first=|date=March 16, 2023|website=IFC PROJECT INFORMATION & DATA PORTAL|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref>. 

As of April 2024, the construction is ongoing. Mitsubishi Power will provide two gas turbines M701JAC for the plant. The plant is expected to become operational in 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://leg.co.ua/stati/turbiny-mitsubishi-budut-rabotat-na-novoy-gazovoy-elektrostancii-v-uzbekistane.html|title=ТУРБИНЫ MITSUBISHI БУДУТ РАБОТАТЬ НА НОВОЙ ГАЗОВОЙ ЭЛЕКТРОСТАНЦИИ В УЗБЕКИСТАНЕ|date=July 11, 2023|website=leg.co.ua|url-status=live|access-date=November 3, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099021524122523695/pdf/P174323198e6990e21988510d503c071902.pdf|title=Uzbekistan Syrdarya Efficient Power Generation Project (P174323)|date=February 15, 2024|website=The World Bank|url-status=live|access-date=April 1, 2024}}</ref> In October 2024, it was reported that the equipment of the power plant had been delivered from Japan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazeta.uz/ru/2024/10/22/edf/|title=«Работать в Узбекистане — это рок-н-ролл» — представитель французской EDF|date=October 22, 2024|website=www.gazeta.uz|url-status=live|access-date=November 18, 2024}}</ref> In December 2024, during a briefing the press secretary of the Uzbekistan's Ministry of Energy mentioned that the power plant would be commissioned in 2025-2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gov.uz/uz/minenergy/news/view/29602|title=Information about major projects being implemented in our country to introduce solar, wind and thermal power plants|date=December 6, 2024|website=Government Portal of the Republic of Uzbekistan|url-status=live|access-date=April 8, 2025}}</ref>

In August 2025, it was reported that the more than 80% of the construction and installation work had been completed. The power plant is scheduled to be commissioned in June 2026. After commissioning, it will be able to cover up to 17% of the country’s electricity demand and allow annual savings of up to 2 billion cubic meters of gas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energyforum.uz/ru/novosti/tes-syrdara-2-smozet-obespecit-do-17--potrebnosti-uzbekistana-v-elektroenergii|title=ТЭС "Сырдарья-2" сможет обеспечить до 17 % потребности Узбекистана в электроэнергии|date=August 19, 2025|website=energyforum.uz|url-status=live|access-date=September 18, 2025}}</ref>

In February 2025, the first firing of Gas Turbine Unit 1 was successfully completed, marking a key step toward commercial operation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DUmZ3QnDS4P/|title=The first firing of Gas Turbine Unit 1 has been successfully completed at the Syrdarya Phase II 1,600 MW Combined Cycle Power Plant in Uzbekistan|date=2026-02|website=www.instagram.com|url-status=live|access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref>

'''Snetterton power station''' is an operating power station of at least 42-megawatts (MW) in Breckland District, Norfolk, England, United Kingdom.
It is also known as Snetterton Renewable Energy Centre, Snetterton Renewable Energy Plant (Snetterton Biomass Plant).

{{Navbar-Global_Coal_Plant_Tracker}} '''Srikakulam Thermal Power Station (Sumitomo)''' is a cancelled power station in Polaki, Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh, India. ==Location== ==== '''Table 1:''' Project-level location details ==== {| class="wikitable" |+ !Plant name !Location !Coordinates ([https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Geodetic_System WGS 84]) |- | Srikakulam Thermal Power Station (Sumitomo) | Polaki, Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh, India | 18.3667, 84.1 (approximate) |} {{ #display_map: 18.3667, 84.1 |width=600 |height=500 |type=normal |zoom=7 }} ==Project Details== ==== '''Table 2:''' Unit-level details ==== {| class="wikitable" |+ !Status !Fuel(s) !Capacity (MW) !Technology !Emergency/Backup |- | Cancelled | coal: unknown{{cite web |url=https://www.gem.wiki/Coal_source_methodology_for_the_Global_Coal_Plant_Tracker}} | 4000 | ultra-supercritical | False |} ==== '''Table 3:''' Unit-level ownership and operator details ==== {| class="wikitable" |+ !Owner !Parent |- | Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corp Ltd [50%]; Sumitomo Corp [50%] | Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corp Ltd [50.0%]; Sumitomo Corp [50.0%] |} '''Project-level coal details''' * '''Coal source(s)''': domestic ==Financing== '''Source of financing:''' [[Japan International Cooperation Agency]]
==Background== Srikakulam Thermal Power Station was originally proposed as a 2,400 MW coal plant by [[Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation]] (APGENCO) for the district of Srikakulam.[http://www.apgenco.gov.in/ "Future Projects,"] APGENCO website, accessed February 2012 In December 2014 it was reported that APGENCO had signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Japan-based Sumitomo Corporation for a 4,000 MW coal plant in Srikakulam. Sumitomo will reportedly share technology for the proposed power plant, prepare a Detailed Project Report, and arrange funding from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). Investment in the project is estimated to be around Rs.200 billion.[http://www.cmie.com/kommon/bin/sr.php?kall=wclrdhtm&nvdt=20141208154654583&nvpc=099000000000&nvtype=TIDINGS "New projects worth Rs.240 bln announced in power sector in November 2014,"] CMIE, Dec 8, 2014 According to Andhra Nation, the location of the plant will be the village of Polaki.[https://andhranation.wordpress.com/2015/03/11/sumitomo-decides-to-set-up-its-4000-mw-thermal-power-plant-at-polaki-in-srikakulam-district/ "Sumitomo decides to set up its 4000 MW thermal power plant at Polaki in Srikakulam district,"] Andhra Nation, Mar 10, 2015 In August 2015, it was reported that the government of Andhra Pradesh told Sumitomo that the company would be limited to 1,650 acres of land, rather than the 3,000 acres that the company had sought. The government argued that the amount of land needed to store coal could be limited by bringing coal by conveyer belt, due to the project's seaside location. By limiting the acreage of the plant, the government reported was seeking to minimize the amount of land that would need to be acquired from local farmers.K. Srinivasa Rao, [http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/govt-decides-to-minimise-land-acquisition-for-1600-acres-for-sumitomo-project/article7565838.ece "Government decides to minimise land acquisition for 1600 acres for Sumitomo project,"] The Hindu, August 21, 2015 On April 12, 2017, AP Energy minister Kimida Kala Venkata Rao stated that Thermal Power Plants (TPP) are not viable in the state as it has sufficient power, and the government planned to put on hold all the proposed TPPs.[http://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/Andhra-Pradesh/2017-04-12/Thermal-power-stations-not-viable-now-in-AP--Kimida-Kala-Venkata-Rao/292775 "Thermal power stations not viable now in AP: Kimida Kala Venkata Rao,"] Hans India, Apr 12, 2017 On April 29, 2017, the AP State government said the decision to set up the 4,000 MW plant was deferred until the year 2022.V. Raghavendra, [http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-andhrapradesh/state-drops-thermal-project-plan-at-polaki/article18289683.ece "State drops thermal project plan at Polaki,"] The Hindu, Apr 29, 2017 ==Opposition== Villagers in Thotada, Rallapalli, and Susaram have opposed the plant on the basis that the government does not actually possess the 1,300 acres that it claims to have available for the project. CPI and CPI(M) leaders say that the land must remain in the status of cultivation under the Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act-2014. “We don’t agree with the argument of the Government. The left parties will continue to extend their cooperation to this agitation. We will not allow acquisition of fertile lands,” said CPI(M) Srikakulam secretary Bhaviri Krishnamurthy.K. Srinivasa Rao, [http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/andhra-pradesh/govt-decides-to-minimise-land-acquisition-for-1600-acres-for-sumitomo-project/article7565838.ece "Government decides to minimise land acquisition for 1600 acres for Sumitomo project,"] The Hindu, August 21, 2015 In July 2016 it was reported that difficulties with acquiring land in Polaki were "causing embarrassment" to officials. After initially believing it owned the 1,300 of the acres needed for the project, it turned out that the land had been under occupation for many decades. Left parties and representatives of farmers' associations accused the government of trying to intimidate opponents of the plant by deploying a heavy police presence. CPI Srikakulam officials vowed to support the opponents of the plant and demanded that cases filed against local leaders be withdrawn. “The government is trying to convert Srikakulam into a dumping yard by proposing thermal and atomic power plants. Such activities will only lead to displacement of thousands of people,” said CPI Srikakulam wing secretary Chapara Venkata Ramana.[http://www.worldtvnews.co.in/?p=55714 "Govt. owns 1,300 acres, but farmers have been enjoying possession for long,"] World TV News, July 1, 2016 ==Articles and Resources== ===References=== ===Additional data=== To access additional data, including an interactive map of coal-fired power stations, a downloadable dataset, and summary data, please visit the [https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-coal-plant-tracker/ Global Coal Plant Tracker] on the Global Energy Monitor website. ==Financing==

*'''Source of financing:''' SK Group (Korea)

==Background==

In May 2018 KEPCO announced that it was in talks with a "local partner" and was investing US$2 billion to develop a 1,000-MW coal-fired plant in Sual but did not name the partner.<ref>[http://www.gmanetwork.com/news/money/companies/655206/kepco-in-talks-with-local-partner-to-develop-1-000-mw-sual-power-plant/story/ KEPCO in talks with local partner to develop 1,000-MW Sual power plant], GMA News Online, May 31, 2018</ref> In June 2018, in what appears to be a reference to the same project, SK Engineering & Construction (SKE&C), a subsidiary of South Korean conglomerate SK Group, announced that it had signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) with the Government of the Philippines to build two 600 MW coal-fired power plants on Luzon island at an estimated cost of KRW2.2 trillion (US$1.98 billion).<ref>[http://www.koreaittimes.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=83851 SK Engineering & Construction signs a 2-billion-dollarcontract to build coal-fired plants in the Philippines], Korea Times, Jun. 18, 2018</ref> 

In January 2019 KEPCO signed a memorandum of understanding with Trans-Asia to acquire the site of Trans-Asia's proposed 3 x 300 MW [[Baquioen power station]] and use it for KEPCO's 1 x 1,000 MW Sual KEPCO power station.<ref>[http://manilastandard.net/business/power-technology/286666/kepco-plans-to-build-1-000-mw-coal-fired-plant-in-pangasinan.html Kepco plans to build 1,000-MW coal-fired plant in Pangasinan], Manila Standard, Jan. 31, 2019</ref> In August 2019 the Philippine Department of Energy (DOE) listed the plant as a 2 x 500 MW project with a commissioning date of 2024.<ref>[https://www.doe.gov.ph/sites/default/files/pdf/electric_power/luzon_indicative_2019_jan_aug.pdf PRIVATE SECTOR INITIATED POWER PROJECTS (LUZON) INDICATIVE], Philippine Department of Energy, 31 August 2019</ref> The project will cost an estimated US$1.834 billion or P91.7 billion.<ref>[https://businessmirror.com.ph/2019/02/01/kephilco-keen-on-pursuing-coal-plant-project-in-sual-pangasinan/ Kephilco keen on pursuing coal plant project in Sual, Pangasinan], Business Mirror, Feb. 1, 2019</ref>

In October 2020 KEPCO announced that it would no longer finance foreign coal-fired power plants with the exception of [https://www.gem.wiki/Banten_Suralaya_power_station Jawa-9 and Jawa-10] in Indonesia and [https://www.gem.wiki/Banten_Suralaya_power_station Vung Ang-2 power station] in Vietnam. “We hope that this is not a false promise and that KEPCO will soon make an explicit statement that it is withdrawing from the Sual 2 project,” said Ian Rivera of the Philippine Movement for Climate Justice (PMCJ).<ref>[https://news.mongabay.com/2020/10/south-koreas-move-away-from-coal-leaves-a-philippine-power-plant-in-limbo/ South Korea’s move away from coal leaves a Philippine power plant in limbo], Mongabay, Oct. 26, 2020</ref>

In October 2020, KEPCO announced that it was cancelling its investment in this project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.power-eng.com/2020/10/20/south-koreas-kepco-cancels-foreign-coal-power-investment/#gref|title=South Korea’s KEPCO cancels foreign coal power investment|last=|first=|date=October 20, 2020|website=Power Engineering|url-status=live|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=}}</ref> According to the Philippine Movement for Climate Justice (PMCJ) the project is cancelled.<ref>Communication with PMCJ, January 2021</ref>

==Background==

In October 2014, PT Tanjung Power Indonesia signed a power purchase agreement with [[PLN]] for the construction of a two-unit, 200-MW coal-fired power plant in South Kalimantan Province. Tanjung Power, the project's developer, is a joint venture between [[Adaro Indonesia]] and Korea East-West Power (a subsidiary of Korea Electric Power Corporation, or [[KEPCO]]). The plant would be located near Adaro's [[Tabalong coal concession]], and would cost $450-550 million. The project is part of Phase II of Indonesia's Fast Track Program, and would be built under a Build, Own, Operate, & Transfer (BOOT) agreement with PLN. Financing is scheduled to be finalized by late 2015, and the plant is scheduled for completion in 2019.<ref>[http://bisnisuntung7.blogspot.com/2014/10/pltu-2-x-100-mw-kabupaten-tabalong.html PLTU 2 x 100 MW Kabupaten Tabalong Kalsel Akan Dibangun], Bisnis Energi, 17 Oct. 2014.</ref><ref>[http://energitoday.com/2014/11/28/adaro-bangun-pltu-2x100-mw-di-tabalong-us-550-juta/ Adaro Bangun PLTU 2×100 MW di Tabalong US$ 550 Juta], Energi Today, 28 Nov. 2014.</ref><ref>[http://www.pln.co.id/blog/pln-tandatangani-kesepatakan-dengan-dua-pengembang-swasta/ "PLN Tandatangani Kesepatakan Dengan Dua Pengembang Swasta,"] October 15, 2014</ref>

In January 2017, it was reported that construction of the plant was 30% complete.<ref>[https://finance.detik.com/energi/3404026/pembangunan-pltu-tabalong-2x100-mw-di-kalsel-capai-30 Pembangunan PLTU Tabalong 2x100 MW di Kalsel Capai 30%], ''Detik Finance'', Jan. 24, 2017</ref> In August 2017 a building on the construction site collapsed and injured 7 workers.<ref>[https://kumparan.com/@kumparannews/bangunan-pltu-di-kalimantan-selatan-ambruk-7-orang-terluka Bangunan PLTU di Kalimantan Selatan Ambruk, 7 Orang Terluka] ''Kumparan'', Aug. 21, 2017</ref> Construction was expected to be complete in Q3 of 2018.<ref>[http://www.jsbmarketresearch.com/construction/tpi-kalsel-coal-fired-power-plant-200-mw-south-kalimantan-project-profile TPI – Kalsel Coal-Fired Power Plant 200 MW – South Kalimantan - Project Profile
], JBS Market Research, Mar. 26, 2018</ref> In September 2018 it was reported that construction of the plant was 85% complete.<ref>[https://industri.kontan.co.id/news/adaro-energy-adro-pastikan-proyek-pltu-bakal-rampung-tepat-waktu Adaro Energy (ADRO) pastikan proyek PLTU bakal rampung tepat waktu], Kontan, Sep. 23, 2018</ref> In June 2019 Adaro announced that the plant would be commissioned in the second half of 2019.<ref>[https://katadata.co.id/berita/2019/06/28/adaro-pastikan-pltu-tanjung-beroperasi-tahun-ini Adaro Pastikan PLTU Tanjung Beroperasi Tah], Katadata, Jun. 28, 2019</ref> Unit 1 was commissioned in September 2019 and Unit 2 was commissioned in December 2019.<ref>[http://www.adaro.com/pages/read/7/24/Ketenagalistrikan Adaro Power Making Progress Downstream], Adaro, accessed November 2020</ref>

In October 2022, the Institute for Essential Services Reform listed Tabalong power station as a strong candidate for early retirement.<ref>[https://databoks.katadata.co.id/datapublish/2022/10/21/ini-daftar-pltu-yang-layak-pensiun-dini-pada-2023-menurut-iesr Ini Daftar PLTU yang Layak Pensiun Dini pada 2023 menurut IESR], Katadata, October 21, 2022</ref>

In May 2024, PT Tanjung Power Indonesia signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Tabalong Regency Government for the co-firing of municipal waste at their coal-fired power station in Tabalong.<ref>[https://www.antaranews.com/berita/4125738/tabalong-gandeng-swasta-manfaatkan-sampah-organik-bahan-bakar-pltu Tabalong gandeng swasta manfaatkan sampah organik bahan bakar PLTU], Antara News, May 28, 2024</ref>

In July 2025, an article recounted the negative public health impacts attributed to Tabalong power station and [[Tabalong Wisesa power station]].<ref>[https://mongabay.co.id/2025/07/20/pekat-jerubu-pltu-batubara-selimuti-komplek-purnawirawan/ Pekat Jerubu PLTU Batubara Selimuti Komplek Purnawirawan], Mongabay, July 20, 2025</ref>

As of January 2026, the AlamTri Power website stated that Tabalog power station had a 25-year power purchase agreement.<ref>[https://www.alamtri.com/pages/read/7/24/Power AlamTri Power], AlamTri, accessed January 5, 2026</ref>

==Financing==

In October 2015, Adaro Energy secured financing for the proposed plant.<ref>[http://jakartaglobe.beritasatu.com/business/adaro-secures-540m-loan-s-kalimantan-power-project/ "Adaro Secures $540m Loan for S. Kalimantan Power Project,"] Jakarta Globe, October 09, 2015</ref> The project reached financial closure after it secured US$540 million in loans from Korea Development Bank, MUFG Bank, DBS Bank, Mizuho Financial Group, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, and HSBC. The financial advisor for the project is DBS Bank.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/32622/kalsel-coal-fired-power-plant-200mw-ipp|title=Preview of KalSel Coal-Fired Power Plant (200MW) IPP {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-09-17}}</ref>
