==Background==

Tanjung Jati B power station is a 2,640 megawatt (MW) coal-fired power station located in Central Java Province, Indonesia. The power station comprises four 660 MW generating units.<ref name="GEO">[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/41518 "Tanjung Jati-B Coal Power Plant Indonesia,"] Global Energy Observatory, accessed December 2013</ref><ref>[http://www.edf.org/documents/9584_coal-plants-spreadsheet.xls "Coal-Fired Plants Financed by International Public Investment Institutions Since 1994"], Appendix to ''Foreclosing the Future: Coal, Climate and International Public Finance: Investment in coal-fired power plants hinders the fight against global warming'', Environmental Defense, April 2009.</ref> [[Tanjung Jati Coal Terminal]] serves the power station.<ref>[http://www.censin.com/indonesia-coal-ports/ "Indonesia Coal Ports"] Censin Resources, accessed on August 16, 2011.</ref>

The current plant was built in two phases, each comprising two 660 MW units. A third phase of two 1,000 MW units is planned. The project owner, PT Central Java Power (owned by Sumitomo) has executed a finance lease agreement with [[PT PLN]] as the lessee. When the lease period expires the assets will be transferred to PLN.<ref>[http://web.archive.org/web/20150325053944/http://www.sumitomocorp.co.jp/english/news/detail/id=25675 "Completion Ceremony of Tanjung Jati B Coal-Fired Power Plant Expansion in Indonesia"] Sumitomo Corporation, Feb. 2012</ref>

In November 2022, Sumitomo announced that Units 1-4 of the Tanjung Jati B power station would be retired early in favor of developing the 9 GW Kayan Cascade Hydropower project.<ref>[https://ekonomi.bisnis.com/read/20221125/44/1602103/sumitomo-lepas-aset-pltu-tanjung-jati-b-alihkan-investasi-ke-plta-kayan "Sumitomo Lepas Aset PLTU Tanjung Jati B, Alihkan Investasi ke PLTA Kayan"] Bisnis Indonesia, November 25, 2022</ref>

In December 2023, construction work on a chute repair was underway at Tanjung Jati B power station.<ref>[https://www.plnnpc.com/?p=6407 "Revitalisasi Chute Stare A PLTU Tanjung Jati B"] PT PLN Nusantara Power Construction, December 15, 2023</ref>

As of May 2025, Phases I and II were reportedly targets for co-firing sawdust.<ref>[https://energyandcleanair.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/EN-IDN-Biomass-co-firing-in-Indonesia.pdf Biomass co-firing in Indonesia: Prolonging, not solving coal problem], Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, May 2025</ref>

===Phase I (Units 1 and 2): 2 x 660 MW===
The first phase went through a long history of development before finally being commissioned in 2006. The website "Power Plants Around the World" describes the story as follows:<ref name="trading">[http://www.industcards.com/st-coal-indonesia.htm "Coal-Fired Power Plants in Indonesia,"] Power Plants Around the World, accessed December 2013</ref>

:" Tanjung Jati-B was proposed by Hopewell Holdings and initially bid as an IPP in June 1994. A PPA with PLN followed in September 1994. The EPC contract was signed in September 1995 and site work started on 15 April 1997. The Asian financial crisis combined with allegations about mismanagement of the PPA terms led to Hopewell withdrawing, leaving the project about one-third complete. Sumitomo renegotiated the development as a leasing scheme and construction resumed in September 2003 with financing from JBIC. The 5-year project suspension led to parts and equipment being stored onsite and at 75 locations worldwide."

===Phase II (Units 3 and 4): 2 x 660 MW===
Unit 3 was commissioned in November 2011 and Unit 4 was commissioned in January 2012. The units cost $2.1 billion.<ref name="GEO">[http://globalenergyobservatory.org/geoid/41518 "Tanjung Jati-B Coal Power Plant Indonesia,"] Global Energy Observatory, accessed December 2013</ref>

In August 2024, a fire broke out in the Phase II units.<ref>[https://jurnalhariankota.com/kebakaran-di-pltu-tanjung-jati-b-jepara-tidak-ada-korban-jiwa/ Kebakaran di PLTU Tanjung Jati B Jepara, Tidak Ada Korban Jiwa], Jurnal Hariankota, August 21, 2024</ref>

===Phase III (Units 5 and 6): 2 x 1000 MW===
A third phase of two 1000 MW units is described in PLN's long-range plan for 2013-2022. It is referred to as "PLTU Jawa-4 #5 and #6" and is slated for 2019 and 2020.
<ref name="LT">[http://energy-indonesia.com/03dge/0140317pln.pdf “PLN Long Term Electricity Plan (2013-2023),”] presentation by Moch. Sofyan, Head of New & Renewable Division of PT PLN (Persero), 06 March 2014, p. 11</ref><ref>Muhammad Oliez, [http://ekbis.sindonews.com/read/2013/12/03/34/812581/pltu-tanjung-jati-b-unit-5-dan-6-mendesak-dibangun "PLTU Tanjung Jati B unit 5 dan 6 mendesak dibangun" (Tanjung Jati B power plant units 5 and 6 urgent constructed),] SindNews.com, December 3, 2013</ref> 

In December 2013, the government of Jepara Regency renewed its push for the two units to be built. Outstanding issues that that point included lining up investors, land acquisition, building a new transmission line, and lining up government support.<ref>Muhammad Oliez. [http://ekbis.sindonews.com/read/812581/34/pltu-tanjung-jati-b-unit-5-dan-6-mendesak-dibangun-1386041087 PLTU Tanjung Jati B unit 5 dan 6 mendesak dibangun]. Sindo News, 3 Dec. 2013.</ref>

As of March 2015, the plant's proponents were holding public hearings as part of the EIA environmental permit application process. Sumitomo said it hoped to complete the units by 2019.<ref>[http://www.suaraonlineterkini.com/2015/03/konsultasi-publik-amdal-pembangunan-dan.html Konsultasi Publik AMDAL Pembangunan dan Pengoperasian Unit 5&6 PLTU TJB], Suara Online Terkini, 3 Mar. 2015.</ref>

PLN's long-range plan for 2016-2025 included Jawa-4 as a 2,000 MW addition in 2019.<ref name="LTP">[http://www.djk.esdm.go.id/pdf/RUPTL/RUPTL%20PLN%202016-2025.pdf “Rencana Usaha Penyediaan Tenaga Listrik, PT PLN (Persero), 2016-2025,”] Kementerian Energi Dan Sumber Daya Mineral, June 2016</ref> Sumitomo announced in December 2015 that a power purchase agreement had been signed for two units of 1,000 MW each. According to Sumitomo, the company along with Kansai Electric Power and PT United Tractors (an affiliate of Indonesian conglomerate Astra Group) signed the agreement with PT PLN (Persero) on December 21, 2015.<ref name="Sumo">[http://www.sumitomocorp.co.jp/english/news/detail/id=29092 "Tanjung Jati B coal-fired power plant Unit 5 & 6 Expansion Project (2,000MW),"] Sumitomo, December 21, 2015</ref>

In February 2016, RambuEnergy reported that an environmental impact study, also known as an "Amdal study," for the two projects had been underway since the previous year. The head of the Amdal study team said that the study might be completed by the end of February. Governor Pranowo said that growing electricity demand in Central Java made the project crucial. The RambuEnergy article described the units as 1,070 MW each and described the combustion technology as [[ultra-supercritical]]. According to the article, local NGOs were calling on the government to postpone the Amdal document. A spokesperson for the United Jepara Forum (Forum Jepara Bersatu/FJB) said that the document needed further clarity.<ref name="Rambu">[http://www.rambuenergy.com/2016/02/development-of-tanjung-jati-b-unit-5-6-in-central-java-drags-on/ "Development of Tanjung Jati B Unit 5 & 6 in Central Java drags on,"] RambuEnergy, February 24, 2016</ref>

The projects is a BOT (Build, Operate and Transfer) scheme of 25 years, after which it will be transfered to PT PLN. The total project cost is expected 500 billion yen, mainly funded by project finance.<ref name="Sumo">[http://www.sumitomocorp.co.jp/english/news/detail/id=29092 "Tanjung Jati B coal-fired power plant Unit 5 & 6 Expansion Project (2,000MW),"] Sumitomo, December 21, 2015</ref> In February 2017, the financing for the plant was US$3.355 billion.<ref name="jbic2-217">[https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2016/0227-53954 "Project Finance for Re-expansion of Tanjung Jati B Coal-Fired Power Plant in Indonesia,"] JBIC announcement, 27 February 2017</ref>

In March 2017, industri.bisnis.com reported the signing of a statement and guarantee document by PLN and BJP, described as a key part of the pre-financial close phase. PLN and BJB had previously. In December 2015 the two parties signed a power purchase agreement (PPA), and they amended the PPA in September 2016.<ref>[http://industri.bisnis.com/read/20170328/44/640693/pln-percepat-pembangunan-tanjung-jati-b- "PLN Accelerates Development of Tanjung Jati B,"] industri.bisnis.com, 28 March 2017</ref>

In August 2017 it was reported that construction had begun on the units, with completion planned for 2021.<ref>[https://en.tempo.co/read/news/2017/09/05/056906034/Jawa-4-Power-Plant-to-Begin-Operations-in-2021 "Jawa 4 Power Plant to Begin Operations in 2021,"] Tempo, Sep 5, 2017</ref> In August 2018 it was reported that construction was 32% complete.<ref>[http://jateng.tribunnews.com/2018/08/09/komang-berharap-pltu-tanjung-jati-b-unit-5-dan-6-rampung-2021 Komang Berharap PLTU Tanjung Jati B Unit 5 dan 6 Rampung 2021], Tribun Jateng, Aug. 9, 2018</ref> In May 2019 it was reported that construction was at 55%-60% and that Unit 5 and Unit 6 would be commissioned in September 2021.<ref>[https://www.suaramerdeka.com/news/baca/184069/pltu-tanjung-jati-b-jepara-siap-beri-pasokan-listrik-4640-mw PLTU Tanjung Jati B Jepara Siap Beri Pasokan Listrik 4,640 Mw], Suara Merdeka, May 16, 2019</ref> In July 2019 it was reported that construction of Unit 5 and Unit 6 was 75% complete.<ref>[https://semarang.bisnis.com/read/20190731/536/1131090/salip-paiton-tanjung-jati-b-siap-jadi-pltu-terbesar-di-indonesia Salip Paiton, Tanjung Jati B Siap Jadi PLTU Terbesar di Indonesia], Semarang, Jul. 31, 2019</ref>

In March 2020 the project's sponsor announced that it might be delayed as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref name="ko">[https://industri.kontan.co.id/news/jadwal-operasional-pembangkit-terganggu-wabah-corona-ini-tanggapan-pln?page=all Jadwal operasional pembangkit terganggu wabah corona, ini tanggapan PLN], Kontan, Mar. 8, 2020</ref> Construction of Units 5 and 6 was reportedly 93% complete as of May 31, 2020.<ref>https://market.bisnis.com/read/20200707/192/1262425/diadang-pandemi-tiga-emiten-kebut-penyelesaian-proyek-pembangkit-listrik Diadang Pandemi, Tiga Emiten Kebut Penyelesaian Proyek Pembangkit Listrik], Bisnis, Jul. 7, 2020</ref> In April 2021 it was reported that construction was behind schedule and would not be completed until early 2022.<ref>[https://investasi.kontan.co.id/news/operasi-komersial-pltu-tanjung-jati-diperkirakan-mundur-hingga-awal-2022 Operasi komersial PLTU Tanjung Jati diperkirakan mundur hingga awal 2022], Kontan, Apr. 9, 2021</ref> PLN supported the decision to delay operation, stating that the electrical grid was likely to face an oversupply if three major power generation facilities came online in 2021, including the Tanjung Jati B power station and the [[Central Java Power Project|Central Java Power Station]].<ref>[https://industri.kontan.co.id/news/ada-potensi-oversupply-pln-ingin-tunda-jadwal-cod-tiga-pembangkit-ini Ada potensi oversupply, PLN ingin tunda jadwal COD tiga pembangkit ini], Kontan, May 7, 2021</ref> In January 2022, the project was reported to be 99.8% complete but an exact commissioning date was not announced due to Covid-19-related uncertainties.<ref>[https://market.bisnis.com/read/20220109/192/1486913/soal-pltu-jawa-4-untr-masih-koordinasi-dengan-pln Regarding PLTU Jawa 4, UNTR is still coordinating with PLN], Bisnis, Jan. 9, 2022</ref>

In early 2023, Jawa-4 appeared listed as a 2022 achievement in a Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) report through the Directorate General of Electricity, but the commercial operation date was unclear.<ref>[https://voi.id/ekonomi/249884/progres-proyek-listrik-35-gw-baru-47-persen-hingga-desember-2022 "Progres Proyek Listrik 35 GW Baru 47 Persen hingga Desember 2022,"] VOI, Feb. 1, 2023</ref>

In April 2023, a PT Bhumi Jati Power company announcement stated that Units 5 and 6 achieved commercial operation in September 2022.<ref>[https://www.bhumi-jati.co.id/news/news-detail/announcement-of-new-president-director.html "Announcement of New President Director,"] Bhumi Jati Power, April 14, 2023</ref>

In April 2024, Phase III was included in a cost benefit analysis comparing early retirement with the use of carbon capture and storage technology. The analysis used 2047 as the planned retirement date for the units, which was the end of the units' power purchase agreement.<ref>[https://caseforsea.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Coals-Endgame-Early-Retirement-of-CFPP-vs-CCS-CASE-Indonesia.pdf Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) of Early Retirement Coal-Fired Power Plant (CFPP) versus CFPP with Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)], Institute for Essential Services Reform, March 2024</ref>

==Public opposition==

At a public hearing in Tubanan Village in March 2015, local fishermen spoke out strongly against the proposed plant. They argued that the company had failed to live up to the standards that it had set in the EIA for Units 3 & 4 in 2007. One complaint was that the plant's owners had failed to put a filter on the water intake as promised, with the result that small fish were getting sucked in and killed.<ref>[http://beritajateng.net/berita-jateng-terbaru-hari-ini/nelayan-jepara-tolak-pembangunan-unit-5-dan-6-pltu-jepara/16563 Nelayan Jepara Tolak Pembangunan Unit 5 dan 6 PLTU Jepara], Berita Jateng, 3 Mar. 2015.</ref>

In November 2023, local farmers held a demonstration in front of Tanjung Jati B power station. Nearby rice fields had reportedly become unsuitable for farming since the power station was constructed.<ref>[https://berita.murianews.com/faqih-mansur-hidayat/403435/breaking-news-petani-bondo-jepara-demo-pltu BREAKING NEWS: Petani Bondo Jepara Demo PLTU], Murianews.com, Nov. 19, 2023.</ref>

In December 2024, residents highlighted that the power station was negatively impacting the surrounding community. Beyond contributing to climate change, the operation of Tangjung Jati B was reportedly damaging local road infrastructure. However, they also acknowledged that the power station was providing many jobs.<ref>[https://gistara.com/2024/12/31/dampak-sosial-dan-lingkungan-pltu-tanjung-jati-b-bagi-masyarakat-setempat/ Dampak Sosial dan Lingkungan PLTU Tanjung Jati B bagi Masyarakat Setempat], Gistara, December 31, 2024</ref>

==Waste issues==

The plant has had problems with waste disposal. Waste was originally being moved out of the plant via truck, but locals complained that the trucks were damaging local roads. The company then started transporting waste by barge, but fishers were worried that leaking waste would impact fish stocks. The company has only a limited amount of space onsite to store waste, and was concerned that the plant would have to shut down.<ref>[http://citizen6.liputan6.com/read/589826/pltu-tanjung-jati-b-jepara-terancam-off PLTU Tanjung Jati B Jepara Terancam 'Off'], Liputan 6, 18 May 2013.</ref>

==Financing==

Financing for Phase II (Units 3&4) was closed in 2003. Financing was arranged by the Japan Bank for International Cooperation, the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation and the Tokyo Branch of BNP Paribas Bank. Approximately US$1.5 billion in loans was provided by thirteen financial institutions: Japan Bank for International Cooperation, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, BNP Paribas, MUFG Bank, Shinsei Bank, ING Group, Deutsche Bank, Societe Generale, Mizuho Financial Group, HSBC, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, WestLB, and Standard Chartered Bank.<ref>[http://web.archive.org/web/20160928114317/http://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2008/1230-7135 JBIC Provides Project Finance and Political Risk Guarantee for Tanjung Jati B Coal-Fired Power Plant Expansion Project in Indonesia], Japan Bank for International Cooperation, Dec. 30, 2008, Archived Sep. 28, 2016</ref><ref>[https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/30563/1320mw-tanjung-jati-b-coal-fired-power-plant-units-3-and-4 1320MW Tanjung Jati B Coal-fired Power Plant (Units 3 & 4)], IJGlobal, May 29, 2017</ref>

Financing for Phase III (Units 5&6) was closed in March 2017. US$3,355 million in loans will be provided by [[Japan Bank for International Cooperation]] (JBIC), MUFG Bank, Mizuho Bank, Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, OCBC Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Holdings, and Norinchukin Bank. Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI) provided insurance for the private bank loans. The financial advisor for the project is Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation<ref name="jbic2-217">[https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2016/0227-53954 "Project Finance for Re-expansion of Tanjung Jati B Coal-Fired Power Plant in Indonesia,"] JBIC announcement, 27 February 2017</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/34100/tanjung-jati-b-coal-fired-power-plant-units-5-and-6-ipp-2000mw|title=Preview of Tanjung Jati B Coal-Fired Power Plant (Units 5 & 6) IPP (2000MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-09-17}}</ref>. US$838.81 million in equity is being provided by Sumitomo Corporation, Kansai Electric Power, and PT United Tractors.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/34100/tanjung-jati-b-coal-fired-power-plant-units-5-and-6-ipp-2000mw|title=Preview of Tanjung Jati B Coal-Fired Power Plant (Units 5 & 6) IPP (2000MW) {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-09-17}}</ref>

==Coal==

For the existing plant, PLN concluded a coal deal in April 2017 with PT Indominco Mandiri and PT Kaltim Prima Coal (KPC) under which the plant will receive 4.8 million tonnes of coal per year for 5 years. The coal is 5,500-5,700 kcal/kg, i.e. [[bituminous]] coal. Units 5 and 6 will require an additional 7 million tonnes per year.<ref>Michael Agustinus, [https://finance.detik.com/energi/3501988/pasokan-batu-bara-untuk-pltu-tanjung-jati-b-dipastikan-aman "Pasokan Batu Bara untuk PLTU Tanjung Jati B Dipastikan Aman,"] delikFinance, 16 May 2017</ref>

==Background==

The 2009 agreement between the Government of Mongolia and the companies developing the Oyu Tolgoi copper project outlined two possible long term power options. One was a coal-fired power station which supplied power to the mine complex, and the other was a coal-fired power station within the mine lease area of the project. (See [[Oyu Tolgoi Investment Agreement and power supply]] for more details on the provisions of the agreement). Oyo Tolgoi is currently sourcing power from China and wants a domestic power supply by the second half of 2017.<ref name=TTunit>[http://ttpp.mn/1/single_news/2/eng "About project"], Tavan Tolgoi Power Plant project website, accessed June 2014.</ref> Ahead of the full commissioning of the mine the Oyo Tolgoi consortium was importing power from the Chinese grid.)

In early 2012 Energy Director T. Tserenpurev of the Mongolian Ministry of Mineral Resources and Energy stated that a power plant at Tavan Tolgoi would not only supply the Oyu Tolgoi mine but "also provide electricity to the Tsagaansuvarg deposit, mines of SouthGobi Sands, Chinhua MAK, Mongolyn Alt and such. The demand will be so huge that importing electricity will be no solution. We must be self-sufficient and developing the domestic electricity sector will also create employment opportunities."<ref name=water>[http://en.mongolianminingjournal.com/content/19084.shtml "Energy Ministry prefers Tavan Tolgoi as site for power plant"], ''Mongolian Mining Journal'', March 3, 2012.</ref>

In July 2013 the Oyu Tolgoi mine reached full production capacity.<ref>Rio Tinto, [http://www.riotinto.com/documents/RT_Annual_report_2013.pdf "2013 Annual Report"], Rio Tinto, March 2014, page 28.</ref> In October 2013 Bloomberg reported that the Mongolian the Ministry of Energy had developed a short-list of companies for the project including Marubeni Corporation, Daewoo Engineering & Construction Company, Kansai Electric Power Company, [[GDF Suez]], and Posco Energy Corporation. No date was announced by the Ministry of Energy for the announcement of the selected bidder.<ref>Michael Kohn and Yuriy Humber, [http://www.bloomberg.com/news/2013-10-15/marubeni-gdf-suez-among-final-bidders-for-mongolia-power-plant.html "Marubeni, GDF Suez Among Final Bidders for Mongolia Power Plant"], ''Bloomberg'', October 15, 2013.</ref> The proposed plant was reported to be 450 MW for Phase 1, 600 MW in Phase 2, and possibly up to 1200 MW total.<ref>[http://www.asiaminer.com/news/archive/140-2013/march-2013/5038-mongolia-wanted-investors-to-fund-ot-power-plant.html#.U7cH37EwCnQ "MONGOLIA - Wanted: Investors to fund OT power plant"], ''Asia Miner'', March 2013.</ref>

In April 2015, the parliament cancelled a deal with a consortium of foreign firms, including China's Shenhua Energy and Japan's Sumitomo Corp., interested in developing the Tavan Tolgoi mine. In July 2015 Mongolia representatives said it was considering the sale of its stakes in 10 state-owned companies, including part of its US$4 billion Tavan Tolgoi mine. Tavan Tolgoi has coking coal deposit used in steelmaking, with reserves estimated at 7.4 billion tonnes.<ref>Cecilia Jamasmie, [http://webcache.googleusercontent.com/search?q=cache:9yQa7Ea5NxEJ:www.mining.com/mongolia-to-sell-stake-in-its-giant-tavan-tolgoi-coal-mine/+&cd=2&hl=en&ct=clnk&gl=us "Mongolia to sell stake in its giant Tavan Tolgoi coal mine,"] Mining.com, July 6, 2015</ref> 

It is unclear what this means for the proposed power station. In May 2015 the Mongolia government and Rio Tinto agreed to terms for moving forward with the Oyu Tolgoi gold and copper mine in Mongolia, which would include purchasing power from the Tavan Tolgoi power station, as the proposed [[Oyu Tolgoi power station]] was shelved as the Oyu mine negotiations stalled for two years.<ref>[http://www.marketwired.com/press-release/turquoise-hill-provides-additional-details-on-oyu-tolgoi-underground-mine-development-nyse-trq-2020909.htm "Turquoise Hill Provides Additional Details on Oyu Tolgoi Underground Mine Development and Financing Plan,"] Market Wired, May 18, 2015</ref>

In February 2016 Japan’s Marubeni Corporation was awarded the 450 MW Tavan Tolgoi Power Plant project tender. Feasibility studies have been submitted.<ref>[http://mad-intelligence.com/japans-marubeni-wins-tavan-tolgoi-power-plant-investment-tender/ "Japan’s Marubeni wins Tavan Tolgoi Power Plant investment tender,"] MAD, March 3, 2016</ref> The company will finance the plant, making it Mongolia's first IPP. The plant is planned for operation in 2023.<ref>Khaliun Chimeddorj, [http://theubpost.mn/2016/06/27/investment-agreement-signed-for-tavan-tolgoi-power-plant/ "Investment agreement signed for Tavan Tolgoi power plant,"] UB Post, June 27, 2016</ref> 

In 2017 it was reported the plant may be eventually be expanded by an additional 150 MW unit to support the [[Oyu Tolgoi]] mine,<ref name=bank>[http://bankwatch.org/sites/default/files/Mongolia-energy-sector-web.pdf "Mongolia's Energy Sector,"] Bankwatch, April 2017</ref> but in February 2018 it was reported the Government of Mongolia no longer viewed the Tavan Tolgoi Power Project as a viable option for Oyu Tolgoi, which will have to find its own domestic power source.<ref>[http://www.riotinto.com/media/media-releases-237_24270.aspx "Rio Tinto committed to domestic power solution for Oyu Tolgoi,"] Rio Tinto, February 16, 2018</ref> 

In February 2018 it was reported that the Tavan Tolgoi project lacked a lead investor, which made it unable to secure financing.<ref>[https://www.ft.com/content/c71e5604-1895-11e8-9376-4a6390addb44 "Rio to build power station at copper, gold mine in Mongolia,"] FT, February 23, 2018</ref><ref>[https://www.pressreader.com/mongolia/the-ub-post/20180226/281513636641707 "Oyu Tolgoi considering forgoing Tavan Tolgoi power,"] PressReader, February 26, 2018</ref>

In December 2018 Rio Tinto announced the signing of a Power Source Framework Agreement (PSFA) between Rio Tinto and the Government of Mongolia, the [[Tavan Tolgoi power station (Rio Tinto)]]. Under the agreement, a 300 megawatt coal plant will be majority owned by Rio's Oyu Tolgoi LLC and will be situated close to the Tavan Tolgoi coalfields. Construction is scheduled to start in 2020 following studies, with the commissioning of the plant by mid-2023.<ref name =RioTinto>[http://www.riotinto.com/media/media-releases-237_26605.aspx "Oyu Tolgoi power solution progresses,"] Rio Tinto press release, December 31, 2018</ref> <ref>Oyu Tolgoi, [http://ot.mn/the-ttpp-power-source-framework-agreement-signed/ "The TTPP Power Source Framework Agreement signed"], Media Release, December 31, 2018.</ref> 

The [[Tavan Tolgoi power station (Rio Tinto)]] likely supplanted plans for the original Tavan Tolgoi coal plant by Marubeni, although this has not been made official.

==Location debate==

Tserenpurev stated that the government wanted to quickly push ahead with building a coal-fired power station at Tavan Tolgoi to obviate the need for power imports from China for the mine as soon as possible. Tserenpurev indicated that, while a power station in the Tavan Tolgoi area was their preferred option, that they had been advised that "water could be a problem in Tavan Tolgoi."<ref name=water>[http://en.mongolianminingjournal.com/content/19084.shtml "Energy Ministry prefers Tavan Tolgoi as site for power plant"], ''Mongolian Mining Journal'', March 3, 2012.</ref>

Odon Sainbuyan, the Executive Director of Erdenes MGL, a government-owned company with shares in both Oyu Tolgoi and Taban Tolgoi, explained that another factor in the government favouring the power station being located at Tavan Tolgoi was that it would avoid the need to transport coal. "If the power station is located at Oyu Tolgoi then the coal will need to be transported to the project site. If it’s at Tavan Tolgoi, there will be no need to ship any coal. It’s more economical, logical and efficient,” he said.<ref>Michael Kohn, [http://www.businessweek.com/news/2013-03-13/mongolia-seeks-investors-for-thermal-plant-to-power-oyu-tolgoi "Mongolia Seeks Investors for Thermal Plant to Power Oyu Tolgoi"], ''Bloomberg'', March 13, 2013.</ref>

==Financing==

*'''Source of financing:''' Marubeni (US$300 million - 30% project costs)<ref name=bank>[http://bankwatch.org/sites/default/files/Mongolia-energy-sector-web.pdf "Mongolia's Energy Sector,"] Bankwatch, April 2017</ref>
On July 3, 2014, the Government of Mongolia resolved to provide US$50 million in the form of mezzanine financing to the project. Government financing will not exceed 1/3 of the equity of the project.<ref>[http://www.infomongolia.com/ct/ci/8082 "Government of Mongolia and Oyu Tolgoi LLC to Establish an Agreement of Cooperation in Energy Sector in Southern Gobi Region,"] InfoMongolia.com, July 3, 2014</ref>

In February 2016 Japan’s Marubeni Corporation was awarded the 450 MW Tavan Tolgoi Power Plant project tender. The company will finance the plant, making it Mongolia's first IPP. The developer has to provide 30 per cent of the USD 1 billion estimated costs while the other 70 per cent has to be secured from international finance.<ref name=bank>[http://bankwatch.org/sites/default/files/Mongolia-energy-sector-web.pdf "Mongolia's Energy Sector,"] Bankwatch, April 2017</ref> 

Following Rio Tinto's December 2018 announcement of its agreement with the Government of Mongolia for a 300 MW plant<ref name =RioTinto>[http://www.riotinto.com/media/media-releases-237_26605.aspx "Oyu Tolgoi power solution progresses,"] Rio Tinto press release, December 31, 2018</ref>, ''Reuters'' reported that in July 2018 Rio Tinto had entered into "agreements with three Chinese contractors on designing a power station to supply Oyu Tolgoi". While ''Reuters'' reported a spokesman for Rio Tinto "declined to comment on the status of those tenders", the article was silent on the question of whether Chinese finance would be involved.<ref>Barbara Lewis and Munkhchimeg Davaasharav, [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-riotinto-mongolia/rio-tinto-mongolia-sign-power-deal-for-oyu-tolgoi-copper-mine-idUKKCN1OU0QL "Rio Tinto, Mongolia sign power deal for Oyu Tolgoi copper mine"], ''Reuters'', January 1, 2019.</ref> 

Shortly after Rio Tinto's announcement, it was reported that Mongolia is proposing to raise up to US$3 billion in on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange by selling a 30 per cent stake of the publicly-owned coal mining company [[Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi]]. The company’s Chief Executive, Gankhuyag Battulga, stated the proceeds would be used to fund the Tavan Tolgoi coal plant.<ref>Haliun Bayartsogt, [https://asia.nikkei.com/Business/Markets/Mongolian-state-coal-miner-chooses-Hong-Kong-for-3bn-IPO "Mongolian state coal miner chooses Hong Kong for $3bn IPO"], ''Nikkei Asian Review''', January 10, 2019.</ref>

==Water concerns==

While building a mine-mouth power station would obviate the need to transport coal, there were concerns about the availability of water. Tserenpurev said:<ref name=water>[http://en.mongolianminingjournal.com/content/19084.shtml "Energy Ministry prefers Tavan Tolgoi as site for power plant"], ''Mongolian Mining Journal'', March 3, 2012.</ref> 

:"There is underground water but this will be needed for the coal washing plant. There may still be enough for the power plant and we have not taken any firm decision to shift it from Tavan Tolgoi. Indeed, we would like to stick to the original plan but the whole water issue needs careful re-evaluation."

The Government of Mongolia, via the Ministry of Energy, has called for tenders on the option of building a 450 MW power station near one of the operating coal mines in the Tavan Tolgoi coal field and constructing a transmission approximately 150 kilometres to the Oyu Tolgoi mine. The website of the Tavan Tolgoi Power Plant project unit states that the Government of Mongolia has "entered into a Cooperation Agreement" with Oyu Tolgoi, [[Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi]] and the privately-owned [[Energy Resources ]], a subsidiary of MCS for the development of the Project. While the plant is initially aimed at having a capacity of 450MW, Oyu Tolgoi want the plant to have the option of being expanded to 600MW.<ref name=TTunit>[http://ttpp.mn/1/single_news/2/eng "About project"], Tavan Tolgoi Power Plant project website, accessed June 2014.</ref>

==Background==

===Ownership===
Alabama Power (a Southern Co. subsidiary) plans to purchase Tenaska’s Lindsay Hill power station for USD 622 million. Alabama Power has already filed for approval with the Alabama Public Service Commission and estimates the deal may increase residential bills by about USD 3.80/month. Alabama Power’s move to acquire the Lindsay Hill plant is aimed at closing a projected capacity gap and enhancing winter reliability. However, the deal is facing regulatory pushback over concerns about monopolistic control and possible cost impacts to customers. Both FERC and the PSC are now evaluating competition, cost, and environmental considerations. Environmental and public-interest groups (Energy Alabama, GASP, Public Citizen) have urged FERC to reject the deal, citing market power concerns and the lack of evidence that Alabama Power will not raise rates or cross-subsidize affiliated entities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.utilitydive.com/news/alabama-power-tenaska-lindsay-hill-ferc-psc/739639/|title=Alabama Power’s $622M deal to buy Tenaska power plant faces challenge at FERC|date=February 11, 2025|website=Utility Dive|url-status=live|access-date=June 30, 2025}}</ref>

==Background==

Appendix II of Vietnam's 2011-20 National Master Plan for Power Development, approved in July 2011, lists a two-unit, 1,200-MW coal-fired power plant in Bạc Liêu province, to be constructed by 2028.<ref>[http://www.moit.gov.vn/Images/Upload/QD%201208-TTg.pdf Quyết định phê duyệt Quy hoạch phát triển điện lực quốc gia giai đoạn 2011 - 2020 có xét đến năm 2030] (Approval of the National Master Plan for Power Development for the 2011-2020 Period with Vision to 2030), Prime Minister of Vietnam, Statement No. 1208/QD-TTg, July 21, 2011, Appendix II, p. 3.</ref> The Revised Power Development Plan VII lists the project as coming online in 2029/2030 in case renewable energy projects cannot meet the planned schedule. <ref>DANH MỤC CÁC DỰ ÁN NGUỒN ĐIỆN VÀO VẬN HÀNH GIAI ĐOẠN 2016 - 2030, Ban hành kèm theo Quyết định số 428/QĐ-TTg ngày 18 tháng 3 năm 2016 của Thủ tướng Chính phủ (''LIST OF POWER PROJECT IN OPERATION PERIOD 2016 - 2030, Issued together with Decision No. 428 / QD - TTg of March 18, 2016 by the Prime Minister'')</ref>

In February 2015, representatives of Sojitz Kyushu Corporation (a subsidiary of Japanese firm [[Sojitz]]) met with Bac Lieu provincial officials and [[EVN]] representatives to discuss initial preparations for the project.<ref name=baobaclieu>[http://baobaclieu.vn/newsdetails/1D3FE183D9F/UBND_tinh_tiep_va_lam_viec_voi_dai_dien_Cong_ty_Kyushu_va_Sojitz_ve_du_an_Trung_tam_Dien_luc_Bac_Lieu.aspx UBND tỉnh tiếp và làm việc với đại diện Công ty Kyushu và Sojitz về dự án Trung tâm Điện lực Bạc Liêu], Bac Lieu Online, 12 Feb. 2015.</ref>

In September 2016, the provincial governor stated that, given that the province's priority being on promoting the growth of the intensive shrimp farming industry, the environmental risk is too great to justify building the Cái Cùng coal power plant.<ref>[http://baodatviet.vn/chinh-tri-xa-hoi/tin-tuc-thoi-su/bac-lieu-choi-nhiet-dien-than-nhat-ban-lam-van-khong-chon-3319596/ Bạc Liêu chối nhiệt điện than: Nhật Bản làm, vẫn không chọn], Bao Dat Viet, 30 Sept. 2016.</ref> The provincial leaders recommended a greater emphasis on wind and other clean power sources as an alternative to the "Brown economy."<ref>[http://endcoal.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/VSEA-NCDs-Press-release-on-Bac-Lieu_2309.pdf "Press Release,"] Vietnam Sustainable Energy Alliance and Vietnam Non-Communicable Diseases Alliance, September 23, 2016.</ref>

In March 2017, provincial officials asked the central government to take the Cái Cùng plant out of their national plan.<ref>[http://www.thiennhien.net/2017/03/20/bac-lieu-xin-loai-du-nhiet-dien-cai-cung-khoi-quy-hoach/ Bạc Liêu xin loại dự án nhiệt điện Cái Cùng khỏi quy hoạch], ThienNhien.net, 20 Mar. 2017.</ref>

==Plans for Renewable Energy==

With a coastline of 56 km, strong and stable winds, and almost year-around sunshine, Bạc Liêu province is well situated for both solar and wind power development. Currently, the province has a 99.2 MW wind power plant invested in by Cong Ly Construction Trade Tourism Company Limited, reportedly the largest wind power facility in the country. 

On November 5, 2017, a cooperation contract was signed between the Long Điền Đông commune and Group SY (a Korean corporation) to deploy a 300 MW solar power plant on the 400-hectare location that had been previously allocated for the power plant. According to the agreement, the project will begin with a first phase of 50 MW from 2017 to June 2019. If developed, it will be the largest solar facility in Vietnam. In addition to the Group SY project, a second solar power project of 150 MW has been proposed by Kimin Group (UK), comprising a first phase of 40 MW and a second phase of 110 MW. UPC Renewables Company (USA) has also also conducted preliminary work to develop a wind power facility, with 50 MW in the first phase and 150 MW in the second phase.<ref name=renew>[http://nld.com.vn/kinh-te/bac-lieu-huong-den-nang-luong-sach-20171106220353441.htm "Bạc Liêu hướng đến năng lượng sạch,"] Người Lao Động, 7 November 2017</ref>

==Plans for gas==

In May 2018, US-based company Energy Capital Vietnam signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) for a 3200 megawatt (MW) LNG-fired plant in Bac Lieu Province, as an alternative to a proposed coal plant.<ref>Viet Phong, [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/business/pm-talks-up-mekong-delta-potential-for-gas-fired-power-plants-3783967.html "PM talks up Mekong Delta potential for gas-fired power plants,"] Vien Express, July 27, 2018</ref>

==Background==

Trumbull Energy Center is an independent, dual-fuel combined-cycle gas turbine facility with a maximum design capacity of 950 MW, located in Lordstown, Ohio. Operating within PJM's ATSI zone, this power station achieved financial close in November 2023 with a targeted Commercial Operation Date of Jan 31, 2026. Trumbull Energy Center stands on contributions from three equity sponsors: Korea Southern Power Company (KOSPO), Siemens Energy, and Korea Overseas Infrastructure and Urban Development (KIND).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/company/trumbull-energy-center/|title=Trumbull Energy Center, LLC|website=LinkedIn|url-status=live|access-date=June 12, 2024}}</ref> The first turbine for the project was delivered by Siemens in October 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://businessjournaldaily.com/first-turbine-delivered-to-trumbull-energy-center-site/|title=First Turbine Delivered to Trumbull Energy Center Site|date=November 6, 2023|website=businessjournaldaily.com|url-status=live|access-date=June 12,2 2024}}</ref> In June 2025, it was reported that the Trumbull Energy Center had completed multiple phases of construction and was transitioning to the final phase, which consists of equipment installation, commissioning, and testing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dis.puc.state.oh.us/DocumentRecord.aspx?DocID=9477d3fd-a073-463c-9b21-b14b2977a22e|title=Document Record|date=2025-06-27|website=dis.puc.state.oh.us|url-status=live|access-date=2025-11-19}}</ref>

==Background==

Guam has no natural gas reserves and does not produce or use natural gas. The Guam Power Authority plans to have a new 198-MW power plant in service that is capable of burning either imported ultra-low sulfur diesel fuel or liquefied natural gas (LNG) that is regasifed to generate electricity. The new plant will enable the utility to comply with U.S. federal environmental requirements to release fewer greenhouse emissions while using either fuel.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/state/print.php?sid=GQ|title=Guam Territory Energy Profile|date=March 21, 2024|website=EIA|url-status=live|access-date=June 12, 2024}}</ref>

In March 2024, the Guam Power Authority proposed paying an additional USD 5 million to the contractor for the Ukudu power plant to expedite the completion of the new plant. According to the schedule, the contractor, Guam Ukudu Power, was expected to have the plant operational by January 2026 at the earliest. However, the increased payment will accelerate the completion date to September 2025. The original completion date was set for the end of 2024, but the project was delayed due to damage caused by Typhoon Mawar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.guampdn.com/news/gpa-wants-to-pay-5m-to-speed-up-ukudu-power-plant-completion/article_f31ef236-e751-11ee-985b-479300087767.html|title=GPA wants to pay $5M to speed up Ukudu power plant completion|date=March 21, 2024|website=www.guampdn.com|url-status=live|access-date=June 12, 2024}}</ref> The same month, the Guam's Consolidated Commission on Utilities approved the deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://energycentral.com/news/ccu-approves-5m-plan-accelerate-ukudu-power-plant-completion|title=CCU approves $5M plan to accelerate Ukudu power plant completion|date=March 27, 2024|website=energycentral.com|url-status=live|access-date=June 12, 2024}}</ref>

==Background==

In January 2011, the Van Phong Economic Zone Management Authority approved a plan by the [[Sumitomo Corporation]] to build the two-unit, $2 billion, 1,320-MW, coal-fired Vân Phong-1, as part of a port-industrial complex being planned in Vân Phong Bay.<ref>[http://www.vir.com.vn/news/en/coverage/green-light-for-van-phong-projects.html Green Light for Van Phong Projects], ''Vietnam Investment Review'', Jan. 16, 2011.</ref> In November 2012, with only site clearing completed, the Vietnamese government urged Sumitomo to line up investors by June 2013 or risk having the project ceded to other investors.<ref>[http://www.vinacomin.vn/en/news/Home-News/Power-investors-set-to-enter-last-chance-saloon-386.html Power Investors Set to Enter Last Chance Saloon], Vinacomin website, Nov. 26, 2012.</ref> 

In August 2013, Sumitomo contracted Finnish company [[Pöyry]] to build the plant.<ref>[http://www.poyry.com/news-events/news/poyry-awarded-owners-engineer-services-assignment-van-phong-1-coal-fired-power Pöyry Awarded Owner's Engineer Services Assignment for Van Phong 1 Coal-Fired Power Plant Project in Vietnam], Pöyry press release, Aug. 1, 2013.</ref> As of November 2013, however, Sumitomo was still having trouble with negotiations with the Vietnamese government; the current plan is for construction to begin in April 2015, and for the plant to go online in 2019.<ref>[http://www.vir.com.vn/news/en/corporate/sumitomo-red-tape-tangle-delays-power-plant-project.html Sumitomo Red Tape Tangle Delays Power Plant Project], ''Vietnam Investment Review'', Nov. 25, 2013.</ref> However, this timeline involved Sumitomo signing a BOT contract in early 2014, and getting the final license in July 2014; as of November 2014, though, the BOT contract had not yet been finalized.<ref>[http://vietnamnews.vn/economy/262956/red-tape-thwarts-energy-investors.html Red tape thwarts energy investors], Viet Nam News, 19 Nov. 2014.</ref>

As of April 2016, Sumitomo was having trouble with compensation, and some families were still living on the project's site.<ref>[http://www.baokhanhhoa.com.vn/kinh-te/201604/du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-van-phong-1-chua-the-khoi-cong-2430128/ Dự án Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Vân Phong 1: Chưa thể khởi công], Bao Khanh Hoa, 4 Apr. 2016.</ref> In July 2016, Sumitomo negotiated the location of a transmission line with provincial officials.<ref>[http://www.khpc.com.vn/Chitiettin/tabid/65/id/324/Du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-BOT-Van-Phong-1/Default.aspx Dự án nhà máy nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1], EVN Khanh Hoa press release, 5 July 2016.</ref> In August 2016, the provincial premier met with the Ministry of Industry & Trade to push for the acceleration of the project. At the time, the schedule called for construction by the end of 2017, and completion in 2021.<ref>[http://vanphong.khanhhoa.gov.vn/article/tin-van/khoi-sac-o-nam-van-phong.html Khởi sắc ở Nam Vân Phong], Van Phong Economic Zone website, 2 Nov. 2016.</ref>

In a March 2017 meeting with provincial officials, Sumitomo said its schedule was to apply for investment certificates by the end of June, and to begin construction by the end of the year.<ref>[http://baocongthuong.com.vn/nhiet-dien-van-phong-1-se-khoi-cong-cuoi-nam-2017.html Nhiệt điện Vân Phong 1 sẽ khởi công cuối năm 2017], Cong Thuong, 2 Mar. 2017.</ref>

In May 2017, Sumitomo signed and investment agreement with the Ministry of Industry and Trade, and December 2017 the company received an investment certificate to development the plant. Work will start in 2018.<ref>[http://english.vietnamnet.vn/fms/business/191494/japanese-firm-gets-nod-to-build-us-2-58-billion-thermal-power-plant.html "Japanese firm gets nod to build US$2.58-billion thermal power plant,"] Vietnam.net, 4 December 2017</ref>

In March 2018, the environmental impact assessment was approved.<ref name=mfmar>[https://www.marketforces.org.au/research/vietnam/van-phong-1/ "Van Phong 1 (1320 MW),"] Market Forces, updated March 24, 2018</ref>

In June 2019 the completion date for Unit 1 was delayed to 2023 and the completion date for Unit 2 was delayed to 2024 in the Ministry Of Industry And Trade's report on the implementation of the revised seventh Power Development Plan (PDP7).<ref>[http://vepg.vn/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/MOIT_Report_58_BC_BCT.pdf Implementation of Power Projects iIn the Revised Power Development Plan 7], Ministry of Industry and Trade, Republic of Vietnam, Jun. 4, 2019</ref>

In August 2019 Sumitomo announced that construction of Vân Phong-1 had begun.<ref>[https://www.sumitomocorp.com/en/jp/news/release/2019/group/12310 Construction Commences on Van Phong 1 Coal-fired Power Project in Vietnam], Sumitomo Corporation, Aug. 26, 2019</ref> However satellite photography from [https://www.planet.com/stories/van-phong-1-power-station-az2Ew2yWR Planet] shows only ground-clearing occurring between July 2019 and December 2019, not actual construction. As of December 2019 GreenID continued to list the plant as Permitted.<ref>Communication with GreenID, December 2019</ref> In February 2020 the National Steering Committee on power development stated that Unit 1 was scheduled to be commissioned in November 2023 and Unit 2 in March 2024.<ref name=vl>[http://nangluongvietnam.vn/news/vn/dien-luc-viet-nam/tinh-hinh-thuc-hien-cac-du-an-dien-theo-hinh-thuc-bot-o-viet-nam.html Tình hình thực hiện các dự án điện theo hình thức BOT ở Việt Nam], Feb. 14, 2020</ref> In May 2020 it was reported that engineering plans and the procurement of supplies and materials from China are being delayed because of Covid-19-related travel restrictions and logistical problems.<ref name=bdt>[https://baodauthau.vn/dau-tu/covid19-tac-dong-toi-tien-do-nhieu-du-an-dien-128323.html Covid-19 tác động tới tiến độ nhiều dự án điện], Bao Dau Thau, May 6, 2020</ref>

In April 2021, construction began on the steel structure for Van Phong-1 Unit 1's coal-fired boiler. Lilama 18 Joint Stock Company is the contractor in charge of installing 2 boilers, each with capacity of 660 MW, and each with a contract value of USD 28.6 million.<ref>[https://congthuong.vn/khoi-cong-lap-dat-ket-cau-thep-lo-hoi-so-1-du-an-nhiet-dien-van-phong-1-155723.html Commencement of installation of steel structure for boiler No. 1 of Van Phong 1 điện thermal power project], Báo Công Thương, Apr. 20, 2021</ref>

According to PDP7, phase I of the project is scheduled for completion in 2022 and 2023. Phase II of the project is cancelled.<ref name=PDP>DANH MỤC CÁC DỰ ÁN NGUỒN ĐIỆN VÀO VẬN HÀNH GIAI ĐOẠN 2016 - 2030, Ban hành kèm theo Quyết định số 428/QĐ-TTg ngày 18 tháng 3 năm 2016 của Thủ tướng Chính phủ (''LIST OF POWER PROJECT IN OPERATION PERIOD 2016 - 2030, Issued together with Decision No. 428 / QD - TTg of March 18, 2016 by the Prime Minister'')</ref>

On July 4, 2022, the Ministry of Industry and Trade appeared to provide an update on the draft PDP. The document’s list of major power projects planned for 2021-2030 (PDF pages 18-20) includes the project with target completion dates of 2023 and 2024 for units 1 and 2 respectively. Construction was reportedly 70.52% complete.<ref>[https://ia601508.us.archive.org/4/items/pdp-8-jul-22/PDP8%20-%20jul%2022.pdf “Draft National Power Development Plan VIII,”] MOIT, July 4, 2022</ref>

In October 2022, the project's related substation and transmission lines were reportedly nearing completion. According to scheduling approved by the project's investors, these elements must be finished by December 26, 2022.<ref>[https://www.evn.com.vn/d6/news/Cum-cong-trinh-giai-toa-cong-suat-Nha-may-Nhiet-dien-BOT-Van-Phong-1-Nuoc-rut-ve-dich-6-13-31328.aspx “Cụm công trình giải tỏa công suất Nhà máy Nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1: ‘Nước rút’ về đích,”] EVN, October 3, 2022</ref>

In December 2022, the project was reportedly 87% complete. Commercial operation for Units 1 and 2 was expected in August 2023 and December 2023 respectively.<ref>[https://tuoitre.vn/thang-8-2023-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-van-phong-1-chinh-thuc-phat-dien-thuong-mai-20221218094256842.htm “Tháng 8-2023, Nhà máy nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1 chính thức phát điện thương mại,”] TuoiTre, December 18, 2022</ref>

In May 2023, Vietnam officially approved the updated power development plan (PDP8). Under this plan, the country will domestically generate 20% of its electricity needs with coal by 2030 and fully phase out coal-fired power stations by 2050. The plan involved increasing energy generation using coal to a peak of 30 GW and replacing all other outstanding coal projects with LNG or renewables. PDP8 listed Van Phong I among the projects under construction, with an updated capacity of 1,432 MW.<ref>[https://media.licdn.com/dms/document/D561FAQGybqltmh4EvA/feedshare-document-pdf-analyzed/0/1684231974788?e=1684972800&v=beta&t=PweOeGMVDy7VIQ2LFiSwUZPv9fwqhx2v7mtSCqnSChg Approving the national electricity development plan for the period of 2021-2030, with a vision to 2050], Prime Minister of Vietnam, May 16, 2023</ref> 

In September 2023, construction of Unit 1 was completed. Final inspection work was underway to prepare for commercial operation.<ref>[https://www.erav.vn/tin-tuc/t2672/du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-van-phong-1-chap-thuan-ket-qua-nghiem-thu-hoan-thanh-cua-chu-dau-tu-doi-voi-to-may-so-1-va-cac-hang-muc-dung-chung.html “Dự án Nhà máy nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1: Chấp thuận kết quả nghiệm thu hoàn thành của Chủ đầu tư đối với Tổ máy số 1 và các hạng mục dùng chung,”] Cục Điều tiết điện lực, September 17, 2023</ref>

===Operation begins===
In October 2023, Unit 1 was approved for commercial operation. In December 2023, Unit 2 was approved for commercial operation. Unit 1 was officially inaugurated in December 2023.<ref>[https://baoxaydung.com.vn/hoi-dong-chap-thuan-ket-qua-nghiem-thu-hoan-thanh-du-an-nha-may-nhiet-dien-van-phong-1-367510.html "Hội đồng chấp thuận kết quả nghiệm thu hoàn thành dự án Nhà máy Nhiệt điện Vân Phong 1,"] Báo điện tử Xây dựng, December 30, 2023</ref> Unit 2 was officially inaugurated in March 2024.<ref>[https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/2-5b-thermal-power-plant-goes-online-in-central-vietnam-4722421.html "$2.5B thermal power plant goes online in central Vietnam,"] VnExpress, March 14, 2024</ref>

In August 2024, a contract was signed for major repairs to Unit 1 of Van Phong power station.<ref>[http://pvps.vn/du-an/10798/pvps-ky-ket-hop-dong-cung-cap-dich-vu-sua-chua-lon---cap-do-b-cho-to-may-so-1-nam-2024-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-van-phong-1-cong-suat-tinh-1320-mw.html "PVPS ký kết Hợp đồng cung cấp dịch vụ sửa chữa lớn - cấp độ B cho Tổ máy số 1 năm 2024 Nhà máy nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1 công suất tinh 1.320 MW,"] PetroVietnam Power Services, August 12, 2024</ref> In October 2024, construction began. In November 2024, the repairs were completed.<ref>[https://petrovietnam.petrotimes.vn/pv-power-services-hoan-thanh-sua-chua-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-van-phong-1-trong-26-ngay-721359.html PV Power Services hoàn thành sửa chữa Nhà máy Nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1 trong 26 ngày], PetroTimes, November 30, 2024</ref>

In May 2025, Sumitomo announced intention to transfer a 50% stake in Van Phong Power Company to an undisclosed entity.<ref>[https://doanhnhan.baophapluat.vn/sumitomo-chuyen-nhuong-50-co-phan-tai-du-an-nhiet-dien-van-phong-1-82768.html Sumitomo chuyển nhượng 50% cổ phần tại dự án Nhiệt điện Vân Phong 1], Báo Mới, May 6, 2025</ref>

As of July 2025, Vân Phong-1 was reportedly not operating at full capacity.<ref>[https://tapchicongthuong.vn/thu-truong-nguyen-hoang-long-tham-va-lam-viec-voi-nha-may-nhiet-dien-bot-van-phong-1-150424.htm Thứ trưởng Nguyễn Hoàng Long thăm và làm việc với Nhà máy nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1], Tạp chí Công Thương, July 23, 2025</ref>

In September 2025, Vietnam’s Ministry of Finance proposed exempting the foreign owners of seven coal power plants from the requirement to pay a 15% global minimum corporate tax rate set by the OECD. The list of coal plants, which were developed under “build-operate-transfer” (BOT) contracts, included [https://www.gem.wiki/Mong_Duong_power_station Mông Dương-2], [https://www.gem.wiki/Vinh_Tan_power_station Vĩnh Tân-1], [https://www.gem.wiki/Nghi_Son_coal_power_station Nghi Sơn-2], Vân Phong-1, [https://www.gem.wiki/Vung_Ang_power_station Vũng Áng-2], [[Hai Duong Thermal Power Plant]], and [https://www.gem.wiki/Duyen_Hai_Power_Generation_Complex Duyên Hải-2].<ref>[https://vneconomy.vn/de-xuat-mien-tru-thue-toi-thieu-toan-cau-cho-du-an-bot-dien-co-bao-lanh-chinh-phu.htm “Đề xuất miễn trừ thuế tối thiểu toàn cầu cho dự án BOT điện có bảo lãnh Chính phủ,”] VnEconomy, September 11, 2025</ref> The Ministry argued that imposing the 15% minimum tax could trigger compensation obligations that “would expose the Vietnamese government to the risk of having to pay compensation that exceeds the tax revenues.”<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/vietnam-exempt-mitsubishi-kepco-other-coal-power-plant-operators-global-tax-2025-09-12/ “Vietnam to exempt Mitsubishi, Kepco, other coal power plant operators from global tax, document shows,”] Reuters, September 11, 2025</ref>

In October 2025, Aboitiz Power agreed to buy a 25% stake in Van Phong Power from Sumitomo for about US$220 million, subject to regulatory approval.<ref>[https://business.inquirer.net/555428/aboitiz-power-buying-25-stake-in-vietnam-coal-plant “Aboitiz Power buying 25% stake in Vietnam coal plant for $220M,”] Philippine Daily Inquirer, October 30, 2025</ref>

In January 2026, Vân Phong power station Unit 2 reportedly experienced a transformer malfunction.<ref>[https://www.evn.com.vn/d/vi-VN/news/Nha-may-Nhiet-dien-BOT-Van-Phong-1-duoc-cac-don-vi-truyen-tai-trong-EVN-ho-tro-khac-phuc-su-co-kip-thoi--60-12-506363 Nhà máy Nhiệt điện BOT Vân Phong 1 được các đơn vị truyền tải trong EVN hỗ trợ khắc phục sự cố kịp thời], Tập đoàn Điện lực Việt Nam (EVN), January 7, 2026</ref>

===Financing===
In August 2018, a report by Market Forces found that Vân Phong-1 may not be eligible for financing from the Japanese banks SMBC, MUFG, and Mizuho because of their policies that rule out financing supercritical coal plants.<ref>[https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-08-27/these-3-coal-plants-might-not-get-japan-funds-under-new-rules These 3 Coal Plants Might Not Get Japan Funds Under New Rules], Bloomberg, Aug. 27, 2018</ref> 

In April 2019, the Japanese Bank For International Cooperation (JBIC) agreed to loan up to approximately USD 1.199 million to Van Phong Power Company Limited (VAN PHONG) for Van Phong-1. The loan is co-financed with Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, MUFG Bank, Ltd., Mizuho Bank, Ltd., Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, Limited, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited and DBS Bank Ltd., and the Bank of China, with a total co-financing amount of approximately USD 1.998 million.<ref>[https://www.jbic.go.jp/en/information/press/press-2019/0419-012106.html Project Finance for Van Phong 1 Coal-Fired Power Generation Project in the Republic of Vietnam], JBIC, Apr. 19, 2019</ref> US$1,001 million in equity was provided by the Sumitomo Corporation. The Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation acted as financial adviser to the sponsor. Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI) provided political risk coverage for the deal.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/19252/van-phong-1-coal-fired-power-plant-132gw-ipp|title=Preview of Van Phong 1 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1.32GW) IPP {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-20}}</ref>

*'''Source of financing:''' Vân Phong-1: [[Japan Bank for International Cooperation]] (US$1.5-US$1.8 billion); <ref>[http://www.researchviews.com/energy/power/fossil-fuels/DealReport.aspx?sector=Fossil%20Fuels&DealID=209229 Sumitomo and Hanoinco Plan Project Financing for Van Phong I Thermal Power Plant in Vietnam], ResearchViews, Nov. 26, 2012.</ref><ref name=mfmar>[https://www.marketforces.org.au/research/vietnam/van-phong-1/ "Van Phong 1 (1320 MW),"] Market Forces, updated March 24, 2018</ref> Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG), Mizuho Financial Group (Mizuho), Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), DBS Bank, OCBC Bank, Bank of China (US$ 1.998 million);<ref>[https://www.marketforces.org.au/research/vietnam/van-phong-1/ Japanese Banks: Respect Your Committments], Market Forces, Apr. 19, 2019</ref> US$1,001 million in equity from Sumitomo Corporation<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://ijglobal.com/data/transaction/19252/van-phong-1-coal-fired-power-plant-132gw-ipp|title=Preview of Van Phong 1 Coal-Fired Power Plant (1.32GW) IPP {{!}} Transaction {{!}} IJGlobal|website=ijglobal.com|access-date=2020-11-20}}</ref>

===Sumitomo's Coal Policy===
In August 2019 a group of Japanese NGO's including JACSES, Kiko-Network, FOE Japan, Mekong Watch and 350 Japan released a statement calling on Sumitomo to withdraw from Vân Phong-1 because the project conflicts with Sumitomo's policies on coal plant construction.<ref name="foe">[http://www.foejapan.org/en/aid/pdf/190821_en.pdf Sumitomo Corporation Must Aim at Complete Coal Phase-Out to Combat Climate Change], FOE Japan, Aug. 21, 2019</ref> Sumitomo had stated a general policy of not developing new coal-fired plants in its "Integrated Report 2019," but also stated that it might support individual projects on a case-by-case basis.<ref name="foe">[http://www.foejapan.org/en/aid/pdf/190821_en.pdf Sumitomo Corporation Must Aim at Complete Coal Phase-Out to Combat Climate Change], FOE Japan, Aug. 21, 2019</ref>

==Vân Phong-2==

In October 2014, Korean company [[Keangnam Enterprises]] and Vietnamese company Hanoi Industrial Construction and Investment JSC signed an initial agreement with Khanh Hoa provincial government to build the additional two-unit, 1,320-MW coal-fired Vân Phong-2 power plant. The next step for the potential developers was to undertake a feasibility study. Construction was scheduled to begin in 2017, and completion was scheduled for 2020.<ref>[http://www.baokhanhhoa.com.vn/xa-hoi/201410/nha-may-nhiet-dien-van-phong-2-du-kien-khoi-cong-vao-nam-2017-2348071/ Nhà máy nhiệt điện Vân Phong 2: Dự kiến khởi công vào năm 2017], Khanh Hoa Online, 28 Oct. 2014.</ref>
